source: trans. for ScriptureBot from the Latin (ed. Morard, 1480/81 text)

1.1:
**“There came”** — For the fewness of spiritual teachers, to whom the authority of judging is given, there came a famine of the word of God, when the law too was corrupted by the traditions of the Jews.
**“And a certain man … went”** — Rabanus. Christ, that is, born in Bethlehem Juda, visited the sojourning of this world, with his wife, that is, the Church, and with two children, namely the two orders of the prophets and the apostles, who were freed from the slavery of sin by the blood of Christ.
**“A certain man … went”** — Rabanus. Some understand him as the decalogue, and his wife as the Synagogue, and the two sons as the royal and the priestly honour, which won themselves a union not only in the nation of the Jews but also of the proselytes, as was done in the time of David and Solomon and others.
**“to sojourn in the land of Moab”** — that is, in the country of the devil, who is the prince of this world
1.2:
**“He was named Elimelech”** — “My God is king”: this is Christ, to whom it is said: “Hearken to the voice of my prayer, O my King and my God.”
**“and his wife, Noemi”**
• beautiful
• “Thou art beautiful, O my love”, and so on
**“Mahalon”** — Who is “from the window”, or “from the beginning”. This is the choir of the prophets, through whom the first light of faith went forth into the world from the window, who were also the first preachers of the true light, that is, of Christ.
**“and the other Chelion”** — Chelion: consummation. These are the apostles, who brought the riddles of the prophets to the consummation of full understanding. These are rightly Ephrathites, and sprung from Bethlehem Juda, who, filled with the heavenly bread, gathered the fruit of preaching through the preaching of the gospel. For Ephrathite is interpreted “fruitful”, Bethlehem “house of bread”, Juda “confession”. Whence: “Give you them to eat.” Again: “Going, preach the gospel of the kingdom of God.” And elsewhere: “I have chosen you out of the world, that you should go, and should bring forth fruit.”
**“Ephrathites of Bethlehem Juda. And entering into the country of Moab”** — Judea, which made ill use of the law
1.3:
**“And Elimelech the husband of Noemi died: and … remained”** — in the exile of this world
**“she”** — the Church
**“with her sons”** — with the teachers
1.4:
**“And they took wives of the women of Moab”** — because the apostles joined to themselves the fellowship of two peoples, namely of the Jews and of the Gentiles
**“of which one was called Orpha”**
• her neck
• these are the faithful from among the Jews, who first received the strength of faith and the fortitude of working
**“Ruth”** — She is interpreted “seeing”, or “hastening”, or “failing”; in whom is signified the obedience and believing of the Gentiles, of whom it is said: “A people which I knew not hath served me”, and so on. And elsewhere: Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God. So the two peoples were called by the holy preachers to the fellowship of faith and of God’s elect, that out of divers flocks there might be one fold.
1.5:
**“And they both”** — the apostles and prophets
**“died, to wit, Mahalon and Chelion”** — in this sojourning, after the Lord’s ascension
**“died”** — After the completion of their holy labour, that is, they had passed from the exile of this world to the heavenly kingdom, that, the commandment of the decalogue being fulfilled, they might receive the penny of blessedness.
**“and the woman was left alone, having lost”** — the Church
**“both her sons and her husband”** — the prophets and apostles, whose temporal or bodily presence she lacked
1.6: **“And she arose to go from the land of Moab to her own country with both her daughters in law: for she had heard that the Lord had looked upon his people, and had given them food”** — of life
1.7:
**“she went forth … with both her daughters in law”** — The Church takes earnest pains to bring the peoples whom the apostles and prophets instructed in their time to the unity of the faith and the fellowship of the Christian religion; for she has learnt from the Scripture that the just man “is not forsaken”, “nor his seed seeking bread”, the bread “that came down from heaven”.
**“Wherefore … out of the place of her sojournment”** — out of the world
**“with both her daughters in law”** — with each people
**“and being now in the way”** — in Christ, or in his commandments
**“to return”** — firmly
1.8: **“Go ye home”** — The Church does not act without discernment, nor receive anyone without discernment; whence: Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God. These things can also fit the Synagogue, which draws back those coming to the faith of Christ; and above all this, that, overcome by the truth, she knows herself weak and worn out, saying: Return, my daughters.
1.11:
**“But she answered them: Return, my daughters: why come ye with me? have I”** — elsewhere: have I then
**“have I any more sons”** — Rabanus. The voice of the Synagogue confessing the truth and not keeping silent about the guilt that has come upon her, who, forsaken by her husband, that is, David, and deprived of her sons, that is, kings and princes, confesses that after the coming of Christ she is barren and too weak to conceive sons to God.
1.12: **“Return again, my daughters, and go your ways”** — elsewhere: my daughters, and go your ways
1.14: **“And they lifted up their voice”** — By these women, one of whom, grieving and mourning, departs from her mother in law, while the other clings to her with a steadfast mind, believers are signified: some of whom, having received the grace of baptism and the fellowship of faith, fall back into their former errors, whom Orpha signifies, who went back to her gods; but others, with settled purpose, keep the grace they have received, whom Ruth signifies.
1.16: **“for whithersoever thou shalt go, I will go”** — So the Church called from the Gentiles, leaving her country, that is, abandoning idolatry, fleshly life and desires, professes that her God is he in whom the saints believed, and that she will go where the flesh of Christ ascended, and suffer for his name in this world even unto death, and be with the people of the saints and prophets and patriarchs; whence: “Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.”
1.18: **“Then Noemi, seeing”** — Noemi, seeing, and so on. The Gentile people follows the preachers with steadfast mind into the holy land and into Bethlehem, the city of God, where it is prepared to receive the bridegroom born of the stock of Abraham, in whom all nations or tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
1.20: **“But she said to them: Call me not Noemi”** — Call me not, and so on. The Synagogue acknowledges her calamity, which she deservedly suffers after the coming of Christ, and shrinks from being called beautiful, because she sees the times of her prosperity ending.
1.22: **“So Noemi came with Ruth the Moabitess her daughter in law, from the land of her sojournment: and returned into Bethlehem, in the beginning of the barley harvest”** — In the beginning of the barley harvest, and so on. That is, when it turns the order of his incarnation to the mystery of Christ’s passion. For the barley harvest expresses the time of the Lord’s passion, which fell in the month of new corn, that is, in the first month. Rightly then they come to Bethlehem at that time, when the law preaches that Christ, whom it teaches was born in Bethlehem, was slain at the pasch, that is, in the month of new corn. Holy Church too labours with all her strength to steep those whom she calls to the faith in the merit of the incarnation, passion and resurrection. The barley harvest expresses the believing of the Jews, who, the sacrament of the passion being accomplished, came first to the faith at the apostles’ preaching; who elsewhere are read to have been fed by the Lord with five barley loaves.

2.1:
**“Now her husband Elimelech had a kinsman, a powerful man, and very rich, whose name was Booz”** — “The strength of God”; whence: “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Prince of Peace, the Father of the world to come.”
**“Now her husband … had”** — This man, the kinsman of Elimelech, is Christ, the lamb of the law and the lawgiver, because he was promised through the law and born of the patriarchs, and of the nation of the Jews according to the flesh. Whence: “God will raise up to you a prophet of your brethren; him you shall hear as myself.” He is the powerful one who vanquished the prince of the world and subdued the whole world to his rule; and very rich, because he is “possessor of heaven and earth”, and “in him are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge”. For he is “the power of God and the wisdom”.
2.2:
**“And Ruth the Moabitess said to her mother in law: If thou wilt, I will go into the field”** — the Church
**“and glean the ears of corn”** — The ears left behind signify the faithful who, the rest having been taken up to heaven, are left to us as an example
**“that escape the hands of the reapers”** — The harvest is the saints, who are gathered to be laid up in God’s barn. The reapers are the angels.
2.3: **“She went therefore and gleaned the ears of corn after the reapers. And it happened that the owner of that field was Booz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech”** — And it happened, and so on. Because holy Church belongs to Christ, whose bride and body she is; of whom it is said: “The Lord is my strength and my praise.” And elsewhere: “The Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.” He is the kinsman of Elimelech, who, born of Bethlehem and of the stock of David, has witness from the law and the prophets. He brought the words of salvation to his household; at his birth the angels sang: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will. When he came into Jerusalem, the crowd met him, crying out: “Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.”
2.5: **“And Booz said to the young man that was set over the reapers: Whose maid is this?”** — because Christ, as if not knowing, asks about the faith of the Gentiles of any of the teachers who is set over the lesser priests, when he stirs him up to preach
2.7:
**“And she desired leave to glean the ears of corn that remain, following the steps of the reapers: and she hath been in the field from morning”** — because from the beginning, that is, of faith, to the perfection of good work
**“till now, and hath not … home for one moment”** — of the old superstition
**“gone”** — And she desired leave, and so on. Because holy Church perseveres in the field of divine reading after the reapers and preachers, gathering the mysteries of the Scriptures, so as to store the testimonies and examples of the virtues in the bosom of her mind. Or that field is the discipline of heavenly study; the harvest, spiritual understanding; the reapers, the preachers; the ears left behind, the sentences of the Scriptures, which, being much hidden in mystery, remain as it were fuller, for the exercise of one who meditates. So the Gentile people ardently longs for the Church’s discipline, that it may be admitted to the meditation of the divine law and the fellowship of the saints, and be refreshed by the teachings or examples of the saints.
2.8: **“do not go to glean in any other field”** — As if to say: Do not depart from the state of faith, do not follow the errors of heretics or schismatics, but rather join thyself to holy souls, that thou mayest reap the holy Scriptures by meditating and fulfilling them in deed, and mayest drink the draught of divine wisdom from the books of the two Testaments, whence the young men, that is, the saints, drink.
2.10: **“She fell on her face”** — The Church of the Gentiles gives thanks to the Saviour, who has deigned to regard her. He answers her that it pleases him that, her husband, that is, the devil, being dead, she has left her idolatrous parents and the land of her birth, that is, fleshly desires, and has joined herself to the people of the saints, which was unknown to her before, when she followed the lust of the old man.
2.12:
**“The Lord render unto thee for thy work, and mayest thou receive a full reward of the Lord the God of Israel”** — that is, by faith; whence: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he hath sent.”
**“to whom thou art come, and under whose wings thou art fled”** — the two Testaments, with which God protects those who flee to him; whence: “In the shadow of thy wings will I hope.”
2.13: **“And she said: I have found grace in thy eyes, my lord, who hast comforted me and hast spoken to the heart of thy handmaid, who am not like to one of thy maids”** — I have found, and so on. Note the humility of the Church of the Gentiles, which knows herself unequal to so great a grace, and does not dare to make herself equal to the first Church. Whence she says: “For the whelps also eat of the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters.” And elsewhere: “Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed”, and so on.
2.14:
**“At mealtime”** — The hour of eating was when it was said to the apostles: “Going, teach ye all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.” For it had been said by the Lord: “Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles.”
**“come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar”** — Dip thy morsel, and so on. In the law, that is, which, so long as it was meditated upon, persevering in the former people, corrupted by the conditions or traditions of the Pharisees, lost its native savour. In this the Church dips her morsel, that is, she learns that the mysteries of Christ’s incarnation are in the Old Testament; and so she believes the more firmly, because she knows it was prefigured long before.
**“So she sat at the side of the reapers”** — because the Gentile Church joins herself to the holy preachers through faith
**“and she heaped to herself frumenty, and ate and was filled”** — because the knowledge of the divine law refreshed her devout mind
**“and took the leavings”** — because she chewed over each word that she heard with fine discernment
2.15: **“And she arose from thence, to glean the ears of corn as before”** — because she kept the words she had heard in her heart, and laboured earnestly in meditating, that she might take in greater things
2.16:
**“some of your handfuls”** — Note the humility of the householder, who not only lets the ears of the testimonies that are left be gathered, but also bestows handfuls of knowledge with unasked largess.
**“And let fall some of your handfuls of purpose, and leave them, that she may gather them without shame, and let no man rebuke her when she gathereth them”** — Some of your handfuls, and so on. Because he does not despise the weakness of the Gentile people, nor reproach it with its former errors, but by the shrewdness of his care leads it on to edification.
2.17:
**“She gleaned therefore in the field till evening: and beating out with a rod and threshing what she had gleaned”** — because holy Church with the rod of discernment draws the spiritual sense out of the letter of the law
**“about the measure of an ephi”** — When in reading she learns the catholic faith through the confession of the holy Trinity. In the measure of an ephi, which contains three bushels, is signified the one substance of the godhead and the property of the three persons.
2.18:
**“Which she took up and returned”** — Because she shows her faith to mother Church. Or the Church shows the Synagogue the grace she has received by the gift of her bridegroom, to stir her up to come to her.
**“gave her of the remains”** — “My heart hath uttered a good word”: that is, the food of preaching, from the fulness of the heart.
2.19: **“And her mother in law said to her: Where hast thou gleaned today, and where hast thou wrought? blessed be he that hath had pity on thee”** — Blessed, and so on. The Synagogue, the Church of the Gentiles preaching, acknowledges the goodness and power of the Lord and the strength of her protector, and at length, the truth compelling her, blesses the name of the Lord, because he has kept for the dead the kindness which he showed to the living.
2.20:
**“And Noemi answered her: Blessed be he of the Lord: because the same kindness”** — of bounty
**“which he shewed to the living”** — to the Jews, when they enjoyed his benefits
**“he hath kept also to the dead”** — to the Gentiles, who were buried in sins
**“And again she said: … our kinsman”** — to the Synagogue according to the flesh, to the Church by union of the spirit
**“The man is”** — Christ
**“The man is our kinsman”** — Mother Church recognizes the kinsman by the free benefits bestowed on the people of the Gentiles, and, hearing the name, remembers the ancient benefits; whence: “I remembered the days of old, I meditated on all thy works.”
2.21: **“And Ruth said, He also charged me, that I should keep close to his reapers, till all the corn should be reaped”** — He charged me, that I should keep close, and so on. Because Christ charges all who come to him to join themselves rather to his faithful for the harvest of the spiritual crop than to strangers; to which counsel the mother in law consents, saying: It is better, my daughter; as good and useful the Synagogue cannot deny it.
2.22:
**“And her mother in law said to her: It is better for thee, my daughter, … with his maids”** — with holy souls
**“to go out to reap …, lest in another man’s field some one”** — of the heretics
**“may resist thee”** — the teaching of the schismatics, as quarrels and contentions
2.23:
**“So she kept close to the maids of Booz: and continued to glean with them, till … the wheat”** — the grace, though not that which is given to rational creatures for refreshment, in which the flesh and blood of Christ is offered, of which it is said: “Unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, itself remaineth alone.”
**“all the barley”** — the letter of the law, which was given to the Jews as to beasts for fodder
**“till all the barley”** — That is, she cleaves to the teachers in the meditation of the Scriptures until she has stored the knowledge of the Old and New Testaments in the cell of her heart, whence she might have food enough for the soul.

3.1: **“After she was returned to her mother in law, Noemi said to her: My daughter, I will seek rest for thee, and will provide that it may be well with thee”** — The first Church conferred with the Gentile Church on how she might come to union with Christ.
3.2: **“he winnoweth barley in the threshingfloor”** — The Synagogue of the Jews, where the law is stored up. Christ winnows it when, preaching the Gospel on the threshingfloor, he threshes out the counsels and wills of each towards himself. Whence: “But Jesus did not trust himself unto them, for that he knew all men, and because he needed not that any should give testimony of man.”
3.3:
**“Wash thyself therefore”** — with the water of baptism, or with the tears of penance
**“and anoint thee”** — with chrism, or the anointing of the Holy Spirit
**“and put on thy best garments”** — with the adornment of the virtues
**“and go down to the barnfloor: but let not the man see thee, till he shall have done eating and drinking”** — Here, that is, Christ dwells and calls the human race back to himself, that is, by dying for you, where he won all things; whence: “If I be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all things to myself.”
**“let not the man see thee, till”** — Because the faith of the Gentiles did not appear to the Church before Christ had fulfilled the mystery of his incarnation, when, living bodily among men, he took food and drink, and at last, supping with his disciples, imparted to them the sacraments of his body and blood. But when the mystery of Christ’s dispensation was fulfilled, the Church of the Gentiles came confidently to the faith.
3.4:
**“thou shalt … lift up the clothes”** — As if to say: Know Christ, who suffered for thee, and come with a devout mind; uncover the covering of the letter of the Old Testament, in which the sacrament of Christ’s incarnation is held; and when thou hast learnt the salvation promised thee there, flee humbly to his help, that thou mayest remain there for all time.
**“and he will tell thee what thou must do”** — because thou must learn the order of thy salvation from him. But if thou refer Noemi’s words to the Synagogue, thou wilt find in the law and the prophet that after the passion the Church of the Gentiles is to come to the faith.
3.5: **“She answered: Whatsoever thou shalt command, I will do”** — the Church’s obedience deserves the fulfilment of her desire; whence: “O woman, great is thy faith: be it done to thee as thou wilt.”
3.7:
**“And when Booz had eaten”** — Christ ate and drank when at the supper he handed on the sacraments of his body and blood to the apostles; whence, because the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he himself also hath partaken of the same.
**“he went to sleep by the heap of sheaves”** — heap
**“the heap”** — The testimonies of the Scriptures; whence: “The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him.” Or beside the troops of faithful souls whom by his death he called back from hell. To this bed the Church hastened, and, uncovering the cloak, and so on.
**“and she came softly and uncovering his feet, laid herself down”** — because, the world being wrapped in darkness, she showed the Church’s swift faith for us to imitate
3.8:
**“And behold, when it was now midnight the man was afraid, and troubled: and he saw a woman”** — the Church
**“lying at his feet”** — humbly worshipping the sacrament of the incarnation
3.9:
**“And he said”** — Christ
**“Who art thou?”** — he asks for the Church’s confession
**“And she answered: I am Ruth thy handmaid: spread thy coverlet over thy servant, for thou art a near kinsman”** — The Church desires above all things the grace of faith and of Christ’s protection.
**“spread thy coverlet”** — She who asked that the cloak be spread over her deserved to receive a blessing. For he who fully receives the grace of faith will possess blessing and virtue alike.
3.10:
**“And he said: Blessed art thou of the Lord, my daughter, and thy latter kindness has surpassed the former”** — by which, taking counsel for thyself, thou didst cast away idolatry
**“because thou hast not followed”** — because after thou camest to Christ thou hast steadfastly persevered
**“young men either poor or rich”** — heretics or schismatics, who have no ripeness of counsel, because they are always unstable and uncertain
3.11: **“Fear not therefore, but whatsoever thou shalt say to me I will do to thee”** — “Ask, and you shall receive”; “Seek, and you shall find.” Whatever faith rightly asks, the kindness of Christ grants.
3.12:
**“Neither do I deny myself to be near of kin, but there is another nearer than I”**
• because the faithful are firmly persuaded that the Church is full of virtues; of whom it is said: “Who shall find a valiant woman?”
• But there is another than I, and so on. John the Baptist, who was thought to be the Christ, but did not usurp the name of bridegroom, but kept it for Christ, saying: “He that hath the bride is the bridegroom”, and so on. He is nearer because he was born first in the world. Or this kinsman is the decalogue of the law, which seemed nearer to the Synagogue than the Gospel, because it was given especially to that people and is earlier in time.
3.14:
**“So she slept at his feet till the night was going off”** — because, resting in the hope of the incarnation, she waited patiently until the darkness of unbelief should withdraw
**“And she arose before”** — Because before the Jews, steeped in the teaching of the law, knew the rights of their nature, the Church of the Gentiles, shaking off the sleep of her sloth, rose again at the dawn of the newborn faith and hastened to the grace of Christ.
**“Beware lest any man know that thou camest hither”** — do not seek praise for thy way of life. When thou dost alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth.
3.15:
**“And again he said: Spread thy mantle”** — Enlarge thy faith
**“wherewith thou art covered”** — practise in deed what thou receivest in heart
**“and hold it with both hands. And when she spread it and held it, he measured six measures of barley”** — He measured six measures, and so on. Because the measure of perfect working is granted according to the capacity of understanding, that she may be enriched within and without by the divine gift. The number six can also signify this, that in the sixth age the Lord granted the Church of the Gentiles the barley of the law spiritually understood.
**“and laid it upon her”** — namely, seasoned with Christ’s gifts and adorned with the fruits of the virtues
3.16: **“And came to her mother in law; who said to her: What hast thou done, daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her”** — the great works of God, that is, so as to stir the first Church to praise, or the Synagogue to conversion
3.17:
**“And she said: Behold he hath given me six measures of barley: for he said: I will not have thee return empty”** — The Church promised confidently, because the truth will not cease to fulfil the promises, which says: “He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved.”
**“to thy mother in law”** — the first Church, or the Synagogue

4.1:
**“Then Booz went up to the gate, and sat there”** — Because Christ brings to fulfilment the prophecy written of his incarnation
**“went up to the gate”** — Because he took flesh in the virgin’s womb, in which he would appear. Of this gate it is said: “This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass through it: because the Lord the God of Israel hath entered in by it.”
**“Turn aside for a little while”** — Because Christ saw the law set up bodily for the Jews, and bade it turn aside to him, because he bent it to bear witness to the mystery of his dispensation. Otherwise: he saw the kinsman going by, when he saw the coming of his forerunner hastening on after the manner of human life, and mercifully turned him to the office of forerunner.
**“and sit down here, calling him by his name”** — that is, through Gabriel, saying: his name shall be called John
4.2:
**“And Booz taking ten men”** — for a witness of his second coming
**“of the ancients of the city”** — the fathers of the Old Testament, that is, those who kept the decalogue, and knew that Christ’s incarnation was foreshadowed there
4.3: **“he spoke to the kinsman”** — Fittingly he offered the part of Noemi’s field to the lawyer to buy, when he showed the masters of the Synagogue the part of the people that remained to be saved, grace having now appeared, that they might acknowledge their weakness, and commit what they themselves could not do to the true physician to be done; whence it is said to the lepers: Go, show yourselves to the priests; and as they went, they were made clean.
4.5: **“to raise up”** — He signifies no other possession of the people than the joining of the Church in marriage to Christ, who raised up the ancient name of sons of God, which the saints had at the beginning. Whence: “The sons of God seeing”, and so on; and Luke says: “Adam, who was of God”; which name he raised up in the Church of the Gentiles by the grace of God. Whence: “He gave them power to be made the sons of God”, and so on. This name the decalogue of the law could not raise up among the nations. But if thou refer this to John the Baptist, thou wilt find him yielding his right of kinship and saying: “I baptize with water; but there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to loose.” And elsewhere: “I am not Christ, but … I am sent before him. He that hath the bride is the bridegroom.” The law too yields to the Gospel. For the law entered in, that sin might abound, grace abounding more. There is indeed a setting aside of the former commandment, because of its weakness; but a bringing in of a better hope, by which we draw nigh to God, through Jesus Christ.
4.8: **“So Booz said to his kinsman: Put off thy shoe. And immediately he took it off from his foot”** — Put off his shoe, and so on. The shoe is the veil of the mysteries. The law took off the shoe from its foot and gave it to Christ, because it could not make the sacraments plain through the masters of the people, but kept this to be done by Christ. So John claimed the shoe not for himself but for Christ, because he understood that the bride belonged to Christ alone; whence he says: “I am not worthy to loose the latchet of his shoe.”
4.9: **“You are witnesses”** — So Christ has witnesses enough from both Testaments, that the people of the Gentiles, which the decalogue, now ended, could not make fruitful spiritually, he himself made fruitful with the seed of the word, possessing all that the earlier and later saints had.
4.11:
**“Then all the people that were in the gate, and the ancients answered”** — And the ancients, and so on. Isidore. The blessing of the ten ancients shows that all nations are to be blessed in the name of Jesus. For iota, which is the first letter in the name of Jesus, signifies ten among the Greeks.
**“The Lord make this woman”** — They pray for prosperity for the Church of the Gentiles, that she may receive the grace of fruitfulness that the first parents of the Israelites had.
**“Rachel”** — The beauty of inward contemplation, having inward understanding of the truth. Whence Rachel, “well favoured and of a beautiful countenance”, whom every devoutly zealous man loves and for whom he serves Laban, who is interpreted “whitening”, which he compares to the grace of God, who says: “If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow.”
**“Lia”** — The action of this life in which we live is laborious, from faith, and uncertain as to the outcome by which it will come to the profit of those whom we wish to help. This is Lia, the first wife of Jacob, who is recorded to have had weak eyes.
4.12: **“And that the house may be, as the house of Phares”** — Phares, and so on. Because the Gentile people held the grace, and in the birth went before the brother who had first put out his hand. For Israel first put out its hand in the work of the law, and drew it back defiled with the blood of the prophets and of Christ himself. But afterwards the people of the Gentiles broke forth, that “the first should be last, and the last first”. Thamar too is interpreted “changing” or “bitterness”. For the Church of the Gentiles, both in name and in bearing, which was foul and bitter in idolatry, becomes sweet and beautiful in penance.
4.13:
**“Booz therefore took Ruth, and married her”** — because the Church joined to Christ bears spiritual offspring; whence: “The barren hath borne many: and she that had many children is weakened.”
**“to conceive and to bear”** — The Church is always made fruitful by the gift of the Holy Spirit, and as some depart to everlasting light others will succeed, so that the Christian name may remain for ever, and the most holy mother may have comfort from new offspring in her old age. As the patriarchs and prophets departed, too, the evangelists and apostles succeeded them. Whence: “Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee.”
4.14: **“And the women said to Noemi”** — the Synagogue
4.15:
**“For he is born of thy daughter in law”** — The daughter in law of the Synagogue is the Gentile Church, which married Christ, born of the Synagogue. Him, namely, she could not bring forth through the law; received through the mystery of prophecy, she carried him hidden, figured under a veil, and performed the office of a nurse, because she lacked the privilege of a mother.
**“is much better to thee”** — That is, than the multitude of those who were nourished in the Old Testament by the teaching of the law, who, namely, did not believe the word of the Lord, “and they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to devils”, and at last killed Christ and persecuted the apostles.
4.16: **“and she carried it, and was a nurse unto it”** — The spiritual lineage of the generation is shown. For Obed is interpreted “serving”; Isai, “sacrifice in the sun”, or “incense”; David, “strong of hand”, or “desirable”. For he who serves God earnestly offers him a pleasing sacrifice and incense of sweetest odour through works of virtue and zeal in prayer; and so, strengthened by faith and devotion, he is desirable and pleases God.
4.17: **“And the women her neighbours”** — The powers of heaven, which rejoice in the fruitfulness of the Church, and call his name Obed, that is, serving, whom they desire to serve the King on high with them.
4.22: **“These are the generations”** — There are ten generations from Juda’s son to David. From which thou knowest that the purpose of the whole divine law tends to Christ, who was born of the seed of David, to proclaim his coming and to show the perfection of the law in him: “For the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth.” So before the law Jacob says of Christ’s incarnation: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and so on. And to David, because Christ is of the seed of Juda, it was said: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne. It is plain, then, that the oracle of all the prophets and patriarchs belongs to the dispensation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

1.1:
**“In the days of Assuerus, who reigned from India to Ethiopia over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces”**
• which were small
• In the days of Assuerus. Rabanus. The book of Esther, which the Hebrews number among the Hagiographa, contains the sacraments of Christ and the Church. For Esther, in figure of the Church, frees the people from danger, and, Aman (which is interpreted “iniquity”) being slain, hands down to posterity the portions of the feast and a solemn day.
• We do not doubt that the history of Esther was in the time of Assuerus, but who Assuerus was we do not know. Josephus, however, records that he was Cyrus, the son of Xerxes, who ruled the empire of Persia after his father Darius. He said that this Cyrus is called Artaxerxes among the Greeks, who, surnamed Longhand, reigned forty years; but Esther does not seem to have lived at that time, for perhaps Esdras would not have passed her over, who wove the history of the things done when the captives returned from Babylon to Jerusalem. But Eusebius in his Chronicles judges that this is the Artaxerxes who is surnamed Memnon, the son of Darius and Parysatis. He is called Assuerus by the Hebrews, Artaxerxes by the Seventy interpreters, and reigned forty years after Darius, surnamed Nothus.
1.2: **“the city Susan”** — Susa is the chief city in Persia, which the historians say Memnon’s brother founded, and that it took its name from the river Susis. There is the royal house of Cyrus, of white and varied stone, with golden pillars and ceilings set off with gems, containing an image of the heavens marked with twinkling stars, and many incredible things. There Assuerus held a very great feast, with riches and an abundance of delights. For the power of the sacred word sometimes so tells things past as to express things to come; so approves the doer as to gainsay him in his ministry; so condemns deeds done as to urge that they be done mystically.
1.3:
**“Now in the third year of his reign he made”** — Assuerus, namely, who shows Christ by name and dignity; for he is interpreted “my court” or “door”. And Christ says: “I am the door of the sheep”, etc.
**“Now in the third year”** — In the time, namely, of this world he laid open the sacrament of his incarnation, and served most abundantly the spiritual feasts of preaching and of his body and blood. The first time is before the law, the second under the law, the third under grace.
**“a great feast”**
• A great feast. “The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king, who made a marriage for his son.” And elsewhere: “A certain man made a great supper, and invited many.”
• The history of this feast shows the pomp of riches and the luxury of the king, but allegorically it signifies the spiritual delights of Christ, which he deals out to each. For Christ is that most rich king, who, moved by the prayers of his wife, that is, the Church, frees his own, that is, his confessors, from the hand of the enemies, and condemns those justly. For it is not necessary that, if the good things of some signify Christ, their evil things too should fit Christ himself. For Moses signified Christ in many things, but not in this, that he doubted at the waters of contradiction; nor Aaron in the making of the calf, nor Solomon in the filth of lust. So Assuerus in this judgement, as in the liberal feast, signifies Christ; as Isaias signifies Christ in Cyrus, king of the Persians, of whom he afterwards adds: “I girded thee, and thou hast not known me”, etc. For if wicked kings in their misdeeds signify the devil, why should not just kings in their good deeds show forth Christ? Nabuchodonosor commanded the peoples, when they heard the sound of the symphony and the music, to fall down and adore the statue; and the devil, by worldly sweetness, bends the human race from uprightness of mind to follow covetousness, which is the service of idols.
**“for all the princes, and for his servants, for the most mighty”**
• the apostles. Whence: “Children, have you any meat?” And elsewhere: “Because the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner hath been partaker of the same”
• “whom neither death, nor life … shall separate from the love of Christ”
**“of the Persians, and the nobles of the Medes, and the governors of the provinces”** — the prelates of the churches
**“in his sight”** — before him, in his good pleasure
1.4:
**“That he might shew the riches of the glory of his kingdom”** — of knowledge and wisdom, which lead to the kingdom of blessedness
**“and the greatness, and boasting”** — the display
**“of his power, for a long time, to wit, for a hundred”** — for eternal life, because a hundred is a perfect number and passes from the left hand to the right
1.5:
**“the days of the feast”** — Of the great, or of the first faithful, who were first refreshed, according to that: “I was not sent but to the sheep that are lost of the house of Israel.”
**“And when the days of the feast were expired”** — In the sacrament of the Lord’s resurrection, and of the New Testament, and of true circumcision; and there are eight beatitudes, to which this feast leads; which is held only by days, but the wicked will feast in the nights.
**“he invited”** — through the apostles; whence: “Behold we turn to the Gentiles”
**“all the people”** — the Gentiles too
**“that were found in Susan”** — which is a city of the Gentiles, and by synecdoche the nation is signified
**“from the greatest to the least: and commanded … seven days”** — the whole time of this life, which is passed in seven days
**“a feast to be made … in the court”** — in the present Church, in which by faith and works we prepare ourselves to enter paradise, in which the elect are filled with the dishes of the Word of God
**“of the garden”** — the garden of eternal delight, where fruitful trees are planted, that is, the saints, glorious in merits
**“and of the wood, which was planted by the … of the king”** — for by the gift of Christ our king the saints there enjoy an everlasting kingdom
**“care and the hand”** — by works
1.6:
**“And there were hung up on every side … hangings”** — a special adornment
**“sky coloured”** — of heavenly conversation
**“and green”** — green: the colour carbasinus is likened to gold
**“and violet … fastened with cords of silk”** — of heavenly contemplation
**“And there were hung up”** — Fine linen signifies the mortification of the flesh; purple, the blood of martyrdom; the marble pillars, the firmness of the teachers. It is well said, then, that hangings of divers colours were hung on marble pillars by cords of linen and purple through rings of ivory; because the beauty of the Church ought to shine forth in the teachers in the meditation of wisdom and in the ascent of the virtues, through mortification of the flesh and chastity, with the dignity of martyrdom, and by their word and example come to the knowledge of others; that, taught and strengthened by them, they may deserve to enter the hall of paradise.
**“and … with … pillars”** — That is, the teachers, of whom it is said: “I have established the pillars thereof.” And elsewhere: “The pillars thereof he made of silver, the seat of gold.”
**“The beds”**
• whence in the Canticle: “Our bed is flourishing”
• that is, the rest of contemplation, in which the saints rest
**“also were of gold”** — for wisdom
**“and silver”** — for eloquence
**“upon a floor”**
• the humility of the prelates, by which they prepare a bed for the lesser
• The emerald (smaragdus), called so from its great greenness, a small kind of marble, very white. For by the greenness of faith and the whiteness of chastity the foundation of humility is built. For “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven”, and “he that humbleth himself shall be exalted”, and elsewhere: “Learn of me”, etc.
**“paved with porphyry”** — by the greenness of faith
**“and white marble”** — by the whiteness of chastity
**“placed in order … which … of wonderful variety”**
• “The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing”
• of the virtues
**“was embellished with painting”** — God made the painting, not man
1.7:
**“And … drank”** — the spiritual guests
**“they that were invited … in golden cups”** — with the words of the gospel, seasoned with spiritual wisdom
**“in divers vessels one after another”** — of the law and the apostles and the prophets
**“the meats were brought”** — that is, the spiritual delights with which souls are fattened
**“Wine also”** — of the Word of God, of heavenly grace
**“Wine”** — According to that: “The charity of God is poured forth in our hearts”, etc. “To one is given the word of knowledge, to another of wisdom, to another faith, to another the grace of healing.” To receive a gift: God wills sons, not slaves; he wills will, not necessity; according to that: “He that can take, let him take it.” Again: “If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments”, and “If thou wilt be perfect, go sell all.”
**“as … of a king’s magnificence”**
• not by our smallness
• “dividing to every one according as he will”
**“in abundance and of the best was presented, as was worthy”** — he gives abundantly and upbraideth not
1.8:
**“Neither was there any one to compel them to drink that were not willing, but as the king had appointed, who set over every table”** — of the Scriptures
**“one”** — the teachers
**“of his nobles”** — the elders of the Church, who give “the measure of wheat in due season”
**“every man”** — According to the quickness, capacity and profit of each. For preaching is to be so tempered that it may be useful in all, harm none, and pass among the vices of all as a two-edged sword; so cutting away pride as not to increase timidity; so laying the care of work on the idle and sluggish as not to increase importunate activity in the restless and curious; and so of the rest.
1.9:
**“Also Vasthi the queen”** — the Jewish people, which seemed to reign, since in the worship of one God it stood above the other nations
**“made a feast”** — the refreshment of the law
**“for the women”** — of holy souls
**“in the palace”** — Jerusalem, where the temple was and the holy of holies. Or in the meditation of holy Scripture, in which the Godhead gives the knowledge of its power.
1.10:
**“Now on the seventh day, when the king was merry”** — to us, according to opinion
**“and after very much drinking”** — the plenteous grace of the Holy Ghost, which the apostles were given to drink
**“was well warmed”** — in the apostles
**“with wine”** — with the new wine of the Holy Ghost, of which it is said: “But thou hast kept the good wine until now”
**“he commanded Mauman, and Bazatha, and Harbona, and Bagatha, and Abgatha, and Zethar, and Charcas, the seven eunuchs”** — the preachers, filled with the sevenfold spirit, “who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven”
**“that served in his presence”** — the word of God
1.11:
**“To bring in queen”** — the Jewish people
**“Vasthi before the king”** — to the spiritual feast
**“with the crown set upon her head”** — by the honour of religion
**“to shew”** — “When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son”, etc. For then the Son of God, made flesh, laid open with more abundant grace the mysteries of the law, with which he had fed the faithful before.
**“to all the people”** — nations
**“and the princes”** — the nobler kings
**“her beauty … for she was exceeding beautiful”** — the privilege of the fathers, the knowledge of the law and the prophets
1.12:
**“But she refused”** — Despising not only the messengers but also the king’s command. Whence in the gospel the elder son, asked by the father, would not go in to the feast; and those who were called to the supper and, taken up with other things, would not come, were cast out by the indignation of the master of the house, and others put in their place.
**“and would not come at the king’s commandment, which he had signified to her by the eunuchs. Whereupon the king, being angry, and inflamed with a very great fury”** — our Saviour, of whom it is said: “The king shall greatly desire thy beauty”
1.13:
**“Asked the wise men”** — the teachers, excelling in the sevenfold spirit
**“who according to the custom of the kings, were always near his person”** — by right faith and working
**“and all he did was by their counsel, who knew the laws, and judgments of their forefathers”** — of the prophets
1.14:
**“Now the chief and nearest him were, Charsena, and Sethar, and Admatha, and Tharsis, and Mares, and Marsana, and Mamuchan, seven princes of the Persians”** — the preachers of the Gentiles
**“and of the Medes, who saw the face”** — the will
**“of the king, and were used to sit first after him”** — in the kingdom of the Church, or of heaven
1.16:
**“And … answered”** — This one, counted last in the order of the seven wise men, gives the sentence, and signifies Paul the apostle, who says: “I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle”; and, the Jews gainsaying and filled with envy, says: “Because you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles.”
**“in the hearing of the king and the princes: Queen Vasthi hath not only injured the king”** — as if it were a public matter
**“but also all the people”** — those under them
**“and princes”** — the preachers
**“that are in all the provinces”** — the churches
1.19:
**“If it please thee, let an edict go out from thy presence, and let it be written according to the law of the Persians and of the Medes, which must not be altered, that Vasthi come in no more”** — the Synagogue, which despised
**“to the king”**
• as a bride in the bedchamber
• where she reigned with the king
**“but another … be made queen in her place”** — the Church from the Gentiles
**“that is better than her”** — in faith and devotion; of which it is said: “The queen stood on thy right hand”
1.20:
**“And let this be published through all … (which is very wide,)”** — “Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth”
**“the provinces of thy empire”** — of the churches
**“and let all wives”** — the peoples under them
**“as well of the greater”** — of the apostles
**“as of the lesser”** — of their successors
**“give … to their husbands”** — to the prelates
**“honour”** — of obedience, namely
1.21:
**“His counsel pleased the king, and the princes”** — the fellow apostles
**“and the king did according to the counsel of Mamuchan”** — of Paul
1.22:
**“And he sent”** — through the preachers
**“letters”** — admonitions, rebukes
**“to all the provinces of his kingdom, as every nation could hear and read, in divers languages and characters”** — “The apostles spoke with divers tongues the wonderful works of God”

2.1:
**“After this”** — After this. Judea being cast off, divers men from divers parts of the world are brought to share the royal dignity through the preachers who minister the word of God; and they are handed over, that is, committed, to the hand of Egeus, who is interpreted “festive” and is the keeper of the king’s women; that is, to the shepherds to whom the keeping of faithful souls is given, that by word and example they may minister to them whatever they see needful for the worship of godliness. And whoever pleases the most high King by right faith and a pure conscience will go in to him, Vasthi being cast off.
**“when the wrath of king Assuerus was appeased, he remembered Vasthi, and what she had done”** — despising the king
**“and what she had suffered”** — the casting off
2.2:
**“And the king’s servants and his officers said”** — comforting the king
**“Let young women be sought for the king”** — new souls
**“virgins”** — from the corruption of the devil
2.3:
**“And let some persons be sent”** — the apostles, of whom it is said: “Behold I send you”
**“to look for”** — carefully
**“through all the provinces … beautiful maidens and virgins”** — in virtues and works
**“and let them bring them”** — by word and example
**“to the city”** — “A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid”
**“of Susan”** — in which Assuerus reigned
**“and put them into the house of the women under the hand of Egeus the eunuch, who is the overseer and keeper of the king’s women”** — of the brides of the great king
**“and let them receive”** — from God
**“women’s ornaments”** — the food and the adornment of souls
2.4:
**“And whosoever among them all shall please the king’s eyes”** — because “many are called, but few chosen”
**“let her be queen instead of Vasthi”** — one, not many: “the multitude of believers had but one heart”
2.6:
**“Who had been carried away”** — made a persecutor of the Church
**“from Jerusalem”** — the spiritual
**“at the time that … Jechonias king of Juda”** — those prepared for spiritual captivity. For Jechonias is interpreted “the preparation of the Lord”
**“Nabuchodonosor”** — the devil
**“king of Babylon”** — of confusion
2.7:
**“And he had brought up”**
• the master
• And he had brought up. Esther is called “hidden”, Edissa “having obtained mercy”. This is the Church of the Gentiles, which, nourishing in the hidden place of the heart the chastity of faith and mercy, found grace before the eyes of the Lord, the Synagogue being cast off, which in Osee was called “Without mercy”. Her the spiritual Mardochai nourishes and adopts as his daughter, who is the teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth, and is of the stock of Jemini, that is, of the stock of Benjamin.
**“daughter”** — of the Church
**“his brother’s”** — of Christ, who says: “I will declare thy name to my brethren”
**“Edissa, who by another name was called Esther”** — hidden: “Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth”
**“now she had lost both her parents”** — error and Gentile superstition
**“and was exceeding fair and beautiful”** — “Thou art beautiful and comely, O daughter of Jerusalem”
**“And her father and mother being dead, Mardochai adopted her for his daughter”** — by the word of the gospel he begot her to eternal salvation; whence: “My little children, of whom I am in labour again”
2.8:
**“And when the king’s ordinance was noised abroad, and according to his commandment many beautiful virgins were brought to Susan, and were delivered to Egeus”** — to chaste parents
**“Esther also”** — Her the spiritual Nabuchodonosor, the king of confusion, carried away from the natural law and the worship of one God into the confusion of idolatry; but the divine kindness called her back to the way of truth through the preachers.
2.9:
**“And she pleased him, and found favour in his sight. And he commanded the eunuch to hasten the women’s ornaments”** — sound doctrine, the knowledge of the Scriptures, and an eternal and honourable life
**“and seven … maidens”** — That is, faithful souls regenerated and dedicated by the grace of the Holy Ghost, who follow her footsteps in faith, doctrine and good working; of whom it is said: “The young maidens have loved thee exceedingly.”
**“of the king’s house, and … both her”** — the bride
**“and her waiting maids”** — the young maidens
**“to adorn”** — with the gifts of the virtues
**“and deck out”** — by word and example
2.10:
**“she”** — the Church of the Gentiles
**“would not tell him”** — She would not. Because, cleansed through baptism of the stain of sins and the filth of idolatry, she would no longer bear the reproach of her former iniquity.
**“her people nor her country. For Mardochai had charged her to say nothing at all of that”** — the teachers, who say: “Forget thy people”, etc.
2.11:
**“And he walked”** — carefully searching out the faith and works of the people committed to him
**“every day”** — constantly; whence the Apostle: “the solicitude for all the churches”, and: “Who is weak, and I am not weak?”
**“before the court”** — before the rule of right faith
**“of the house”** — of the heavenly Jerusalem
**“in which the chosen virgins were kept”** — souls
2.12:
**“Now when every virgin’s turn came to go in”** — as brides
**“to the king”** — the heavenly
**“after all had been done for setting them off to advantage, it was the twelfth month: so that for six months they were anointed with oil of myrrh”** — in the name of faith and the fatness of love
**“and for other six months they used certain perfumes”** — of good works
**“and sweet spices”** — of the virtues
2.13:
**“And when they were going in”** — into baptism
**“to the king”** — Going in. Whatever soul strives to hasten to the bridechamber of Christ receives a worthy adornment from its teachers; and the more devoutly it prepares itself for the knowledge of the faith and the exercise of works, the more fully it is instructed by the teachers; so that from the number of the candidates it may come to the whole faith and confession of the holy Trinity, to the receiving of baptism and the anointing of chrism, that it may be truly joined to the heavenly bridegroom.
**“whatsoever they asked to adorn themselves they received”** — from the teachers first
**“and being decked out, as it pleased them, they passed from the chamber”** — of the faith of the Trinity
2.14:
**“And she that went in at evening, came out in the morning”** — because after the setting of the vices the brightness of the virtues rises
**“and from thence”** — He who has separated himself from the Church by the filth of vices is rightly thrust into the second house, where the king’s concubines dwell; because the fall of sound faith deserves a lowering of honour, and he has no more power to return to the king unless, visited by grace from above, he is restored to the former state of dignity.
2.15:
**“as the time came orderly about”** — That is, the five ages of the world being past, through which the line of the fathers had gone forward, the sixth age was at hand, with the coming of the Redeemer, in which the multitude of the Gentiles was to be called through the gospel.
**“the day was at hand”** — the sixth age: “When the fulness of the time was come”
**“when Esther”** — the Church of the Gentiles
**“the daughter of Abihail the brother of Mardochai”** — of the teachers, and above all of Paul
**“whom he had adopted for his daughter”** — as above
**“was to go in to the king”** — through baptism
**“But she sought not women’s ornaments, but whatsoever Egeus the eunuch the keeper of the virgins had a mind, he gave her to adorn her”** — because she trusted the teachers more than herself; the physician knows better than the sick what is useful
**“For she was exceeding fair”** — “surrounded with variety” of virtues
2.16:
**“So she was brought to the chamber of king Assuerus the tenth month, which is called Tebeth”** — Tebeth among the Hebrews, Audynaeus among the Greeks, is January among the Latins; in which the Lord, made flesh, was circumcised on the eighth day, adored by the Magi and honoured with mystic gifts; in which also he is declared to have been baptized by John.
**“in the seventh year of his reign”** — in the year of kindness, filled with the sevenfold grace of the Holy Ghost
2.17:
**“And … loved her”** — the Church
**“the king”** — Christ
**“more than all the women”** — nations
**“and she had favour”** — of the virtues
**“and kindness”** — the forgiveness of sins
**“before him above all the women, and he set the royal crown”** — he made her a sharer of his kingdom
**“on her head”** — in the mind
**“and made her queen”** — “The queen stood on thy right hand”
**“instead of Vasthi”** — of the Synagogue, which, by spurning and crucifying the king, lost the dignity of the kingdom
2.18:
**“And he commanded a magnificent feast to be prepared for all the princes, and for his servants”** — the feast: spiritual joy in the whole world, where there are spiritual dishes, where there are the mysteries of the Lord’s body and blood
**“for the marriage and wedding of Esther”** — of the Church
**“And he gave rest”** — “Come to me, all you that labour”, etc.
**“to all the provinces”** — the burden of sins being laid down
**“and bestowed gifts”**
• spiritual
• “he gave gifts to men”
2.19:
**“And when … the second time”** — It is not enough for Christ to join the first Church to himself, but through the preachers he gained a plentiful multitude from the Gentiles. Whence: “Other sheep I have, that are not”, etc., and “them also I must bring”.
**“and gathered together, Mardochai”** — the teachers, who call the Gentiles together to the entrance of the faith and the sacrament of baptism
2.20:
**“Neither had Esther as yet declared her country and people, according to his commandment”** — because holy Church does nothing through arrogance; whence: “All the glory of the king’s daughter is within”, and elsewhere: “Our glory is this, the testimony of our conscience”
**“For whatsoever he commanded, Esther observed: and she did all things in the same manner as she was wont at that time when he brought her up a little one”** — when he instructed her among the first of the Church of the redeemed
2.21:
**“At that time, therefore, when Mardochai abode at the king’s gate, Bagathan and Thares, two of the king’s eunuchs … were angry”**
• unmanned, without strength of mind
• the scribes and philosophers, having the key of knowledge, neither going in themselves nor letting others go in
• Two eunuchs. In the two eunuchs can be marked the schismatics and the heretics, who, bearing in their heart the venom of fraud and malice, take counsel against the truth, to take it away from believers and to kill Christ, that is, the faith of Christ, in the faithful themselves; but the holy teachers lay bare their iniquity, that the innocent may be saved and those punished with just vengeance.
**“who were porters, and presided in the first entry of the palace”** — as if princes of doctrine
**“and they designed to rise up”** — “The chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council”
**“against the king”** — Christ
2.22:
**“And Mardochai”** — the order of preachers
**“had notice of it, and immediately he told it”** — to the faithful
2.23: **“in the histories, and … in the chronicles”** — The two Testaments, in which is written what rewards are due to the just and what punishments to the unjust; whence: “These shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting.” And in Ezechiel: “The justice of the just shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.”

3.1:
**“After these things, king Assuerus”** — Christ
**“advanced”** — in time
**“Aman”** — is interpreted “iniquity”
**“Aman, the son of Amadathi”** — The powerful of the world, who, abusing the benefits conferred by the divine power, scorn to have as sharers of grace those whom they have as sharers of nature, and strive to transfer to themselves the honour and reverence which they owed to God alone. And those who will not consent they pursue with hatreds and torments; but by the just judgement of God the wicked are caught in their own snares. Whence it is said: “The just is delivered out of distress: and the wicked shall be given up for him.” By Aman, whom Josephus records to be of the stock of Amalec, the people of the Jews can be figured, who slew the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and his apostles, losing the nobility of their race through unbelief and hardness of heart; who by Isaias are called “ye rulers of Sodom … ye people of Gomorrha”. Whence Ezechiel: “Thy father was an Amorrhite, and thy mother a Cethite.”
3.2:
**“And all the king’s servants, that were at the doors of the palace, bent their knees, and worshipped Aman: for so the emperor had commanded them, only Mardochai”** — the preachers of the gospel
**“did not bend his knee, nor worship him”** — “The Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve”
3.3: **“And the king’s servants … said to him”** — flatterers
3.6:
**“And he counted it nothing”** — that is, he held it
**“upon Mardochai alone”**
• on one only
• but on all the Jews
**“to lay his hands: for he had heard that he was of the nation of the Jews, and he chose rather to destroy all the nation of the Jews”** — all the Catholic people
3.7:
**“In the first month (which is called Nisan)”** — in the last time, when there will be a persecution such as has not been
**“the lot was cast”** — Those who belong to the Lord’s lot are slain; whom that goat signifies which in the law was slain according to the Lord’s lot.
**“which in Hebrew is called Phur, before Aman”** — before the persecutors of the faithful
**“on what day and what month the nation of the Jews”** — of the confessors of the faith
3.8:
**“And Aman said”** — the Jewish people
**“to king Assuerus: There is a people”** — the Christian
**“through all the provinces of thy kingdom”** — “Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth”
**“scattered”** — whence Peter: “to the strangers dispersed through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, elect”
**“and separated one from another, that use new laws and ceremonies”** — the New Testament; whence: “A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another, as I have loved you”
**“and moreover despise the king’s ordinances”**
• the old law
• in the opinion of the Jews; he who despises the law, which kills, follows the spirit, which quickens
**“and thou knowest very well”** — from whom nothing is hidden
**“that it is not expedient for thy kingdom that they should grow insolent”** — against thee
**“by impunity”** — of sinning
3.9:
**“If it please thee, decree that they may he destroyed”** — that is, the perfect observance of the observances of the law
**“and … ten thousand talents”** — by just weight
**“I will pay … to thy treasurers”** — to the scribes and Pharisees
**“thy treasurers”** — that is, “the treasures of wisdom and knowledge” of God
3.10:
**“And the king took the ring”** — in the opinion of the Jews
**“And … took”** — As Aman, sending letters, tries to fortify them with the king’s seal, that his wish may be the more easily fulfilled, so the Jews take the books of the divine law, in which is the seal of the highest King, that is, the grace of the Holy Ghost, as witness to prove their heresy, rejecting fellowship with the Gentiles and the gospel of Christ as if contrary to the divine commandments.
**“that he used, from his own hand”** — by power and working
**“and gave”** — permitted
**“it to Aman, the son of Amadathi of the race of Agag, the enemy of the Jews”** — of the true confessors
3.11:
**“And he said to him: As to the money which thou promisest, keep it for thyself”** — “Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire”, etc.; and: “I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks”
**“and as to the people, do with them as seemeth good to thee”** — as it was said to the devil: “All that he hath is in thy hand”
3.13: **“Were sent by the king’s messengers to all provinces”** — as Paul “received letters from the chief priests”, that if he found any, men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem
3.15: **“The couriers that were sent made haste to fulfill the king’s commandment. And immediately the edict was hung up in Susan, the king and Aman feasting together, and all the Jews that were in the city weeping”** — whence: “You shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice”

4.1:
**“she”** — that is, the slaughter of the Jews
**“Now when Mardochai had heard these things”** — the ministers of the Church
**“he rent his garments”** — searching out his works with discernment, lest in anything he displease God
**“and put on sackcloth”** — namely with tearful compunction of heart, with fasts and alms
**“strewing ashes”** — the remembrance of human frailty; whence: “Dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return”
**“on his head”** — on the mind
**“in the street”** — in the breadth of the common Church, which says: “When I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me”
**“and he cried with a loud voice … in the midst of the city”** — with the strong intent of the heart
**“shewing the anguish”** — compunction
**“of his mind”** — “his soul is in anguish”
4.2:
**“And he came lamenting in this manner even to the gate of the palace”**
• to the sight of the divine majesty
• Even to the gate. So the master of the Church longs to be heard by the King of all ages through the intercession of the queen, of whom it is said: “The queen stood on thy right hand”, etc., who is partly a pilgrim in the world and partly reigns with the Lord.
**“for no one”** — No one can enter the heavenly hall with the corruption of the present life; but before his death each one ought to knock at the entrance of the kingdom by chastisement of the body and compunction of heart, that afterwards he may enter the palace above rejoicing.
**“for no one clothed with sackcloth might enter the king’s court”**
• If anyone asks how a most just king can bring torments on the innocent, let him know that this proceeds not from a wish of malice but from the will of the highest counsel. For “Wisdom overcometh malice. She reacheth therefore from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly.”
• “Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, … in all the deeps.” By whose just judgement it comes about that the faithful are handed over into the hands of persecutors, either for cleansing or for correction or for the increase of merits. So Job is handed over to Satan, Paul is buffeted by an angel of Satan.
4.3:
**“And in all provinces”** — the churches
**“towns, and places”** — the gatherings of the faithful
**“to which the king’s cruel edict was come”** — law
4.4:
**“Then Esther’s maids and her eunuchs went in, and told her. And when she heard it she was in a consternation: and she sent a garment”** — the wedding garment
**“to clothe him, and to take away the sackcloth”** — “a garment of praise for the spirit of grief”
**“but he would not receive it”** — “Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not”
4.6:
**“And Athach going out went to Mardochai, who was standing”** — strong in adversity
**“in the street”** — in the breadth
**“of the city”** — of the Church
4.8:
**“He gave him also a copy of the edict which was hanging up in Susan, that he should shew it to the queen”** — the Church
**“and admonish her to go in”** — “The king hath brought me in”
**“to the king”** — of kings
4.11:
**“All the king’s servants”** — who “serve him with fear: and rejoice unto him with trembling”
**“and all the provinces that are under his dominion, know”** — the several churches
**“that whosoever, whether man”** — who is stronger, and so bolder
**“or woman”** — weaker, and so more submissive
**“who is not called for”** — before the time
**“the king’s inner court”** — the heavenly
**“cometh into”** — not having on a wedding garment
**“is immediately to be put to death without any delay”** — spiritually
**“except the king shall hold out the golden sceptre”** — the sign of merciful power
**“to him, in token of clemency, that so he may live. How then can I go in to the king, who for these thirty days”** — in the age of this life
4.13:
**“He sent word to Esther again, saying: Think not that thou mayst save thy life only”** — seek not the things that are thine own, but the things that are Jesus Christ’s
**“because thou art in the … house”** — the inner
**“king’s”** — of the highest
4.14:
**“For if thou wilt now hold thy peace”** — dost not intercede for us
**“the Jews shall be delivered by some other occasion: and thou, and thy father’s house”** — because thou hast no care for the children
**“shall perish”** — whence: “forget thy people and thy father’s house”
**“And who knoweth”** — few or none
**“whether thou art not therefore come to the kingdom, that thou mightest be ready in such a time as this?”** — as if: the king made thee queen for this, that thou mightest help us in persecution
4.15: **“And again Esther sent to Mardochai in these words”** — Again. Mardochai and Esther, that is, the masters and the disciples, pray for each other; as Paul prays for the disciples and begs that they pray for him; as in the Acts of the Apostles prayer was made by the Church “without ceasing” for Peter.
4.16:
**“Go, and gather together all the Jews whom thou shalt find in Susan, and pray ye for me. Neither eat”**
• he commends fasting
• the bread of desire
**“nor drink”** — the wine of pleasure, against prosperity and adversity
**“for three days”** — in the faith of the Trinity
**“and three nights”** — in which the Son of man was in the heart of the earth
**“and I”** — the Church
**“with my handmaids”** — the faithful souls, humble, cast down in their own eyes
**“will fast in like manner, and then I will go in to the king”** — fortified by continence
**“against the law, not being called”** — not worthy
**“and expose myself to death and to danger”** — “I will put my soul in my hands”

5.1:
**“And on the third day”** — in the time of grace; or after the incarnation, after the passion and resurrection
**“put on”** — with baptism
**“Esther”** — the Church
**“her royal apparel”** — with faith, hope and charity and the other virtues, clothed with which she may be more worthily joined to the king
**“and stood”** — strongly
**“in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s hall”** — the working of the present life, which looks towards the throne of the King above, who grants godly prayers
**“now he sat upon his throne in the hall of the palace, over against the door of the house”** — that he may see the faithful and judge the works of each
5.2:
**“And when he saw Esther the queen standing”** — not wavering in adversity
**“she pleased his eyes”** — who searches all things
**“and he held out”** — showed
**“the golden sceptre”** — The power of rule, or the cross of the passion, by which he gained the power of which it is said: “All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.” And elsewhere: “For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names.”
**“and she drew near, and kissed”** — fulfilling it with all devotion
5.3: **“And the king said to her: What wilt then, queen Esther? what is thy request? if thou shouldst even ask one half of the kingdom, it shall be given to thee”** — as if: “Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you”
5.4:
**“But she answered: If it please the king. I beseech thee to come to me this day, and Aman with thee”**
• not only friends but enemies are invited
• “Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you”
**“to the banquet which I have prepared”** — the bounty of preaching, where there is the bread which strengthens and “wine that maketh glad the heart of man”
5.5:
**“And the king said forthwith”** — the devotion of faith, in which God delights
**“Call ye Aman quickly”** — Call ye. The will of the queen who invites and of the king who commands agree; but woe to him who comes unworthily, who, though he comes invited, will yet not have the joy of the feast, his merits standing in the way. The king, then, will come in, see the guests, and cast him who has not on a wedding garment into the exterior darkness; whence: “The unjust shall be caught in their own snares.”
5.6: **“And the king said to her, after he had drunk wine plentifully”** — of the feast with which God refreshes
5.8:
**“If I have found favour”** — The putting off of the request is counted not to sloth but to patience. For not in the present but in the future the reward will be paid to the good and the wicked. For “tomorrow” is put for the future. Whence: “Be not solicitous for tomorrow”; and Jacob in Genesis says: “My justice shall answer for me tomorrow.” And of the lamb it is said: “Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning.” But when the judgement comes, it will be revealed in what garment each has come in to the feast.
**“and if it please the king to give me what I ask, and to fulfill my petition: let the king and Aman come to the banquet which I have prepared them, and tomorrow”** — in the future
5.9: **“So Aman went out that day joyful and merry”** — not knowing what the day to come might bring forth
5.10: **“and Zares his wife”** — That is, the habit of sinning. Or, according to the letter, the wives of kings and princes consented in the persecution of the faithful.
5.14: **“Then Zares his wife, and the rest of his friends answered him”** — attendants, ministers of crimes

6.1:
**“That night the king passed without sleep”**
• “He shall neither slumber nor sleep, that keepeth Israel”
• That night. Himself abiding unmoved, he contemplates the course of the times and the acts of all, and no thought is hidden from him to whom all things are present. Whence the Apostle: there is not in him “is” and “was”, but in him there is always “is”.
6.2: **“They came”** — The deeds of Mardochai are recalled before the king, because the good works of the holy teachers will never be given over to forgetfulness, but “the just shall be in everlasting remembrance”.
6.3: **“And when the king heard this, he said: What honour and reward hath Mardochai received for this fidelity? His servants and ministers said to him”** — who serve daily, who “desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ”
6.10: **“And the king said to him: Make haste”** — Make haste. The masters of the Church, made illustrious by the practice of all the virtues and the beauty of wisdom, are honoured with the crown of royal dignity as members of the highest King. They mount upon the king’s horse, that is, upon the faithful people, in whose hearts the King of angels dwells. Whence the prophet Habacuc: “Who will ride upon thy horses: and thy chariots are salvation.” To them Aman, the special enemy of the people of God, pays service, though against his will, when the persecutors of the Church are compelled to bear witness to that same Church, unable to hide what is plain.
6.11: **“So Aman took the robe”** — So Aman took, etc. This is the change of the right hand of the most High: he who seemed to himself the more glorious appears below others, viler and lower; according to that: “He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble.” Likewise Isaias says: “Libanus shall be turned into charmel, and charmel shall be esteemed as a forest.” So the pride of the Synagogue was crushed, the humility of the Church exalted. So the persecutors of the faith were brought to nothing, the confessors of Christ exalted in the whole world. The head was turned into the tail and the tail into the head, because everyone “that exalteth himself shall be humbled”.
6.13:
**“And he told Zares his wife, and his friends, all that had befallen him. And the wise men”** — for often worldly men, being converted, understand and confess the truth
**“whom he had in counsel, and his wife answered him: If … be of the seed of the Jews”** — the true
**“Mardochai … before whom thou hast begun to fall, thou canst not resist him”** — in whom God fights

7.1: **“So the king and Aman went in, to drink with the queen”** — So … went in, etc. On the second day of the feast Aman came, invited. But when Esther opened her request, he went out condemned to punishment. For in the gospel a dinner and a supper are mentioned. The dinner signifies the present time of the Church; the supper, the eternal and last feast. Whence, the wicked being separated, the good rejoice for ever. For Aman, because he had not a garment worthy of the feast, deserved to be cast out.
7.7: **“went … into the garden set with trees”** — As the king hastens into the garden, that is, invites the elect with him to the delights of paradise, he strives to entreat the queen for his life, but had not a fitting time. For the remedies of salvation are sought too late when the dangers of death are at hand. Whence Solomon: “Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and shall not find me.”
7.8:
**“And when the king came back out of the garden set with trees, and entered into the place of the banquet, he found Aman was fallen upon the bed on which Esther lay, and he said: He will force the queen also in my presence, in my own house. The word was not yet gone out of the king’s mouth, and immediately they covered his face”** — confusion and shame, according to that: “Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, that desire evils to me”
**“and immediately they covered”** — Aman’s entreaty is called forcing, because in the day of judgement the prayer of the wicked is provocation. Whence: “When he is judged, may he go out condemned; and may his prayer be turned to sin.” Then the oppression with which they oppressed the humble will be cast in their teeth.
7.9:
**“Harbona”** — He signifies the teachers of the law, who foretold the crimes and deceits of the Jews. Whence Moses: “I know that after my death you will do wickedly, and will quickly turn aside from the way that I have commanded you.” And in the gospel: “There is one that accuseth you, Moses, in whom you trust.”
**“one of the eunuchs that stood waiting on the king, said: Behold the gibbet which he hath prepared for Mardochai”** — “He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return to him”
**“in Aman’s house”** — Aman signifies the wicked raging against Christ and persecuting his Church. But Christ had been promised to them in the law; so the law, which was given for the keeping of life, was turned for them into death, by which they strove to blot out Christ and kill his confessors; and those who wished to oppress the innocent by the law received, with the law itself accusing them, the sentence of just judgement: “Whosoever have sinned in the law, shall be judged by the law.”
**“being fifty cubits high”** — on the fiftieth day after the sacrifice of the lamb the law was given on mount Sina
7.10: **“So Aman was hanged on the gibbet”** — “His sorrow shall be turned on his own head”, etc.

8.1:
**“On that day”** — On that day. Esther holds the house of Aman, the enemy of the Jews, when the Church possesses the world which the devil, the enemy of Christians, had possessed. Whence: “When a strong man armed keepeth his court”, etc. Mardochai comes in before the face of the king when daily the souls of the saints go in from their sojourn in this present life to the contemplation of the divine majesty.
**“king Assuerus gave”** — the true king
