**“Do not offer”** — Do not offer: with God neither the size of the gift nor the person of the mighty is regarded, but love and humility of heart; therefore sacrifice ought not to be offered from iniquity but from just labour.
**“And look not upon an unjust sacrifice, for the Lord is judge”** — he is just, not accepting the person of the rich nor despising the person of the poor
35.13:
**“The Lord will not accept any person against a poor man”** — because “the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: his countenance hath beheld righteousness”
**“and he will hear the prayer of him that is wronged”** — the Christian people, of whom it is said: “to thee is the poor man left: thou wilt be a helper to the orphan”
35.14: **“He will not despise the prayers of the fatherless; nor the widow”** — “Blessing I will bless her widow: I will satisfy her poor with bread”
35.16: **“He that adoreth God with joy, shall be accepted, and his prayer shall approach even to the clouds”** — to God
35.17:
**“The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds: and till it come nigh he will not be comforted: and he will not depart till the most High behold”** — with the eyes of mercy
**“but will judge for the just, and will do judgment”** — just
35.18:
**“And the Lord will not be slack”** — his help
**“and the Almighty will not have … with them”** — whom he now bears with
**“patience …, that he may crush their back”** — who “have wrought upon” the “back” of the just
**“And he will repay vengeance to the Gentiles, till he have taken away”** — from the world
**“the multitude of the proud”** — namely, all who are proud
35.19:
**“Till he have rendered to men”** — because he “will render to every man according to his works”
**“according to their deeds”** — each one’s own
**“and according to the works of Adam”** — original sin
**“Till he have judged the cause of his people”** — because he will come to judge the living and the dead
**“and he shall delight the just”** — in eternal blessedness
**“with his mercy”** — eternal life, given in mercy
35.20: **“The mercy of God is beautiful in the time of affliction”** — as rain is needed in drought, so the mercy of God in tribulation

36.1: **“Have mercy upon us”** — Have mercy upon us: in the person of the faithful he directs his prayer to God, that he defend them and bring down their enemies, so that, worthily corrected, these may acknowledge God again and forsake their idols.
36.2: **“And send thy fear upon the nations, that have not sought after thee: that they may know that there is no God beside thee, and that they may shew forth thy wonders”** — God has mercy on those who are merciful and pray for their enemies
36.3:
**“Lift up thy hand over the strange nations”** — the heathen, that, being strangers to Christ, they may become friends
**“that they may see thy power”** — that, seeing the miracles of thy power, they may be converted to the faith and from enemies become friends
36.6: **“Glorify thy hand, and thy right arm”** — Glorify thy hand, etc. He prays that the divine majesty, by the hand and the right arm, that is, by Christ, through whom the ancient miracles were done, may renew them in the time of grace, so that the same God may be understood to be God of the old law and the new.
36.7: **“Take away the adversary, and crush the enemy”** — Take away the adversary, etc. It signifies that by the coming of Christ the devil is to be taken out of the hearts of men. Whence: “When a strong man armed keepeth his court, those things are in peace which he possesseth.”
36.8:
**“Hasten the time”** — that the time may come quickly
**“and remember the end”** — because “it is the last hour”, and the end of the world draws near
**“that they may declare thy wonderful works”** — done at the coming of the Son
36.9:
**“by the rage of the fire”** — of hell
**“Let him that escapeth be consumed”** — that is, “He that loveth his life shall lose it”
**“and … that oppress”** — that is, treat most wickedly
**“thy people”** — who will not lay down his life in Christ
**“let them perish”** — eternal
36.10:
**“Crush the head”** — the devil
**“of the princes”** — of the persecutors
**“of the enemies”** — of God and of the Church
**“that say: There is no other beside us”** — because they think that they alone rule in the world
36.11:
**“Gather together”** — in the unity of the faith
**“all the tribes of Jacob”** — the faithful from among the gentiles, whom Jacob signified
**“that they may know that there is no God besides thee, and may declare”** — may preach to others
**“thy great works: and thou shalt inherit”** — unto the end
**“them”** — as Lord and heir of the Father
**“as from the beginning”** — of the faith
36.12:
**“Have mercy on thy people”** — the Church
**“upon whom”** — to be protected
**“thy name is invoked: and upon Israel”** — namely, of the faithful people beholding God
**“whom thou hast raised up to be”** — thou hast made a co-heir
**“thy firstborn”**
• Christ, who is “the firstborn of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth”
• Have mercy on thy people, etc. Having finished the prayer against sinners and against their head, the devil, wisdom now prays for the state of the Church and the salvation of the faithful.
36.13: **“Have mercy on Jerusalem, the city which thou hast sanctified, the city of thy rest”** — as if: “Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come”
36.14:
**“Fill Sion with thy unspeakable words”** — the Church, which looks upon the joy of the heavenly kingdom
**“and … with thy glory”** — of the miracles of power
**“Sion with thy unspeakable”** — Sion with thy unspeakable: the knowledge of Scripture, in which the unspeakable power of God is preached.
36.15:
**“Give testimony to them that are thy creatures from the beginning”** — of the Church
**“that are thy”** — “we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus in good works”
**“and raise up the prophecies”**
• the prophets praying for the coming of Christ
• And raise up the prophecies: all the prophets give testimony to the incarnation of Christ, that God, made man, would espouse the Church to himself.
36.16:
**“Reward”** — of eternal life
**“them that patiently wait”** — those who wait for the coming of thy Son
**“for thee, that thy prophets may be found faithful”**
• who promised these things
• for “many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see, and have not seen them”
36.17:
**“and hear the prayers of thy servants”** — “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done”
**“According to the blessing of Aaron over thy people, and direct us into the way of justice”** — for the salvation of the Christian people
**“and let all know”** — nations
**“that dwell upon the earth, that thou art God the beholder of all ages”** — namely, before the ages and after all ages; who in past times ordained beforehand through the grace of Christ the things to come
**“According to the blessing”** — According to the blessing: namely, the order and rite of the priesthood which the Lord gave his people; it shows how he united it to Christ, who is the great priest “according to the order of Melchisedech”, who “hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God”. According to the blessing of Aaron it is given to his people when it is directed into the way of justice, so that what Aaron figured in temporal sacrifices he may fulfil in the spiritual sacrifices of the gospel.
36.18: **“all meat”** — All meat: having foretold the calling of the gentiles to the faith of Christ, he warns us to keep a distinction between teachings, that as the throat discerns sweet food from bitter, so we may discern true teaching from false.
36.20:
**“A heart”** — of the heretics
**“A perverse”** — because “all the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice … thou hast wrought deceit”
**“will cause grief, and a man of experience”** — the catholic Church
**“will resist it”** — with “the shield of faith” and “the sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God)”
36.21:
**“every man”** — the divine word, which makes the soul fruitful
**“A woman will receive …: yet one daughter is better”** — as those who say: “I indeed am of Paul; and I am of Apollo; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ”
**“than another”** — or: than a daughter
36.22:
**“The beauty of a woman”**
• of corrected faith and good work
• The beauty of a woman: the grace of Christ, which heals souls through preaching and softens the concupiscence of the flesh. It abounds in the Church, whose desire is above every concupiscence of man, because in her is the comeliness of the virtues and the beauty of doctrine.
**“cheereth”** — delights, because “the heart of her husband trusteth in her”
**“the countenance of her husband”** — of the faithful soul, or of the Church
**“nothing more”** — Nothing more: no concupiscence of man can be compared with this desire, because “Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: the woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.”
36.23: **“her husband is not”** — Her husband is not: Christ, who exceeds human nature. Whence: “Thou art beautiful above the sons of men.” For he “did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.”
36.24:
**“He that possesseth a good wife, beginneth a possession”** — namely, the Church of Christ, his inheritance; whence: “Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance”
**“she is a help like to himself”** — because there is difference in the progress of knowledge and the working of virtues; for “star differeth from star in glory”
**“and a pillar”** — a stay
**“of rest”** — from labour
**“a help”** — A help: the help of the Church is according to the dispensation of Christ. Whence: “Just is my help from the Lord,” etc. He is the pillar of her weakness and the rest from her labour.
36.25:
**“Where there is no hedge”** — the wall of faith, which is founded on the preaching of the saints
**“shall be spoiled”** — by the demons
**“the possession”** — of the virtues
**“and where there is no”** — whatever is outside the Church perishes
**“wife”** — the Church, or the healing of the Holy Spirit
**“where there is no wife”** — Where there is no wife: as if: he who is outside the Church has no rest or protection; for wherever he turns aside through the teachings of heretics or philosophers, he will always be in error and will not find the light of truth.
36.26:
**“Who will trust him that hath no rest, and that lodgeth”** — the wall of faith, which is founded on the preaching of the saints
**“wheresoever the night taketh him, as a robber well appointed, that skippeth”** — namely, wandering and uncertain
**“him that hath no rest”** — Him that hath no rest (literally, no nest): that is, the Church, where the souls of the elect nourish the children of good works. Whence: “the sparrow hath found herself a house, and the turtle a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones.”

37.1:
**“Every friend will say”** — namely, the true and the false friend both profess to be friends
**“I also am his friend: but there is a friend, that is only a friend in name. Is not this a grief even to death?”** — it is a great evil, and one to be wiped out, where faith is hoped for and malice found, and where friendship is hoped for and perversity discovered
**“Every friend”** — Every friend: above he set out more carefully the true friend and the false, saying: “and will not abide in the day of thy trouble.”
37.2: **“But a companion”** — But a companion: the true friend loves with his whole mind and helps by his work; whence: “let us not love in word, nor in tongue, but in deed, and in truth.”
37.3:
**“O wicked presumption, whence camest thou”** — namely, from the evil will of the creature
**“to cover”** — thou
**“the earth with thy malice”**
• or: with wickedness
• or: malice
**“and deceitfulness”** — or: with deceitfulness
**“her”** — of those who have been deceived, and himself
**“O wicked presumption”** — O wicked presumption: he detests hypocrisy, when the wicked man pretends to be good, covering a dry malice, in which namely there is no fatness of charity or mercy.
37.4:
**“There is a companion”** — a false one
**“who rejoiceth with his friend in his joys”** — of pleasure
37.5:
**“There is a companion who condoleth with his friend for his belly’s sake”** — of feasting
**“for his belly’s sake”** — For his belly’s sake: for gluttony, not for friendship. Heretics can be understood in the false friends, who do everything correctly, as if counsellors of souls, when they are betrayers. Whence: “Beware of false prophets,” etc.
37.7:
**“Every counsellor giveth out counsel”** — “Be in peace with many, but let one of a thousand be thy counsellor”
**“but there is one that is a counsellor for himself”** — who chooses to do what pleases God, which is the one counsel poured in by the Holy Spirit
**“Every counsellor”** — Every counsellor: he still teaches that every caution is to be had in taking up friends and counsellors. For many pretend to be friends and counsellors and lay snares. Whence Jeremias: “Let every man take heed of his neighbour.”
37.8:
**“Beware of a counsellor. And know before what need he hath: for he will devise to his own mind”** — for a friend
**“Lest he thrust a stake”** — or: a stake
**“into the ground”** — that is, a sharp pole that is fixed in the ground
37.10:
**“Consult not with him that layeth a snare for thee, and … from them that envy thee”** — the envious
**“with him that layeth a snare for thee”** — With him that layeth a snare for thee (literally, with thy father-in-law): the father-in-law, who is plainly a relative through the woman, shows a womanish and changeable mind; likewise zeal, which is chiefly of souls.
37.11:
**“Treat not with a man without religion concerning holiness, nor with an unjust man concerning justice, nor with a woman touching her of whom she is jealous”** — is puffed up, or envies, or loves
**“nor with a coward concerning war, nor with a merchant about traffic”** — that is, the carrying across of minds
**“nor with a buyer of selling, nor with an envious man”** — that is, envious
**“give no heed”** — Give no heed: he has listed different kinds of counsellors, in which he named many persons who disagree with the truth. So he commanded that one should not take counsel with such, whose counsel is dangerous. The prudence, faith, will and religion of a counsellor must be looked to beforehand.
37.12:
**“But be continually with a holy man”** — “With the holy, thou wilt be holy.”
**“whomsoever thou shalt know to observe the fear of God”** — filial
**“Whose soul is according to thy own soul: and who, when thou”** — leaving the fear of God
**“shalt stumble in the dark”** — because he is unfaithful
37.13:
**“And establish within thyself a heart of good counsel”** — before all things
**“for there is no other thing of more worth to thee than it”** — or: other more faithful
37.14:
**“The soul of a holy man discovereth sometimes true things, more than seven watchmen”** — philosophers endowed with the knowledge of the liberal arts
**“that sit”** — as masters
**“to watch”** — as overseers of their subjects
**“The soul of a holy man”** — The soul of a holy man: having shown the diversity of counsellors, he adds how far the knowledge of the saints, poured in by the Holy Spirit, excels human wisdom.
37.16:
**“In all thy works let the true word go before thee”** — namely, the thought according to which outward speech and action are ordered; for “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh”
**“and steady counsel before every action”** — “Do thou nothing without counsel”
37.18:
**“A … word”** — evil counsel
**“wicked … shall change”** — by dwelling on evil things
**“the beast”** — the conscience
**“four manner of things”** — the words of the heart
**“arise, good and evil”** — counsel and reward
**“life”** — eternal
**“and death”**
• “the wages of sin is death”
• because through the tongue the secrets of the heart are laid open; for “Death and life are in the power of the tongue”
37.19:
**“A skilful man”**
• in holy Scripture
• A skilful man: because he had spoken beforehand of the tongue, he goes on about good and bad teachers.
**“hath taught many, and is sweet to his own soul”** — because from it he will receive an eternal reward
37.20:
**“He that … sophistically”** — twisted speech and heretical wickedness
**“speaketh …, is hateful: he shall be destitute of every thing”** — for show and deceit; but “the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful”
37.21:
**“Grace is not given him from the Lord: for … of all”** — of disputing and speaking
**“wisdom”** — of God
**“he is deprived”** — because he is deceitful
37.22:
**“There is a wise man”** — of Judaea
**“to his own soul”** — to be rewarded
**“that is wise …: and the fruit of his understanding is commendable”** — because he handles in his mind the things that please God, and his tongue sets out in speech what he brings forth
37.23:
**“A wise man”**
• the churchman
• the teacher
**“his own people”** — entrusted to him
**“instructeth”** — by word and example
**“and the fruits of his understanding”** — Scripture, or preaching
**“are faithful”** — or: faithful
37.24:
**“A wise man shall be filled with blessings”** — of heavenly reward
**“and they that see”** — the angels, or the souls of the saints
**“him”** — rewarded
**“shall praise”** — to whom it will be said: “Well done, good and faithful servant,” etc.
37.25:
**“life”** — of heavenly reward
**“of a man is in the number of his days: but the days of Israel”** — of the saints
**“are innumerable”** — because they will reign with the Lord without end
**“The life of a man is in the number”** — The life of a man is in the number: the present life of men is not uncertain with God. Whence: “The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee.”
37.26:
**“A wise man”** — the preacher
**“among his people”** — subject to him
**“shall inherit honour”** — namely, he will receive an eternal reward
37.27: **“My son, prove thy soul in thy life”** — prove the will of thy soul; “But prove all things; hold fast that which is good”
37.28:
**“For all things are not expedient for all”** — namely, keep it carefully, lest it slip away into the vices
**“and every kind pleaseth not every soul”** — namely, of will or of action is useful
37.29: **“Be not greedy”** — Be not greedy: according to the history, he praises frugality and reproaches gluttony, which leads the one who devours to sickness. Mystically, he warns that we be temperate in temporal things. Whence: “Thou hast found honey, eat what is sufficient for thee,” etc. And elsewhere: “not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise.”
37.30: **“For in many meats there will be sickness, and greediness will turn to choler”** — to the pouring out of gall

38.1: **“Honour the physician”** — Honour the physician: he wants us to be discerning in all things, because the works of God are very good; so we ought not to despise what the Creator is known to have made for our use. There are bodily physicians and there are spiritual ones. Bodily physicians cure bodies, spiritual ones souls; both, then, are to be honoured, but the spiritual are to be preferred.
38.2: **“For all healing is from God, and he shall receive gifts of the king”** — bodily or spiritual
38.3:
**“The skill of the physician shall lift up”** — in the world or in heaven
**“his head, and in the sight of great men”** — of the angels or the saints
**“he shall be praised”** — by the Lord
38.4: **“The most High hath created medicines out of the earth”** — for the health of men
38.5:
**“Was not bitter water made sweet with wood?”** — was made pleasant
**“with wood”** — With wood: he touches on the old history, that in the desert of Sur the children of Israel found bitter water, but God showed Moses a tree which, cast in, sweetened the water; where, according to the history, it is shown that the waters were sweetened by the medicine of the wood. Mystically, the bitter water signifies the law, which becomes drinkable if the confession and sacrament of the cross are joined to it.
38.6:
**“The virtue of these things … to the knowledge of men”** — came
**“and the most High hath given knowledge to men”** — of himself
38.7: **“he shall cure and shall allay their pains”** — of men
38.8:
**“By these”** — which he created
**“and of these the apothecary shall make sweet confections, and shall make up ointments of health, and there shall be no end”** — until the end of the world, when “this mortal” shall “put on immortality”
**“of his works”**
• the medicines
• of the true physician
• By these, etc. Physicians set different things against different sicknesses, namely foods and drinks, plasters and ointments, so that the medicines suit the diseases. Spiritual physicians do likewise.
**“For the peace of God is over all the face of the earth”** — namely, when “death is swallowed up in victory”
38.9:
**“My son, in thy”** — as if: pray constantly for thy sins
**“sickness neglect not thyself”** — because in the future, in hell, there is no redemption
**“but pray to the Lord”** — do not despair
**“and he shall heal thee”** — from the sickness of sin
38.10:
**“Turn away from sin”**
• thy mind
• Turn away from sin: it is like “Decline from evil and do good.” And cleanse your heart from all offence, and not the body only, that you may be “innocent in hands, and clean of heart.”
**“and order thy hands aright”** — to good works
38.11:
**“Give a sweet savour, and a memorial of fine flour”** — that is, of fine flour
**“and make a fat”** — with the devotion of charity
**“offering”** — by obeying
**“Give a sweet savour”** — Give a sweet savour: the sacrifice of bread and wine, offered in memory of the Lord’s passion, especially heals the wounds of souls, and is very necessary not only for the living but also for the dead.
38.12:
**“and then give place to the physician”**
• to thy teacher
• Give a sweet savour. Of the sickness and trouble which are sent by God’s ordering, either for the proving and rewarding of the just or for the condemnation of the reprobate; for he who sins in the sight of him who made him shall fall into the hands of the physician. For it is just that he who despises the commandments of God should be chastised and humbled, and seek the help he neglected. Spiritual physicians too seek the time for healing and earnestly pray the Lord to direct their works and give refreshment to the sick.
**“For the Lord created him”** — for thy uses
**“and let him not depart from thee”** — offended by disobedience
**“for his works are necessary”** — to thee
38.13: **“For there is a time when … into their hands”** — or: their
38.14: **“And they shall beseech the Lord, that he would prosper what they give for ease and remedy, for their conversation”** — or: their
38.16:
**“My son, shed tears over the dead, and begin to lament as if thou hadst suffered some great harm, and according to judgment cover”** — in burial
**“his body, and neglect not his burial”** — My son, etc. Because he has discussed sicknesses and the cures of physicians, he adds the funeral rites of the dead.
38.17:
**“for fear of being ill spoken of”** — that is, the parting from one’s neighbour
**“weep bitterly”** — he describes the measure of weeping
**“for a day”** — for a short time, lest too much sorrow take away merit
38.18:
**“For of sadness”** — to the despairing soul
**“cometh death, and it overwhelmeth”** — darkens
**“the strength”** — of good action
**“and the sorrow of the heart boweth down”** — softens
**“the neck”** — the strength
38.19:
**“In withdrawing aside”** — namely, in refusing comfort
**“sorrow remaineth”** — because it begins here and will last in the punishment to come, for want of trust in the comfort from above
38.20:
**“Give not up thy heart to sadness”** — of the world, which works the death of the soul
**“but drive it from thee: and remember the latter end”** — because the more faith and hope fail him, the more grief grows in distress
**“remember the latter end”** — Remember the latter end: the warning of good fathers, that their sons prepare for themselves the provision of good works for the journey.
38.21:
**“Forget it not”** — the last things
**“for there is no returning”** — that is, thou wilt not return here so as to be able to work
**“and thou shalt do him no good, and … thyself”** — with too much grief
**“shalt hurt”** — thou wilt treat badly
**“for there is no”** — For there is no: as if: be cautious in all things, then, lest perhaps at the death of your neighbour you grieve more than is right.
38.22:
**“Remember my judgment”** — namely, of the passing from this world, because “Who is the man that shall live, and not see death?”
**“for thine also shall be so: yesterday for me, and today for thee”** — as if: what is already fulfilled in me awaits thee
38.23:
**“When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest, and comfort him in the departing of his spirit”** — because as thou art, so wilt thou stand before the judge, to receive according to thy works
**“When the dead is at rest”** — When the dead is at rest: as if: keep continually the memory of the dying, and give him confidence, and strengthen him with hope, lest he fail at the last moment.
38.24:
**“The wisdom”** — divine
**“of a scribe”** — learn
**“cometh by his time”** — on the tablets of the heart
**“of leisure”** — of leisure
**“and he that is less in action, shall receive wisdom”** — because when the mind is intent on many things it is less for each
38.25:
**“With what wisdom shall he be furnished”** — those who know these things are not wholly strangers to wisdom
**“that holdeth the plough”**
• the office of the teacher, who tills the hearts of men with the ploughshare of the gospel
• That holdeth the plough: it signifies the holy preachers, who at all times instruct their hearers by teaching and exhorting, that they may draw out the virtue of the inner man and re-form the human soul to the image of God. Whence: “as a wise architect, I have laid the foundation.” And elsewhere: “My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you.” As many as are the kinds of virtues, so many are the workings and lessons the teachers press into the minds of the elect.
**“and that glorieth in the goad”** — of the divine testimonies
**“therewith”** — of exhortation
**“the oxen”** — the brutish
**“that driveth”** — namely, that they may not live sluggishly
**“and is occupied in … labours”** — good
**“their …, and his whole talk is about the offspring of bulls”** — of the proud
38.26:
**“He shall give his mind to turn up furrows”** — to root out vices and plant virtues
**“and his care is to give … fodder”** — fatness
**“the kine”** — of the females, because he has taken up the care of both sexes
38.28:
**“So doth the smith”**
• who forges spiritual weapons
• the order of preachers
**“sitting by the anvil”** — the hard labour of the present life
**“and considering the iron work. The vapour of the fire wasteth his flesh, and he fighteth with the heat of the furnace”**
• the tribulation and persecution of the world
• So doth the smith, etc. The order of preachers, who carry out their ministry through various offices, temper their teaching to their hearers; they form the frail and weak by word and example, so as to make vessels unto honour.
**“The noise of the hammer is always in his ears”** — namely, the edicts of princes strike in the terror of torments
**“and his eye is upon the pattern of the vessel”** — of elect souls
**“He setteth his mind to finish his work, and his watching to polish them, to perfection”** — of souls
**“He setteth his mind”** — He setteth his mind: when, by the footsteps of good works, he shows those under him the changeless way of life amid the rolling course of the present life.
38.29: **“So doth the potter sitting at his work, turning the wheel about with his feet, who is always carefully set to his work”** — of the office entrusted to him
38.30: **“He fashioneth the clay with his arm, and boweth down his strength before his feet”** — With his arm, etc. Because he strengthens the weak with many examples and with the words of catholic teaching, gives them examples of humility and meekness, and applies the intention of his heart, so that by the lesson of his gentleness he may soften whatever is harsh for the lesser of his subjects; and he watches for this, that in the furnace of the heart he may harden the work of his disciples with the fire of charity.
38.31:
**“All these”** — the teachers of the Church
**“to their hands”** — good works
**“trust …, and every one is wise in his own art”** — by the distribution of the Holy Spirit, “dividing to every one according as he will”
38.32:
**“Without these”** — spiritual gifts
**“a city is not built”** — the Church
**“And they shall not dwell”** — the faithful in it
**“nor walk about therein”** — “from virtue to virtue”
**“and … into the assembly”** — the heavenly court
38.33:
**“Upon the judges’ seat they shall not sit”** — since without these the preachers have neither the chair of honour nor the understanding of the law, nor can they teach worthily or do anything good
**“and the ordinance of judgment they shall not understand, neither shall they declare discipline and judgment, and … where parables are spoken”** — but openly
38.34:
**“But … the state”** — namely, the bodily
**“of the world they shall strengthen”** — or: they will consume
**“and their prayer shall be in the work of their craft”** — namely, it is acceptable to God with the works of the virtues
**“applying”** — for the brethren
**“their soul, and searching”** — meditating day and night

39.1:
**“the wisdom of all the ancients”** — of the patriarchs and prophets
**“The wise man will seek out”** — the churchman
**“and … in the prophets”** — in understanding them
39.2:
**“the sayings of renowned men”** — of the apostles and evangelists
**“He will keep”** — by believing and working
**“and … into the subtilties of parables”** — of the evangelists
**“will enter withal”** — by searching diligently
39.3:
**“the hidden meanings of proverbs”** — the mystical sense
**“He will search out …, and … in the secrets”** — the allegories
39.4:
**“among great men”** — of the catholic teachers
**“He shall serve”** — the divine offices
**“and … before”** — namely, pleasing God, not man
**“appear … the governor”** — of the ruler of the whole earth
**“into … countries”** — from God
**“He shall pass … strange”** — by preaching
**“for he shall try good and evil among men”** — namely, those who hear the word of God or despise it
39.5:
**“He will give his heart”** — he sets out the good conduct of the teacher who, keeping the rule of faith, preaches unceasingly both by word and by example
**“to resort early to the Lord that made him”** — namely, driving off the sluggishness of the body, he commends the beginning and the end of his words to God
**“and … in the sight of the most High”** — in his good pleasure
**“he will pray”** — who directs all our works
**“He will open his mouth”** — of the heart
**“in prayer, and will make supplication for his sins”** — for evils to be removed
39.6: **“For if it shall please the great Lord, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding”** — that he may know when and where and how to bring forth the divine words
39.7:
**“And he shall direct his counsel”** — of good will
**“and his knowledge”** — of right conduct
**“and in his secrets”** — in eternal inspiration
39.8: **“He shall shew forth the discipline he hath learned”** — namely, he will labour to preach the commandments of God with confidence
39.9:
**“shall praise”** — from God
**“Many … his wisdom”** — of his teaching
**“The memory of him shall not depart away”** — namely, of his works
39.11:
**“If he continue”** — in a longer life
**“a name”** — an honourable life and teaching
**“he shall leave”** — after him
**“above a thousand”** — namely, the many whom he will gain for the Lord
**“and if he rest”** — in death
**“it shall be to his advantage”** — who will pass over to eternal life
**“If he continue, … a name”** — If he continue, … a name: the name of Christ, whose members they are, from whom they have all things, who is the power and wisdom of the Father.
39.12:
**“I will yet meditate”** — within myself
**“that I may declare”**
• to my hearers
• the wonders of God, how he will render to every man according to his works
**“as with a holy transport”** — useful things
**“for I am filled”** — with the fervour of the Holy Spirit
39.13:
**“By a voice he saith: Hear me, ye divine offspring, and bud forth as the rose planted by the brooks of waters”**
• of the merit of the holy minds which hear the sound of the voice from above
• Hear me. Understand my teaching, you minds of the elect begotten through baptism, and bring forth the fruit of martyrdom in the course of mortal life.
39.14:
**“Give ye a sweet odour as frankincense”** — the odour of martyrdom, because “Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints”
**“Send forth flowers, as the lily, and yield a smell”** — of chastity, whose odour is spread through the world as an example to the faithful
**“and bring forth leaves in grace”** — so
**“and praise with canticles”** — that is, say a canticle of praise
39.15:
**“Magnify his name”** — living well, preach his power, that “your light” may “shine before men”
**“and give glory to him”** — by praising
**“with the voice of your lips, and with the canticles of your mouths”** — as if: bless the Lord in words and deeds
**“and with harps”**
• “Give praise to the Lord on the harp.”
• And with harps: whence: “Give praise to the Lord on the harp.” The harp (cithara) has a hollow of wood, a belly, at the bottom, which sends the strings upward and, when struck, sounds most sweetly. It is called cithara as if ‘struck with quick repetition’ (iteratione cita). To it are compared the works which reach out from earthly things to the grace above, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, etc., which are done for the love of God. The psaltery is a ten-stringed instrument which has its belly at the top, from which the singing strings come down to the lower parts; to it are fitted the commandments of the decalogue, which, after the shape of the psaltery, come to us from above.
39.16:
**“the works”** — bodily and spiritual
**“All … of the Lord are exceeding good”** — “God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good”
39.17:
**“At his word”** — in the Son
**“the waters stood as a heap”** — “he spoke, and they were made”
**“and at the words of his mouth the receptacles of waters”** — that is, which are received or ought to be received; it is said from excipio
**“At his word the waters stood”** — At his word the waters stood: when he gathered the waters and the dry land appeared, and made the firmament in the midst of the waters, that they might not slip outside their order. Or because the waters of the Red Sea “were as a wall on their right hand and on their left.” Or the water of persecution is held back by God’s dispensation.
39.18:
**“For at his commandment favour is shewn”** — the peace of the Church
**“and there is no diminishing of his salvation”** — he gives perfect salvation
39.19: **“The works of all flesh”** — The works of all flesh: the presence of God goes before all things, and whatever happens in time is present to him without time. So nothing is new or changeable in his sight.
39.21: **“There is no saying: What is this”** — There is no saying: What is this: he forbids us to be curious and to search into what it is not fitting to know. For all things will be made plain in their time, when the Lord “will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts.”
39.22:
**“His blessing … like a river”** — of living water
**“hath overflowed”**
• over those who fear him; whence: “out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water”
• His blessing, etc. As after the outpouring of the flood the waters went back so that the dry land might appear and bud, so after the destruction of the wicked the power of bearing fruit is given to the elect.
39.23:
**“And as a flood”** — the deluge
**“the earth”** — the land
**“hath watered”** — in the days of Noah
**“so shall his wrath … the nations”** — unbelieving
**“inherit …, that have not sought after him”** — by searching out his law and commandments
39.24:
**“Even as he turned the waters into a dry land, and the earth was made dry: and his ways”** — of the Lord
**“were made plain for their journey: so to sinners they are stumblingblocks in his wrath”** — because he repays them according to their works; for the ways of the Lord are his judgements, their ways are their works
39.25:
**“Good things … for the good”** — of eternal life
**“were created … from the beginning, so for the wicked, good and evil things”**
• of eternal life
• if they repent
• if they persist
39.26:
**“The principal things necessary for the life of men”** — he rebukes the prodigal and the riotous
**“The principal things necessary”** — The principal things necessary: before the flood men were nourished on the fruit of the earth, their natural food; meat had not yet been granted.
**“are water, fire”**
• by which bodily life is chiefly nourished
• because it is the instrument of various arts
**“salt”** — with which, if things are seasoned, rotting is kept off
39.27:
**“All these things”** — which they use well and lawfully
**“shall be for good to the holy, so to the sinners and the ungodly”** — who abuse them
**“they shall be turned into evil”** — condemnation
39.28:
**“There are spirits”** — evil
**“that … for vengeance”** — of the wicked
**“are created”** — of themselves, not by God
**“and in their fury they lay on grievous torments”** — who for their wickedness and their leading astray of the human race will suffer eternal punishments
**“In the time of destruction”** — of the antichrist, when Satan will be loosed
**“they shall pour out their force”** — because they do not fear to provoke the vengeance of God against themselves
39.29: **“Fire, hail”** — Fire, hail: before sin all things obeyed man, but after sin “the whole world shall fight with him”. Hence famine and death and a thousand dangers of death; the beasts too rage against him, and the sword of heavenly vengeance.
39.31: **“In his commandments”** — In his commandments: because according to the sentence from above, at the fitting time a worthy vengeance will lay waste the sinners. Whence: “I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh.”
39.32: **“Therefore from the beginning I was resolved”** — Therefore from the beginning I was resolved: he looks back to what he said above: “There is no saying: What is this, or what is that?” etc. For he sees the incomprehensible judgements of God and his unsearchable ways, and does not dare to speak or write anything rashly about them; but, discussing them with restraint, he has left set down not the cause but the manner made plain by the divine counsel. Whence he adds: “All the works of the Lord are good,” etc.
39.33: **“All the works of the Lord are good, and … every work in due time”** — in its time
39.34: **“It is not to be said”** — It is not to be said: he gives useful counsel, that we should not discuss the works of God incautiously, but praise and bless the Creator in all things.
39.35: **“Now therefore with the whole”** — Now therefore with the whole: as if: do not say that former times were better than these. Virtues make the days good, vices make them bad.

40.1:
**“Great labour”** — “Man is born to labour”
**“is created”** — in the sin of Adam
**“for all men, and a heavy yoke”** — of the affliction of sin
**“is upon the children of Adam”** — the heirs of original sin
**“from the day of their coming out of their mother’s womb, until the day of their burial into the mother of all”**
• the earth
• “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth, out of which thou wast taken”
40.2:
**“Their thoughts”**
• the various cares of the mind
• Their thoughts: he lists the evils which man suffers for his sins.
**“and fears of the heart”** — of different works
**“their imagination of things to come, and the day of their end”** — namely, by these he is afflicted while he awaits death, and in the day of his end he will receive a certain sentence for his vices
40.3: **“him that sitteth on a glorious throne”** — God does not accept persons, because he is a just judge
40.4:
**“From him that weareth purple, and beareth the crown, even to him that is covered with rough linen: wrath”** — namely, the vengeance on sins
**“and strife”** — because there is no peace there, no easing of pain
40.5:
**“envy, trouble, unquietness, and the fear of death”** — because there “no order, but everlasting horror” dwells
**“continual anger”** — the everlasting burning of the judge
**“And in the time of rest”** — of reward, when, the body laid in the bed of the tomb, the soul is assigned to punishment
**“upon his bed, the sleep”** — because there he thinks very differently about his deeds
40.6:
**“A little”** — A little: because the dead and senseless flesh seems to rest for a time, the soul already feels pain, and after the resurrection it will live with its body in eternal punishments.
**“He is troubled”** — He is troubled: the wicked will be tormented in punishment because in the time given them for penance they do not cease to sin. For, as if deluded in sleep, they think prosperity a time of peace, not of war, though the present life is granted to man that through the good fight he may come to blessedness. So in the time of his safety, while he has an acceptable time, he rose up in pride, burning with desire for earthly things, without any fear of God, against every condition of men, namely of noble and base.
40.8:
**“Such things happen to all flesh, from man even to beast, and”** — therefore
**“upon sinners are sevenfold more”** — namely, those who sin in this way
**“and upon sinners”** — And upon sinners: namely, a full and perfect vengeance will come, so that those who do not cease to sin in the present life, which runs its course in sevens, will be tormented without end.
40.10: **“and for their sakes”** — And for their sakes: manifold punishment is assigned to sinful man, that he may be corrected, repent, and beware thereafter; but because he neglects it and goes on even under punishment, God brings the flood on the world to destroy man whom he had created. Yet compared with the punishment to come, what man suffers in the present is nothing.
40.11:
**“All things that are of the earth, shall return to the earth again”** — men also; whence: “dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.”
**“and all waters shall return to the sea”** — whence: “Unto the place from whence the rivers come, they return”
**“and all waters”** — And all waters: namely, the works of sinners do not gain the fruit of the reward above, but the destruction of punishments.
40.12:
**“All bribery”** — namely, gain gathered through greed
**“and injustice”** — of any kind
**“shall be blotted out”** — because “the world passeth away, and the concupiscence thereof”
**“and fidelity shall stand for ever”** — that is, the reward of the faith “which worketh by charity”
40.13:
**“The riches of the unjust shall be dried up like a river”** — they will be quickly scattered
**“and shall pass away with a noise like a great thunder in rain”** — as if: the greedy make a din like thunder, and their treasure quickly runs away
**“The riches of the unjust”** — The riches of the unjust: they begin to sprout, but they waver in temptation and suddenly wither at the first heat of persecution.
40.14:
**“While he openeth”** — to receive
**“his hands he shall rejoice”** — the greedy man
**“but transgressors”** — of the commandment of God, who says: “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s goods”
**“shall pine away in the end”** — empty of all good things
40.15:
**“The offspring of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches, and make a noise as unclean roots upon the top of a rock”** — the hardness of heart which “believeth for a while, and in time of temptation … fall away”
**“The offspring of the ungodly”** — The offspring of the ungodly: we often see the progeny of the wicked quickly fail, above all when the sons imitate the iniquity of their fathers.
40.16:
**“The weed growing over every water”** — or: water
**“and at the bank of the river, shall be pulled up before all grass”** — “as the grass … which withereth before it be plucked up”
40.17:
**“grace”** — of God, which abounds in the faithful
**“is like a paradise in blessings”** — namely, it bears the fruit of different kinds of virtues
**“and mercy remaineth for ever”** — “Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy”
40.18:
**“The life of a labourer that is content with what he hath, shall be sweet”** — namely, for good and useful labour an eternal reward will be paid
**“The life of a labourer that is content”** — The life of a labourer that is content: “The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much.”
**“and in it thou shalt find a treasure”** — of the heavenly city
**“thou shalt find a treasure”** — Thou shalt find a treasure: a Christian; for he truly proves himself a Christian who believes and does the commandments of Christ.
40.19:
**“Children, and the building of a city”** — the building up of good works
**“shall establish a name, but a blameless wife shall be counted above them both”** — the soul; for virginity too stands out among the merits of the saints
40.20:
**“Wine and music rejoice the heart”** — the fervour of the knowledge of the law gladdens
**“but the love of wisdom is above them both”** — of the gospel
**“Wine and music”** — Wine and music: these naturally soothe and cheer the mind, but the love of wisdom and a tongue that teaches sweetly strengthen the understanding much more.
40.21: **“The flute and the psaltery make a sweet melody, but a pleasant tongue is above them both”** — the preaching of the apostles
40.22: **“favour and beauty”** — Favour and beauty: the adornment of the temple and the variety of worship which the former people had under the law; the preaching of the gospel, sown in the world, excels it in the greenness of good works.
40.23: **“A friend and companion”** — the fellowship of Christ and the Church surpasses every fellowship of the former fathers
40.24:
**“Brethren are a help in the time of trouble, but mercy … more than they”** — of our redemption
**“shall deliver”** — the human race
40.26: **“Riches and strength”** — Riches and strength: the riches given by the Lord in the time of the law strengthened the hearts of the ancients, to whom it was said: “If you be willing, and will hearken to me, you shall eat the good things of the land”; but the fear of the Lord and the voluntary poverty of the Church of Christ excel both these and all the riches of the world. Whence: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
40.27:
**“The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and … above all glory”** — earthly
**“they have covered it”** — eternal rewards
40.28:
**“My son, in thy lifetime”** — present
**“be not indigent”**
• in virtues or good conduct
• he forbids sloth and idleness
**“for it is better to die”** — by bodily death
40.29:
**“The life of him that looketh toward another man’s table is not to be counted a life”** — spiritual; whence: “Give us of your oil, for our lamps are gone out”
**“him that looketh”** — Him that looketh: for it is foolish to be idle and seek a wage from another’s labour; for every one will receive according to his works.
**“But a man, well instructed and taught”** — by divine instruction
**“will look to himself”** — that he may not be idle while he has time to work
40.30:
**“in the mouth”** — in sluggishness
**“in the mouth of the unwise”** — In the mouth of the unwise: he who likes to be idle and sluggish, and not to profit his neighbours by teaching, will burn at last in the pains of hell and in a late repentance.

41.1: **“to a man that hath peace”** — To a man that hath peace: to him who loves the prosperity and riches of the world, bodily death is bitter, because he neglects the joys of the life to come.
41.2:
**“O death, thy sentence is welcome”** — the sentence of death is good for Christians, because through it they pass over to eternal life
**“to the man that is in need”** — in earthly supports
**“and to him whose strength faileth”** — not presuming on himself
**“Who is in a decrepit age”** — whence: “And decaying he died in a good old age”, Abraham
**“and that is in care about all things”** — for fulfilling the commandments of the Lord or helping his neighbours
**“and to the distrustful”** — who does not consent to heretical error
**“that loseth patience”** — of the world, which is foolishness with God
41.3:
**“Fear not the sentence of death”**
• temporal
• who rather fears him who can destroy both soul and body in hell
**“Remember what things have been before thee, and what shall come after thee: this sentence”** — of temporal death
**“this sentence”** — This sentence: it is common to all flesh, and no one can escape it, even if he lives a hundred or a thousand years or more. Whence: “Who is the man that shall live, and not see death?”
41.5:
**“For among the dead there is no accusing of life”** — in hell confession profits nothing; whence: “who shall confess to thee in hell?”
**“children of abominations”** — Children of abominations: abominable are the children of sinners who namely have imitated their wicked fathers. Whence he adds: “they that converse near the houses of the ungodly.”
41.6: **“The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish”** — whence: he shall “pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living”
41.7: **“of an ungodly father”** — Of an ungodly father: he who brings up his children badly or ruins them by example is guilty of their perdition; or he who begets evil works from a perverse will will be condemned for them.
41.9:
**“And if you be born, you shall be born in malediction”** — “For behold I was conceived in iniquities,” etc.
**“and if you die”** — not reborn through grace
**“in malediction shall be your portion”** — “Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire,” etc.
**“And if you be born”** — And if you be born: he answers what went before, where he discussed temporal death; for as man, created of the earth, returns to the earth for original sin, though he will rise again in incorruption, so the wicked, cursed for their sins, will go with body and soul into eternal perdition.
41.11:
**“The mourning”** — “Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted”
**“of men”** — of wise men who obey the divine commandments
**“is about their body, but the name of the ungodly shall be blotted out”** — from the book of the living and from the world
41.12:
**“Take care of a good”** — or: clean
**“Take care”** — Take care: that you live well and religiously; for so a good name is gained. “A good name is better than great riches.”
41.13:
**“A good life”** — there will be
**“hath its number of days: but a good”** — of eternal days; whence: “I will fill him with length of days”
**“name shall continue for ever”** — the reward of a good life and a good name will remain for ever
41.14:
**“discipline”** — of conduct
**“My children, keep … in peace”** — “Follow peace with all men”
**“for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?”** — as if: it is not enough to live well unless you strive to teach others according to your ability
41.15:
**“Better is the man that hideth his folly”** — namely, he who avoids vain talk and wicked teaching
**“than the man that hideth his wisdom”** — “Woe is me, because I have held my peace”
**“Better is the man”** — Better is the man: “He that hideth up corn shall be cursed among the people: but a blessing upon the head of them that sell.”
41.16:
**“Wherefore have a shame of these things I am now going to speak of”** — “The soul which blesseth, shall be made fat”
**“Wherefore have a shame”** — Wherefore have a shame: because he has said beforehand that a good name and a good life are useful, and has rebuked those who hide their knowledge, he urges them to return to the pursuit of teaching; because it is not good to be irreverent and disobedient to one’s teacher. Whence: “and give me not over to a shameless and foolish mind, O Lord.”
**“For it is not good to keep all shamefacedness: and all things do not please all men in opinion”** — as if: yet not all things suit all men; what profits some harms others; whistling calms horses and excites puppies
**“it is not good”** — It is not good: according to the letter, he instructs us to beware of the vices and give our effort to the virtues, and not to despise the better and choose the worse, which everlasting confusion follows.
41.17:
**“Be ashamed of fornication before father and mother”** — of idolatry or of a heretical sect
**“before a governor”** — before the eyes of God
**“and of a lie … and a man in power”** — of the pledge you promised in baptism
41.18:
**“Of an offence before a prince, and a judge”** — before Christ, who is to judge the living and the dead
**“before a congregation and a people”** — of the angels, and the people of the saints
41.21:
**“Turn not away thy face from thy neighbour”** — by not sharing with the needy
**“of taking away”** — from anyone
**“a portion”** — of money
**“and not restoring”** — by admiring eloquence
**“Turn not away thy face”** — Turn not away thy face: when the angels gather out of the Church all scandals and rebuke the unjust for their injustice, then it will be made plain who has acted deceitfully about the truth and covenant of God in the tabernacle of the Church, or committed theft. He too will be convicted who gave himself to revelling and drunkenness, and who greedily seized, or did not pay out, what he received from God. He too will be confounded who hid the talent of the word, who turned his face from his brethren, and who mixed himself in the fornications of the heretics.
**“Gaze not upon … wife”**
• the teaching
• Gaze not upon … wife: fleshly desire, which ought to be subject to the spirit; we ought not to search into it and be subject to its suggestions.
**“another man’s”** — of the heretic, who is a stranger to the faith and religion
**“and be not inquisitive after his handmaid, and approach not her bed”** — by pressing on to pleasure
41.22:
**“Be ashamed of upbraiding speeches before friends”** — whence: “Practise not evil against thy friend, when he hath confidence in thee”
**“and after thou hast given, upbraid not”** — he who upbraids darkens the gift; imitate God, “who giveth to all men abundantly, and upbraideth not”
41.23: **“Repeat not the word which thou hast heard, and disclose not the thing that is secret”** — that is, do not stain the mystical words of the law with the speech of perverse doctrine, or turn the simple truth of faith into error

42.1:
**“Repeat not”** — Repeat not: he forbids saying good and evil together from the hiddenness of the heart. Whence: “Doth a fountain send forth, out of the same hole, sweet and bitter water?”
**“so shalt thou be truly without confusion, and shall find favour before all men: be not ashamed of any of these things”** — the things I have said by way of warning, or have proposed to say
**“and accept no person to sin thereby”** — “Thou shalt not accept person nor gifts,” etc.
42.3: **“Of the affair of companions and travellers”** — lest thou be confounded (understand: by speaking false and silly things, or weaving in some fraud)
42.4:
**“Of exactness”** — Of exactness: equity is to be followed everywhere, and the rule of the balance and weights observed, so that we make a just gain, whether much or little, and do not overreach a brother in buying. Let us also rule those under us with the discretion of discipline.
**“Of exactness of balance and weights, of getting much or little”** — Of exactness of balance. These words show how much hypocrisy and guile displease the Lord. “A deceitful balance is an abomination before the Lord: and a just weight is his will.” He who weighs the cause of the poor otherwise than that of the powerful, or thinks his own errors lighter than those of others, or those who “bind heavy and insupportable burdens, and lay them on men’s shoulders”, or he who does good in public and evil in secret, is abominable to the Lord.
42.5: **“and … of a wicked slave”** — And … of a wicked slave: it signifies that the slave who is not corrected by words must be restrained by blows. The slave of the vices too must be corrected with severe discipline.
42.6:
**“over a wicked wife”** — the heretic
**“Sure keeping is good”** — of the catholic faith, by which his wickedness is overcome
**“Where there are many hands”** — Where there are many hands: he warns that where there are different wills eager for spiritual gain, one must give out cautiously; some seek the word with the wish to tempt, others to learn; but not all things suit all men.
42.8: **“to inform”** — To inform: he who rebukes each with fitting discipline shows himself a learned and approved teacher in the sight of the saints. Nor is youth to be despised in a teacher, since life and discretion commend him. Whence: “Let no man despise thy youth.”
42.9:
**“The father … for the daughter”** — the soul, or the Church
**“when no man knoweth”** — of the faithful man, or of the believing people
**“waketh …, and the care for her taketh away his sleep, when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age, and when she is married, lest she should be hateful”**
• The father … for the daughter, etc. Mystically, the daughter of the father is the soul of the faithful man, or the Church of the believing people, which he commends to a vigorous teacher, who is watchful and shrewd on her behalf in all things, lest while she is still untrained in faith and knowledge she become an adulteress through the craft of the heretics, and hateful to her husband; of whom it is said: “I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ”; lest under his rule she conceive by error, or transgress the law of God and become barren in all good things.
• The daughter … hidden: according to the letter, he teaches parents to bring up their offspring and nourish them with discipline, and not to slacken the reins to wantonness and pleasure. Whence: “Give him not liberty in his youth.”
42.11: **“Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter: lest at any time she make thee become a laughingstock to thy enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and she make thee ashamed before all the multitude”** — Over a shameless daughter, etc. She who needs the diligent keeping of the master. For if she is left to her own will she confounds her teacher and makes him blush before all the multitude of the people. Whence: she who serves you is dangerous to you if you often look at her face. For immodest eyes do not know how to consider the beauty of the soul, but only of bodies.
42.12: **“Behold not everybody’s beauty”** — he teaches us to keep purity of heart and of body
42.14: **“better is the iniquity”** — Better is the iniquity: ‘woman’ signifies the sex, as there: “God sent his Son, made of a woman”; or weakness, as here: “Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.” In this place, then, the man is the strong and discerning in his desires, the woman the weak and undiscerning mind; and it often happens that the discerning man slips into a fault while the weak one shows good work; but the undiscerning one, growing proud of his good deeds, falls more heavily, while the discerning one, repenting, returns to the rule of discretion and thereafter acts more strongly and more cautiously. For the fault of the strong often becomes the occasion of virtue, and the virtue of the weak the occasion of sin. This woman brings to reproach, because she does things worthy of confusion.
42.15:
**“I will now remember the works of the Lord, and I will declare the things I have seen. By the words of the Lord are his works”**
• “he spoke, and they were made”
• I will now remember, etc. So far he has discussed various matters and, fittingly describing the mortality of each, has set out the various kinds of virtues and vices; now he turns to the praise of the Creator and the preaching of his works, and afterwards describes the brave deeds of the fathers.
42.16:
**“The sun giving light hath looked upon all things”**
• Christ, of whom it is said: “unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise”
• because “neither is there any creature invisible in his sight”
**“and full of the glory of the Lord is his work”** — “How great are thy works, O Lord? thou hast made all things in wisdom”
42.17:
**“Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works”** — namely, the things which lie open to men, revealed through the saints; whence: “With my lips I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth”
**“which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established”** — always the same
42.18:
**“the deep”** — the depth of God’s counsels
**“He hath searched out … and the heart of men”** — “the searcher of hearts and reins”
**“For the Lord knoweth”** — For the Lord knoweth: because all the ages of the world are present to him, with whom nothing is past and nothing future; he alone reveals mysteries, who knows the hearts of each, who looks into all thoughts and words; “for all things are naked and open to his eyes.”
42.21:
**“the glorious works of his wisdom”** — The glorious works of his wisdom: namely, when he revealed to the faithful, through the prophets and apostles, the sacrament of his counsel, “hidden from ages and generations”. For he is before all and after all, to whom nothing is added and from whom nothing is taken away.
**“Nor can he be diminished, and he hath no need of any counsellor”** — “who hath been his counsellor?”
42.22:
**“O how desirable are all his works, and what we can know is but as a spark!”**
• because they are perfect; whence: “the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them”
• As a spark, etc. We look into the works of God as at a spark, because we gain scarcely a small knowledge of them.
42.23:
**“All these things live, and remain for ever”** — to the Creator, for whom nothing perishes, to whom all things were present before they were
**“and for every use all things obey him”** — because all things are set in his will
42.24:
**“All things are double, one against another, and he hath made nothing defective”** — nothing is lacking to the divine commonwealth
**“All things are double”** — All things are double: God has so ordered all things that those which seem contrary to one another agree, like the elements or the four seasons.
42.25:
**“He hath established the good things of every one”** — according as they are useful
**“And who shall be filled with beholding his glory?”** — “They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst”

43.1: **“The firmament on high is his beauty, the beauty of heaven with its glorious shew”** — The firmament on high, etc. The beauty of the firmament, through the brightness of the stars, shows the power of the Creator; but still more the comeliness of the Church, in the virtues and miracles of the saints, makes plain the excellence of the Redeemer, who by his splendour enlightens believers and by the heat of judgement will punish sinners. Whence he adds: “The sun when he appeareth,” etc.
43.2:
**“The sun”** — in the presence of the incarnation
**“when he appeareth shewing forth”** — the kingdom of God
**“at his rising, an admirable instrument, the work of the most High”** — “And the Word was made flesh,” etc.
43.3:
**“At noon he burneth the earth, and who can abide his burning heat?”** — because he prepares the punishments of hell for sinners
**“and who can abide”** — And who can abide: no one is equal to the splendour of the Godhead with bodily eyes. Whence: “man shall not see me and live.”
43.4: **“keeping a furnace”** — Keeping a furnace: because the eternal flame torments the proud for evil thought, speech and work.
43.5:
**“Great is the Lord that made him”** — namely, the dispensation of the incarnation, that the proud might be confounded and the humble exalted by the knowledge of God
**“and at his words”** — And at his words: mystically, the word mocks the understanding of the proud. Whence: “To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God.”
**“he hath hastened his course”** — He hath hastened his course: when in the preaching of the gospel the way of salvation and the entrance to the heavenly kingdom were prepared.
43.6:
**“And the moon in all”** — And the moon in all: after discussing the sun he discusses the moon, because the Church follows Christ and is lit by him, as the moon by the sun.
**“And the moon in all in her season, is for a declaration of times and a sign of the world”** — Because he says the moon is a declaration of times and a sign of the world, and it marks the festival day; for by its monthly wanings and its running through the zodiac it shows the series of the years and the age of the world. For the Hebrews measured the reckoning of time and the passing of the year by the course of the moon; they honoured the first month, in which they came out of Egypt, with the solemnity of the Pasch, celebrated the new moons of each month, and named all the months from the word for moon. Whence: “The month is called after her name.” The month (mensis) is called so among the Latins from measure or from the moon, which in Greek is called mēnē, because they reckoned the months by the course of the moon. They call the first month of new things, in which the Pasch is celebrated, Nisan; because of the moon’s wandering course it falls now in March, now in April, and sometimes takes some days of May; but it is more rightly assigned to April, because in it it either begins or ends or is wholly contained.
43.7: **“a light that”** — A light that: the moon has no native brightness but receives it from the sun; so too the Church from Christ, which in persecution seems to wane but grows bright in part; for it grows wonderfully in its perfection.
43.8: **“an instrument of the armies”** — An instrument of the armies: because in it stands the multitude of the faithful, which shines gloriously through the whole world in the firmament of truth and of divine preaching.
43.9: **“The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven; the Lord enlighteneth the world on high”** — The glory of the stars, etc. The adornment of the Church is the fullness of the saints, whom God on high has ordained to enlighten it by the preaching of the gospel; these, abiding in holy words and in the teaching of the true faith, await the judgement of God.
43.10: **“By the words of the holy one they shall stand in judgment, and shall never fail in their watches”** — By the words of the Lord, etc. Because “in their patience they possess their souls”; with their loins girt and lamps in their hands, they wait for their Lord, “when he shall return from the wedding.”
43.11:
**“Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it”** — God set the bow as a sign that he would no more destroy the world with the waters of a flood
**“it is very beautiful in its brightness”** — because Scripture is very bright in its sense
**“Look upon the rainbow”** — Look upon the rainbow: the writing of the Old or the New Testament; whence: “he hath bent his bow and made it ready.” Here a sweet yoke is shown to the faithful, and terrible arms to the stubborn.
43.12:
**“It encompasseth the heaven about with the circle of its glory”** — because it tells sufficiently of the things above and below
**“It encompasseth the heaven”** — It encompasseth the heaven: when the Old and the New Testament were set up by the power and wisdom of God, that is, Christ; whence: “the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these things.”
43.13:
**“By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace”**
• that is, he has brought the cold to the brightness of justice
• the cold hearts of the wicked; whence: “Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow”
**“and sendeth forth swiftly the lightnings”** — the terrors of judgement, or miracles of power
43.14:
**“Through this are … opened”**
• to the world
• as in the conversion of Paul
**“the treasures”** — in the ways
**“and the clouds fly out like birds”** — “Who are these, that fly as clouds”
43.15: **“and … are broken”** — And … are broken: the teachers, who water the earth of the human heart and carry within them the storm of rebuke and pour it out in season; and they break the hailstones, namely by rebuking the hardness of the wicked heart, lest they stone the living grass.
43.16:
**“At his sight shall the mountains be shaken”** — the proud
**“the south wind shall blow”** — The south wind shall blow: this is the auster, a warm wind which by its heat melts the waters hardened with cold. This is the grace of the Holy Spirit, which by its heat scatters what was bound by the frost of mortal sin. So when the south wind blows, that is, when the Holy Spirit sends out the breath of teaching through the preachers, the mountains are shaken, that is, the powerful, sometimes to the persecution of the Christian name and sometimes to repentance.
43.17:
**“The noise of his thunder”** — the preaching of eternal terror, by which earthly hearts are fed
**“shall strike the earth”** — by rebuking vices
**“the northern storm”** — of the devil
**“storm”** — Storm: God permits various temptations through evil spirits, which try to make the fervour of faith and love grow cold.
**“And as the birds lighting”** — because of pride
**“upon the earth, he scattereth snow”** — he scattereth snow to settle, when with the cold of malice he prepares a seat for himself
**“and the falling thereof, is as the coming down of locusts”** — because he strives to lay waste everything green and fruitful
43.18:
**“at the beauty of the whiteness thereof”** — because he “transformeth himself into an angel of light”
**“The eye admireth …, and the heart is astonished at the shower thereof”** — when he stirs up open storms of persecution; for if he cannot deceive, he rages openly
43.19:
**“frost”** — the cold of unbelief
**“as salt”**
• barrenness
• As salt: that is, barrenness; for where salt is scattered, barrenness follows. And the devil, by the cold of unbelief, makes earthly hearts barren of good works.
**“He shall pour … upon the earth: and when it freezeth”** — the storm
**“it shall become like the tops of thistles”** — the very sharp thorns of the vices
43.20:
**“The cold … wind”** — the devil
**“north”** — the storm
**“bloweth”** — by suggesting
**“and … is congealed”** — little by little, with the cold of faithlessness
**“the water … into crystal”** — the hardened sinner; whence: “The waters are hardened like a stone”
**“upon every gathering together of waters”** — of peoples
**“it shall rest”**
• these things were before the coming of Christ, when almost the whole world served idols
• delighted in evil
**“and shall clothe the waters as a breastplate”** — the devil has his soldiers against the soldiers of Christ
43.21:
**“And it shall devour the mountains”**
• as pleasant food
• the proud
**“and burn the wilderness”**
• in minds frozen with unbelief
• with the fire of greed
• the deserters of the truth
**“and consume all that is green”** — the greenness and bud of the virtues
**“as with fire”** — of the vices
43.22:
**“A present remedy of all”** — the salvation of the human race
**“is the speedy coming”** — namely, of the incarnation of Christ and his teaching of the grace from above
**“of a cloud”** — “the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud, and will enter into Egypt”
**“and a dew that meeteth it, by the heat”** — of the devil’s persecution
**“that cometh, shall overpower it”** — namely, he will humble the pride of the devil
43.23:
**“At … word”** — of the gospel
**“his … the wind is still”** — namely, persecution will be eased
**“and with his thought”** — with wisdom
**“he appeaseth the deep”** — namely, deep persecution
**“and the Lord hath planted islands therein”** — “All things were made by him”
43.24:
**“Let them that sail on the sea, tell the dangers thereof: and when we hear with our ears, we shall admire”** — or: we shall not admire
**“them that sail”** — Them that sail: literally, there are many dangers of the sea, and there the wonderful works of God in various beasts, as the writers on natural things have handed down. Whence: “So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms: there are creeping things without number,” etc. In the sea of this world too there are many monsters of demons and many of their snares.
43.25:
**“There are great”** — because he checks the waves and the monsters of demons
**“and wonderful works: a variety of beasts, and of all living things, and the monstrous creatures of whales”** — “Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee.”
43.26:
**“Through him”** — Christ
**“is established”** — completed
**“the end of their journey”** — the order of passing things and the end of the age; for he is the beginning and the end
43.27:
**“We shall say much, and yet shall want words: but the sum of our words is, He is all”** — the perfection, as he is also the maker of our nature
**“We shall say much”** — We shall say much: all eloquence fails in comparison with him, and is not enough to tell his power.
43.28:
**“What shall we be able to do to glorify him?”** — what can a bodily creature avail to discuss the incomprehensible God?
**“for the Almighty himself is above all his works”** — in whose ordering all things are set
43.29: **“The Lord is terrible, and exceeding great”** — “the Lord is high, terrible … above all gods”
43.30:
**“Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can: for he is above all praise”**
• human
• “Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised”
**“When you exalt him put forth all your strength”** — with his work, that you may be able to praise
**“be not weary”** — Be not weary: in comprehending what is incomprehensible. Whence: seek not riches which you cannot reach.
43.31: **“Who shall see him, and declare him? and who shall magnify him”** — worthily
43.32: **“There are many things hidden from us that are greater than these: for we have seen but a few of his works”** — if we consider the whole
43.33:
**“But the Lord hath made all things”** — as if: yet we must confess these things
**“and to the godly”** — those who live religiously
**“he hath given wisdom”** — the knowledge of himself, as much as he knows to be useful

44.1:
**“Let us now praise”** — because more
**“men of renown, and our fathers in their generation”** — Let us now praise, etc. He has set out the mysteries of the divine sacrament by discussing morally and touching on allegory and anagogy in most places. Now he begins to tell of the holy fathers.
**“our fathers”** — Our fathers: the patriarchs, who enjoyed divine speech and vision, and the prophets, who, filled with the Holy Spirit, foretold many mysteries of Christ and the Church.
44.3: **“Such as have borne rule in their dominions, men of great power”** — because many of them were kings abounding in the riches of knowledge, but ruling themselves with a greater power
44.5: **“Such as by their skill sought out musical tunes, and published canticles of the scriptures”** — as David and those who sang psalmody with him
44.6: **“Rich men in virtue, studying beautifulness: living at peace in their houses”** — as Moses and Solomon, who built the tabernacle and the temple in varied colour
44.7: **“All these have gained glory in their generations, and were praised in their days”** — they will be honoured by their subjects for the merit of prudence and virtue
44.8:
**“They that were born of them”** — namely, instructed by their example
**“have left a name behind them, that their praises might be related”** — they celebrated their praises in voice and action together
44.9:
**“And there are some”** — namely, the wicked and sinners
**“of whom there is no memorial”** — namely, not of the good but of the wicked; whence: “their memory hath perished with a noise”
**“who are perished, as if they had never been: and are become as if they had never been born, and their children with them”** — namely, their works, the sins, are in eternal damnation
44.10:
**“But these were men of mercy”** — who merited the mercy of God
**“whose godly deeds”** — godly actions
**“have not failed”** — in the repayment
44.11:
**“Good things continue with their seed”** — for the worshippers of God, who lived religiously as their grandchildren and heirs
**“in the covenants”** — In the covenants: these things, according to the histories, are taken of the patriarchs and prophets, whose seed, that is, the Israelites, were often delivered from distress for their merits and the promises; whence Moses, praying for the sins of the people, recalls Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to memory, that God, appeased by their merits, might grant pardon to the sinning children. The merit of their father David also kept the kingdom for his sons for a long time. But in the sacred sense the men of mercy are the apostles and preachers of the New Testament, who by the word of the gospel and the mystery of baptism daily beget children of God, who, imitators of their parents, follow their examples; whose bodies rest in the hope of the resurrection, when the seed of good works will be repaid with a heavenly reward.
44.14:
**“Their bodies are buried in peace”** — namely, resting, they await the day of resurrection and everlasting glory
**“and their name liveth unto generation and generation”** — lasting among those who come after
44.15:
**“The wisdom”** — praiseworthy
**“Let the people shew forth their”** — their successors
44.16:
**“Henoch pleased”** — Henoch pleased: he did not begin to count the fathers from Adam, who transgressed and was cast out of paradise, but from Henoch, who walked with God and was translated into paradise; because in this the election of the saints is plain, who are carried from the hardship of the world to the rest of the kingdom. So it is believed that he will come at the end of the world to give men the counsel of repentance.
**“Henoch pleased God, and was translated into paradise, that he may give repentance to the nations”** — And was translated, etc. When the world perished in the flood, he was kept to preach repentance to the nations and to show by his example that those who devoutly serve God are freed from eternal destruction. With him the Lord made a covenant that he would no more destroy all flesh with the waters of a flood. It signifies the rulers who, among the waves of the world, steer the ark, that is, the Church, and preach the baptism of repentance, appeasing God for the human race with prayers and sacrifices.
44.17: **“Noe was found perfect, just”** — “in his generations”
44.19:
**“Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations”** — that is, the father of many (understand: nations), namely of those who believe in Christ; because “they who are the children of the flesh … are … not accounted for the seed”
**“and there was not found the like to him in glory”** — because he was the greatest in his time
44.20:
**“who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him”** — because it was promised him that in his seed all nations would be blessed
**“In his flesh he established the covenant, and in temptation he was found faithful”** — when he was commanded to sacrifice his son
