The mass of lead is put into the woman’s mouth, because the wickedness of avarice is weighed down by the weight of its own sin.
5.6:
**“And I said: What is it? And he said: This is a vessel”** — or: a measure
**“going forth”** — by this vessel I show you the sins of the people
**“And he said: This is their eye”** — the Septuagint: iniquity
**“This is a vessel”** — The vessel, or measure, was carried in the air, and the angel himself gave it a name. This is the eye, that is, the showing of all sins; and behold a woman sitting in the midst of the vessel, or measure, who is wickedness. And as he saw these things, behold a mass of lead like a stone was carried, either by its own force, or by God’s command, or by another whose name is not told. And the angel who spoke in the prophet, going out from him, showed him everything; he cast the woman headlong into the midst of the vessel, she who before was carried freely and, sitting on the vessel, was visible to all; and lest she raise her head again and rejoice in her wickedness, he puts the talent of lead like a stone into the mouth of the vessel, crushing wickedness and shutting it in so that it cannot break out.
5.7: **“And behold a talent of lead was carried, and behold a woman sitting in the midst of the vessel”** — the angel
5.8:
**“This is wickedness. And he cast her into the midst of the vessel, and cast the weight of lead”** — where and by whom it is carried, once shut in, the following passage teaches
**“upon the mouth thereof”** — of the vessel
5.9:
**“and behold there came out two women”** — By the two women the Jews interpret the kingdoms of the Medes and of the Macedonians, both of which afflicted the Babylonian people, and there their wickedness set up its seat. They invent this so that what was said of them may not be understood of them.
**“And I lifted up my eyes and looked: and behold there came out two women, and wind was in their wings, and they had wings like the wings of a kite: and they lifted up the vessel between the earth and the heaven”** — The two women who go out of their land are Juda: the ten tribes that were taken by the Assyrians, and the two that were taken by the Chaldeans. In their wings was wind, that is, the power of the devil; snatched away by the evil spirit as if by wind and breath, they were carried in swift flight. The kite is a most rapacious bird, by which is meant the devil, to whose power Juda and Israel are handed over to be led by him into captivity. And those women carried the vessel, or measure, in which wickedness was held shut, pressed down under the mass of lead, through the air between heaven and earth. The prophet, taught above about the vessel, does not ask what they carry, seeing the vessel borne, but whither they carry it; and the angel answers: That a house may be built for it in the land of Sennaar. Sennaar is the plain of the Chaldeans, where Babylon was built. So these women carry wickedness into Babylon, that a sure house may be built for it there. For truly in Babylon is the sure seat of wickedness.
**“two women”** — GREGORY. What else do we take in these two women but the two chief vices, namely pride and vainglory, which are without any doubt joined to wickedness? And they are said to have wind in their wings, because in their actions they serve the will of Satan. They call him a spirit, of whom it is said in the gospel, when “the spirit is gone out of a man”. And they had wings like the wings of a kite. The kite is always eager to snatch chickens. So these women have wings like the wings of a kite, because their actions are without doubt like the devil, for they always lie in wait to snatch the little ones. And they lifted up the vessel between the earth, and so on. Pride and vainglory have this proper to them, that they lift above the rest the one they have infected in his thinking, and, now by the craving for things, now by the desire for dignities, raise to the height of honour the one they have once caught and hold. But he who is between heaven and earth both forsakes the depths and in no way reaches the heights. These women, namely pride and vainglory, so lift up the captured mind that it forsakes any neighbours as if despising them, and seeks high things, glorying; so it can neither keep brotherly equality with its neighbours nor yet reach the heights. Sennaar is “their stench”: as “a good odour” comes from virtue, so on the contrary stench comes from vice. “For the desire of money is the root of all evils”; and because every evil is begotten through avarice, it is fitting that the house of avarice should be built in stench. Sennaar is a very wide valley, which was called Babylon for the confusion of minds and tongues; and because it is certain that all evils spring up through avarice and wickedness, rightly they are said to dwell in confusion.
5.11:
**“And he said to me: That a house may be built for it in the land of Sennaar”** — a shaking out of teeth
**“and that it may be established, and set there upon its own basis”** — that it may rest there in an everlasting abode

6.1:
**“And I turned”** — I passed to another vision
**“and lifted up”** — higher, to heaven
**“my eyes”** — of the heart
**“and saw: and behold four chariots came out from the midst of two mountains”** — what above he calls myrtle trees, shady, he here calls of brass
**“and the mountains”** — those
**“were mountains”** — which no age can wear away
**“of brass”** — were
6.2:
**“In the first chariot were red horses”** — they were bloody and murderous, and terrible with Babylonian cruelty
**“and in the second chariot black horses”** — the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, which, going forth by king Assuerus’s edict, carried the sad news of the death of all the Jews
6.3:
**“And in the third chariot white horses”** — the Macedonians, under whose king Antiochus we read of the victory of the Machabees
**“and in the fourth chariot grisled horses, and strong ones”** — the Roman kings, of whom some were merciful to the Jews, as Julius Caesar, others persecutors, as Vespasian
6.4: **“And I answered, and said to the angel that spoke in me: What are these, my lord?”** — What do they signify?
6.5:
**“And the angel answered, and said to me: These are the four winds of the heaven, which go forth to stand before the Lord of all the earth”**
• that is, the four quarters of the world, which stand by and obey the Lord; for these four kingdoms did nothing without God’s will
• Some say the four chariots are the four gospels, the horses the apostles: some of them red with martyrdom, some dark and black with the depth and knowledge of the mystery, some white with the grace of virginity, some grisled and strong, having the grace of healings and of various powers. These chariots are sent into the four quarters of the world to fulfil God’s will, and the angel says to them: Go, walk throughout the earth, sow the gospel in all the ends of the earth. Behold, they that go forth into the land of the north: the spirit of the Lord, or of the angels, is said to have rested, when in the land of the north the devil’s most stubborn kingdoms were overthrown by the apostolic preaching.
**“These are the four winds”** — Note that in the holy Scriptures the regions of the world are named according to the position of Jerusalem and the temple.
6.6:
**“That in which were the black horses went forth into the land of the north”** — That in which were the black horses went forth. What the first chariot, with the red horses, did is not said. For when the prophet was relating this, the kingdom of the Babylonians had already passed and the Medes held all Asia, under whose king Darius, in his second year, all the things we have set out above were seen. So the black horses went forth into the land of the north, namely to overthrow the kingdom of the Chaldeans.
**“and the white went forth after them: and the grisled went forth to the land of the south”** — that is, the Romans, strong and sturdy, went forth to the southern quarter and laid waste the whole land with swift onslaught
**“and the grisled went forth”** — The kings of the Macedonians follow in the footsteps of the Medes; and as the Medes subdued the Chaldeans, so the Macedonians subdued the Medes and Persians and Chaldeans.
6.7:
**“And they that were most strong, went out, and sought to go, and to run to and fro”** — otherwise: to run to and fro
**“through all the earth. And he said: Go”** — the angel who spoke in me cries to the Roman empire
**“walk throughout the earth: and they walked throughout the earth”** — lay all things under your feet
6.8: **“Behold they that go forth”** — The Hebrews hand down that the white horses, that is, Alexander and the Macedonians, who went forth after the Medes into the land of the north, made the prophetic spirit rest in the land of the north, because they fulfilled God’s will against the Medes, and in a short time the empire of the Medes and Persians was wiped out by the Macedonians. For it is a great comfort to those who are oppressed if they know their enemies will soon perish.
6.10:
**“Take”** — Take the gifts they offer, gold and silver.
**“of them of the captivity”** — from those who returned from the captivity, namely from Holdai and from the others
**“of Holdai”** — entreaty of the Lord
**“and of Tobias, and of Idaias; thou shalt come in that day, and shalt go into the house of Josias, the son of Sophonias, who came out of Babylon”**
• who was keeper and warden of the temple of the Lord, and there the crowns will rest in an everlasting place
• Holdai: entreaty of the Lord. Tobias: good of the Lord. Idaias: known of the Lord. For Holdai, Helem, that is, a dream, will be set afterwards, and in the fourth place Hem, that is, grace, will be added. The captivity of the Jews, that is, of the people that confesses God, is vices and sins. Those who repent return to Jerusalem, that is, the Church; by these, who entreat God in penance and are well pleasing to God, and known, that is, approved, by God, gold and silver are offered, of which crowns are made in the house of Josias, who is called “saved”, and is the son of Sophonias, that is, of the visitation of the Lord, because he who had been sick before is visited by the Lord and saved. These crowns are set on Jesus, that is, Christ, who is crowned in his members as they return; who is the son of Josedec, which is interpreted “Lord of justice”, because Christ “renders to every man according to his works”. To him it is said: Behold a man, the Orient is his name. We do not divide Jesus, nor make two persons of one; but he who is called Jesus because he saves is himself the Orient, because in his days justice arose. Under this Orient a multitude of believers will spring up, which will build the Church for God; and he, crowned in each of his members, will bear their glory; and he, king and high priest, will sit on a throne both royal and priestly, and “the counsel of peace shall be between them both”, because both glories will agree in the Lord Jesus. After Christ is crowned, a crown is promised also to those who dream of him, “through a glass in a dark manner”, and to whom the Lord is good, and who are known by God and, filled with his grace, are visited by him; and those who once groaned in Babylon, far from Judea, will build the house of God by their several advances, and all with one mind will know that God sent the prophet to them.
6.11:
**“And thou shalt take gold and silver: and shalt make”** — in the house of Josias
**“crowns”** — not one but two, distinguished by the difference of gold and silver
**“and thou shalt set them”** — one of them
6.12:
**“And thou shalt speak to him, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME”** — that is, Zorobabel, who is called the Orient because from a lowly captive he will rise to be leader of the people
**“and under him shall he spring up”** — a multitude of the faithful
6.13:
**“and he”** — after the temple is built
**“shall bear the glory”** — the other crown
**“and shall sit, and rule”** — with the power of a prince
**“upon his throne: and he shall be a priest upon his throne”** — but Jesus son of Josedec too will sit upon the priestly seat
**“and the counsel of peace”** — with minds and counsels joined they will govern the people of God
**“shall be between them both”** — who came down from the royal and from the levitical tribe
6.14:
**“And the crowns shall be to Helem”**
• otherwise: Heleti
• Helem is put for Holdai
• The crowns, first set on the heads of the two, will be consecrated in God’s temple with the names of those by whom they were offered, for an everlasting memorial; and then nations from the whole world that are set far off will come and build in the temple of the Lord, each according to his strength.
**“the crowns shall be”** — The Hebrews say that Ananias, Azarias and Misael, returning from captivity, brought gold and silver as gifts for the temple, and crowns for the high priest and the leader; and that Hem, whom he had not named above, that is, “grace”, namely Daniel, came with a gift; and that Helem is put for Holdai so that by the meaning of the name, which is “dream”, it may be shown that Daniel, set in captivity, and the three children knew the mysteries of the king’s dream. For Daniel himself and the three children prayed to the Lord, and so Daniel obtained the interpretation of the dream.
**“and Tobias, and Idaias”** — known of the Lord
**“and to Hem”**
• grace
• here a fourth is added, whereas he set only three
**“the son of Sophonias”**
• visitation of the Lord
• and this shall be
**“a memorial”** — for ever
6.15:
**“And they that are far off”** — from God through sins
**“shall come and shall build in the temple of the Lord”** — where God dwells
**“and you shall know that the Lord of hosts sent me to you”** — and then from the outcome and prosperity of events you will know that I foretold everything at the Lord’s command
**“But this shall come to pass, if hearing you will hear the voice of the Lord your God”** — all these things will come to pass if you obey the Lord’s commandments

7.1: **“And it came to pass in the … year”** — The Hebrews suppose that Sarasar and Rogommelech and the others who were with them were Persians and captains of king Darius who feared God; who, hearing that the temple had been built, asked through envoys of the priests and prophets whether, according to the former custom, in the fifth month, in which Jerusalem was overthrown by Nabuchodonosor, the reason for fasting and weeping still lasted, now that Jerusalem had been restored, or whether rather, because of the restoration, they should change sorrow into joy; so that the Persians who feared God, as they had wept with the weeping Jews, might rejoice with them as they rejoiced. And after the envoys’ inquiry was finished, the word of God comes to Zacharias, commanding him to tell the people and the priests what they ought to answer the envoys.
7.2: **“When Sarasar, and Rogommelech, and the men that were with him, sent to the house of God, to entreat the face of the Lord”** — that is, to the temple, which had now been restored
7.3:
**“To speak to the priests”** — to inquire of the priests
**“of the house of the Lord of hosts, and to the prophets, saying”** — now that Jerusalem has been restored
**“Must I weep”** — in memory of the destruction
**“in the fifth month”** — which is called July
**“or must I sanctify myself as I have now done for many years?”** — weeping and fasting are called sanctification, because those healed through abstinence are sanctified
7.5:
**“Speak”** — you, the prophet, in my person
**“to all the people of the land”** — which fasts or eats with an earthly affection
**“and to the priests, saying: When you fasted”** — abstained from food
**“and mourned”** — with outward mourning, having lost temporal gladness
**“in the fifth”** — when Jerusalem was taken
**“and the seventh month”** — when Godolias was slain by Ismahel
**“for these seventy years”** — of the desolation of the temple and the overthrow of Jerusalem
**“did you keep a fast unto me?”** — did your fasting profit me at all?
7.6:
**“And when you did eat and drink”** — and on the other hand, if ever you ate or fed
**“did you not eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?”** — not for me; for God is not appeased by these things, but by good works, for “meat doth not commend us to God”, but let us do the commandments
7.7:
**“Are not these the words which the Lord spoke by the hand of the former prophets”** — as if to say: I do not change my sentence; what I said while Jerusalem still stood, I say after it is rebuilt
**“Are not these”** — As if to say: why do you ask with such scrupulousness when you ought to fast and mourn, when I have already commanded through Isaias and the other prophets that at all times one must fast from evils and be diligent in works of mercy?
**“when Jerusalem as yet was inhabited, and was wealthy, both itself and the cities round about it, and there were inhabitants towards the south”** — in the hill country
7.9:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: Judge ye true judgment”**
• lest it be thrown in your face: how long will you judge unjustly?
• These things I wanted more, these I sought, these make a fast commendable; for not doing these you were handed over to captivity. I do not seek the fast of desolation and death of the fifth and seventh months.
**“Judge ye true judgment”** — Moses: “You shall judge the great as the small, and you shall not respect any man’s person, nor have pity on the poor in judgment, because it is the judgment of God.”
**“and shew ye mercy and compassion every man to his brother”** — after the truth of judgement let clemency follow towards all, above all towards brothers, whether of the same blood or of the same faith
7.10:
**“And … the widow, and the fatherless”** — whose care is entrusted to you by God
**“and the stranger, and the poor”** — one is made lowly by wandering, the other by want
**“oppress not … and let not a man … evil … against his brother”** — every man is a brother, for all are from one father
**“devise”** — much less do it
7.11:
**“But they would not hearken”**
• when I had commanded these things, they would not hearken
• These things can be referred to those in the Church who will not hear God, but harden their heart; and so, offending in the Church, they are cast out of the land of confession, and the indignation of God comes upon them, and they are scattered through all the kingdoms of the vices; and their land is made desolate, either the soul or the body, not having God for its dweller nor the spirit returning into it; and the land once delightful, which was the lodging of the Trinity, is turned into a wilderness and a dwelling of dragons.
**“and they turned away the shoulder to depart”** — spurning my commands by the bearing of their body
**“and … ears”** — of the heart
**“their”** — not God’s
**“they stopped”** — with a burden
**“not to hear”**
• God commanding
• “like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears”
7.12:
**“And they made their heart”** — of their own will
**“as”** — as it were
**“the adamant stone”** — a hard stone
**“as the adamant stone”** — Adamant is a very strong stone, which breaks all metals and is broken by none; whence it is called “untameable”.
**“lest they should hear the law, and the words which the Lord of hosts sent in his spirit by the hand of the former prophets”** — Isaias, Osee, who had clean hands
**“And”** — therefore
**“a great indignation came”** — for great sins
7.13:
**“And it came to pass”** — the words of the Lord were fulfilled, paying like for like: as they walked perversely towards him, so he would walk perversely towards them
**“that as he spoke”** — the Lord, threatening beforehand
**“and they heard not”** — me
**“so shall they cry”** — to me
**“and I will not hear, saith the Lord of hosts”** — them
7.14:
**“And”** — nay rather
**“I dispersed them throughout all kingdoms”** — of the Assyrians, Medes, Chaldeans, Persians and others
**“which they know not: and the land was left desolate”** — all Judea
**“behind them”**
• from their dwellings
• kingdoms
**“so that no man passed through or returned: and they changed the delightful land into a wilderness”** — the land which, compared with others, flowed with milk and honey for its great abundance, they turned into a wilderness

8.1: **“And the word … came”** — The people of Israel committed fornication in captivity with the Assyrians and Chaldeans; but after it was mocked by its lovers and stripped of its former beauty, remembering its former happiness it says: “I will return to my first husband”; and he, taking her back in marriage, says: I have been jealous.
8.2:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I have been jealous for Sion with a great jealousy”** — I afflicted the Jews who forsook me and worshipped idols
**“I have been jealous”** — The more I was angered before, because, defiled by many lovers, she stained my bed, the more now am I jealous for her, because she has done penance and built the temple in which I will dwell in her midst.
**“and with a great indignation”** — because their sins were great
**“have I been jealous for her”**
• because, prostituted with many lovers, she stained my bed
• but
8.3:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts”**
• because she repented
• but
**“I am returned to Sion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem”** — in the temple that has been built
**“and Jerusalem shall be called The city of truth”** — which before was a city of lies
**“and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, The sanctified mountain”** — on which victims are offered and the order of the ceremonies kept
**“I am returned”** — By Sion and Jerusalem are taken the souls of the faithful, watching for God and seeing peace; when they sin God is angry with them, handing them over to captivity, so that they may feel God through evils whom they had not felt through prosperity and good things. And when they have done penance the Lord will return to them, and in those in which the lies of the vices reigned before, Christ, the truth, will dwell, and they will be called the mountain of the house of the Lord.
8.4: **“There shall yet … dwell”** — So great will be the prosperity of all things that, no enemy remaining, both sexes will reach extreme age and hold up their trembling limbs with a staff to guide them. The streets of Jerusalem, that is, of the Church, are the virtues, in which dwell old men, not in age but “whose understanding is grey hairs”. These also have staffs in their hands, that is, correction, saying to their disciples: “What will you? shall I come to you with a rod, or in the spirit of meekness?” And with the old men will dwell old women, of whom Paul says: “Honour widows that are widows indeed.” The city will be filled also with boys and girls playing, whom the psalmist exhorts to sing to the Lord, saying: “Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger praise the name of the Lord.”
8.5:
**“And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls”** — in the peace of cities it is usual for playful youth to celebrate its joys with games and dances
**“playing in the streets thereof”** — showing the gladness of the mind by the bearing of the body
8.6:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: If it seem hard”**
• by those who see the city utterly destroyed
• and what I promise is as if impossible
• When he had prophesied so great a happiness to the remnant of the people who had come from captivity, it seemed incredible. Against which the prophet says: The answers I give are not mine, nor do I use my own voice; the promises I repeat are God’s.
**“If it seem”** — When, in the time of persecution, the meeting places of the Christians were destroyed, the islands filled with the exiles of the faithful, the divine books burned, who then would have believed that churches would be built by the very men who destroyed them?
**“in the eyes of the remnant of this people”** — faint-hearted
**“in those days”** — when Jerusalem has been built and rejoices
**“shall it be hard in my eyes, saith the Lord of hosts?”** — I who promise with my own mouth, to whom nothing is impossible
8.7:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Behold I will save my people from the land of the east”**
• “Many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.”
• We can say these things were fulfilled in part in the time of Zorobabel, when, the people being brought back under the figure of what was to come, God dwelt in Jerusalem. Whence it was called the people of God, and the Lord was called their God, not in falsehood and iniquity, but in truth and justice. And they are fulfilled above all in the Church under Christ, when “many come from the east and the west, and sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven”, and, the shadow of the old law departing, the truth of the gospel and the justice of Christ are made known.
**“Behold I will save”** — Some of the Jews say these things were fulfilled under Zorobabel and Nehemias, when the temple was built and the walls of the city put up, and the state of the Jewish people restored by the Machabees and the various princes who ruled Judea until Herod. Others refer them to the consummation of the world, and say they are to be fulfilled under the Christ for whom they wait in vain.
8.8:
**“And I will bring them”** — “There shall come out of Sion he that shall deliver and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.”
**“and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem”** — of the Church
**“and they shall be my people”** — obedient
**“and I will be their”** — “There shall be one fold and one shepherd.”
**“God”** — protector
8.9:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Let your hands be strengthened”**
• for the rest
• It is said to the Church: Let your hands be strengthened by good works, on which the house of God is founded, when the foundations of faith are laid and the temple built, when the multitude of the faithful is strengthened and so lives as to deserve to be God’s temple. But before this building, whatever good work they seemed to have, whether men, that is, the rational, or beasts, that is, the simple, they gained no reward from it with God; but there were wars and discords and tribulation among them; brother supplanted brother, and “a man’s enemies shall be they of his own household”, because they lacked the peace which Christ, going to the Father, left to the apostles. Whatever good work a Jew or a heretic or a Gentile does without faith in Christ, he does without reward; but once faith in Christ is received, those who were held captive in the world for their sins and burned with the Babylonian fire now have the fruit of the vine which says: “I am the true vine.” For them the earth gives its fruit, so that “they that sow in tears shall reap in joy”; and “the heavens, which shew forth the glory of God”, will give the dew of the divine word; and the remnant of the people, which the Lord of Sabaoth has left us, will have all these things, that is, peace and the abundance of the land.
**“Let your hands be strengthened”** — Since Aggeus and Zacharias had already exhorted the people to build, and now, following their admonition, the temple has been built, they now exhort both the leaders and the people again, that, having found the truth in what they had heard before, they may now also give credit to what is now promised, and not fear the onslaught of the Medes nor the plots of the surrounding nations that wish to hinder them; but let them be strengthened by the mouth of the prophets, from the day when the foundations of the temple were laid to the day when the temple was built upon them, and let them hear what follows.
**“you that hear in these days”** — in the fourth year of Darius, on the fourth day of the month called Casleu
**“these words”** — about the promise of things to come
**“by the mouth of the prophets”** — who began to speak from the day on which the house of God began to be founded
**“in the day that the house of the Lord of hosts was founded, that the temple might be built”**
• who prophesied that the temple should be built
• you ought to hear, because
8.10:
**“For”** — surely
**“before those days there was no hire for men, neither was there hire for beasts”** — Before the house of God was built all your labour was in vain, and both men and beasts were frustrated in various works by fruitless efforts; outside, adversaries, at home, sedition; brother lay in wait for brother; by all these things peace was broken
**“neither was there peace to him that came in, nor to him that went out, because of the tribulation”** — all were at odds with one another in hostile hatred
8.11:
**“But now”** — because the foundations of the house of the Lord have now been laid and the temple built
**“I will not deal with the remnant of this people according to the former days, saith the Lord of hosts”** — returned from the captivity of Babylon
8.12:
**“But there shall be the seed of peace”** — Christ
**“the vine”** — which before was barren
**“shall yield her fruit”**
• future abundance will make up for the drought and famine of the former time
• the salvation of the human race
**“and the earth”** — which before took away
**“shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew”**
• against the former drought
• all things will sprout by the watering of the rains and the night’s dew
**“to possess”** — for the building
**“and I will cause the remnant of this people … all these things”** — which I have spoken of
8.13:
**“And it shall come to pass, that as you were a curse among the Gentiles, O house of Juda”**
• O two tribes
• In the time of persecution the Christians are a curse and an example to the nations round about, because they have offended against their God; but afterwards, when peace is restored, they are a blessing, because God has mercy on Jerusalem, that is, the vision of peace, and on Juda, that is, those who confess faith in the Lord. Each of the believers too, who is handed over to Satan for his vices, will return to his former state when he has done penance, and will see the peace of God and possess the glory of his confession.
**“And it shall come to pass, that as you were”** — He promises what would come after the building of the temple: that as before they were a curse and a hissing among the nations, so, saved and returned to Judea, they will be a blessing.
**“and house of Israel”** — the ten tribes
**“so will I save you, and you shall be a blessing: fear not”** — the rebellious adversaries
**“let … be strengthened”** — by God’s promise
**“your hands”** — that they may finish the works they have begun
8.14:
**“For thus saith the Lord of hosts”** — who can fulfil what he promises
**“As I purposed to afflict you”**
• to hand you over to captivity
• I have purposed to do good; so that my sentence may stand, then, and my promise not be made void, do these things which I command.
**“As I purposed to”** — In anger he handed the twelve tribes over to captivity; turned to mercy, leaving Israel in captivity, he does good to Jerusalem and to the house of Juda.
8.15:
**“And I had no mercy”** — so that even so I might teach you
**“so turning again”** — in the present time
8.16:
**“These then are the things, which you shall do: Speak ye truth every one to his neighbour”** — every man is a neighbour
**“judge ye truth and judgment of peace in your gates”**
• where they sat to judge
• In precepts that belong to life and are plain we ought not to look for allegory, lest, as the comic poet says, we look for a knot in a bulrush.
**“truth and judgment”** — In judgement truth and justice come first; then mercy follows. For this is the judgement of peace: that the judge should have the purpose of making peace between those at odds.
8.17: **“And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his friend”** — he who is holy neither afflicts his friend nor plots malice against him in his heart
8.18:
**“And the word of the Lord … came”** — To what Sarasar and Rogommelech had asked above through envoys, whether they ought to fast and mourn in the fifth and seventh month, or, after the building of the temple, end the fast and lay aside mourning, after many things have been set in between which they ought to do and hope for, at last the prophet answers in the person of the Lord. The Jews hold that the fast of the fourth month, that is, July, is on the seventh day, and on the tenth of the same month, when Moses, coming down from the mountain, broke the tables of the law; and according to Jeremias the walls of the city were then first broken. In the fifth, that is, August, because of the spies of the holy land, sedition arose among the people, and they were commanded not to go up the mountain, but to go round for forty years at a long distance from the holy land, so that, except for the two, Josue and Caleb, all died in the wilderness. In this month too first Nabuchodonosor and afterwards Titus destroyed the temple in Jerusalem, and took the city of Bethel, to which many thousands of Jews had fled. The temple too was ploughed up by Titus Annius Rufus, to the shame of the oppressed nation. In the seventh, that is, October, Godolias was slain, and the remnant of the tribe of Juda and of Jerusalem was scattered. In the tenth, that is, January, Ezechiel, set in captivity, and the people of the captives heard that the temple had been overthrown in the fifth month. These are the reasons for the mourning and fasts which they have kept until now; but God promises that these days are to be turned into joy and solemnities, if they love peace and truth.
**“And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying”**
• The fast of the fourth and fifth, seventh and tenth month will be turned into solemnities, so much that the cities of Judea which were desert before will be thronged with many dwellers, and one city will go to another and they will exhort one another, saying: For seventy years Jerusalem was weighed down with mourning and bitterness; but now that peace is restored let us go to Jerusalem and offer victims according to the commandment of the law. And another city answers: I also will go. And then many peoples joined together, and nations without number and strong, will adore the Lord.
• Mystically, we fast when “the bridegroom shall be taken away from us” and we do not deserve his presence; but when he has returned and purposes to do good, sorrow is turned into joy, and the former famine of the word of God is made up for by the presence of his teaching and the fulness of the heavenly bread.
8.19:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts: The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall be”** — shall be turned
**“to the house of Juda, joy, and gladness, and great solemnities: only love ye truth and peace”** — this only God seeks
8.20:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts, until … come”** — from every side
**“until … come”** — What is said according to the letter of Jerusalem and Zorobabel is referred to Christ and the Church, to which peoples run together from the whole world to offer sacrifices to God in the temple; and in the time of persecution the masters of the Church promise the believers that the parishes will be built again, and peace restored, and the face of the Lord entreated.
**“people … and dwell in many cities”** — the churches, desolate before
8.21:
**“And the inhabitants go one to another, saying: Let us go”** — “He that heareth, let him say: Come.”
**“and entreat the face of the Lord”** — the Son, who is the image of the Father: “He that seeth me seeth the Father also.”
**“and let us seek the Lord of hosts”** — by working well
8.22:
**“And many peoples … shall come”** — by prayer, faith, work
**“and strong nations”** — as the martyrs
**“to seek”** — by offering sacrifice
**“the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the Lord”** — there is no place of true sacrifice outside the Church
8.23:
**“Thus saith the Lord of hosts”** — these things foretold will come to pass
**“In those days, wherein ten men of all languages of the Gentiles shall take hold, and shall hold fast the shirt of one that is a Jew”**
• Jesus, who was of Juda, and the apostles, who were of the Jews
• In those days, that is, at the coming of Christ, the ten men whom the Lord seeks in Sodom will take hold of Christ in the flesh, longing to cling to his footsteps, because God is with him. Or whoever believe from among the tongues and nations will take hold of the apostles, who are of the Jews, and will say: We will go with you, for we have heard through the prophets that Christ the Son of God is with you. What is read in Isaias, “Seven women shall take hold of one man”, that is, the churches of Christ, is signified in Zacharias by ten men. By seven is understood the Church full of the sevenfold grace, by ten the same Church, because it cleanses the five senses of the flesh and of the spirit, so as to go to meet Christ with the lamps of good works. For the letter iota, from which the Saviour’s name takes its beginning, signifies the number ten not only among the Greeks but also among the Hebrews. So those who are counted by the Christian name and cling to Christ are signified by the number ten.
• Some of the Jews say this was fulfilled under Zorobabel; others that it is to be fulfilled under their Christ, whom they await as one to come.
• Ten men, that is, the churches, which are compared to virgins, because they double the number five, and are holy in body and spirit; whoever also rules the senses of the body well in the present will receive ten cities in the future, the number doubled.
**“saying: We will go with you”** — to the heavenly homeland, “from virtue to virtue”
**“for we have heard”** — from the prophets
**“that God is with you”** — “I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world.”

9.1:
**“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land”** — is
**“of Hadrach, and”** — in the land
**“of Damascus the rest thereof”**
• namely
• The burden. The Septuagint: the taking up. This whole vision, or weight and burden of the word of God, belongs to the calling of the Gentiles and the building of the Church; and the order of the words is: this burden of the word of the Lord is in the land of Hadrach: “ad”, sharp, “rach”, soft. So it marks the word of the Lord as harsh to unbelievers, soft and merciful to the just taken up from Judea. Some refer Hadrach to the blinded Jews, Damascus to the Gentiles taken up. Upon Hadrach, then, is the burden of harshness; in Damascus the Lord’s merciful rest. For she who before her conversion is interpreted “drinking blood”, now turned to penance, is called the rest of the Lord. And so the temple will be built of both peoples, because whoever of the Gentiles or of the Jews looks to God and believes in him is the Lord’s.
**“for the eye of man … is the Lord’s”** — The Septuagint: For the Lord looks upon men and all the tribes of Israel; the Lord, who looks without respect of persons on both the faith of the Gentiles and the faithlessness of the Jews, laying the weight of sentence on the latter and resting in the faith of the believers.
9.2:
**“Emath”** — indignation
**“also in the borders”**
• shall be
• That this may be fulfilled: “The daughters of Tyre with gifts shall worship him.” And the woman of Chanaan came out of the borders of Tyre and Sidon to meet the Lord.
• The Jews say that all the peoples named here will serve their great king, the Christ they await, so that none will dare lift a hand against him, all round about being at peace.
**“Emath also”** — Emath is the same as Antioch, a city of Syria.
**“thereof”** — of Damascus or of the land of Hadrach, so that they may believe in the Lord the Saviour
**“and Tyre”** — distress
**“and Sidon”** — hunting
**“they have taken”** — because before they believed
**“to themselves to be … wise”** — worldly
**“for they have taken to themselves to be exceeding wise”** — So much that with sophistries and dialectical arguments they resisted the words of Christ, the true peacemaker; and they gathered silver, that is, the polish of eloquence, and gold, that is, the cunning of the senses, which are compared to dust and trodden mire, so as to hold firmly the kingdom of idolatry they had fortified. But they can do nothing against the truth, for behold the Lord possessed her, overthrowing every height that raises itself against the knowledge of God; and he will strike her in the most bitter sea of this world, so that nothing of her former wisdom and fear may remain in her, but she will be refined and cleansed by the fire which the Lord came to cast upon the earth.
9.3: **“And Tyre hath built herself a strong hold, and heaped together”** — otherwise: heaped together
9.5:
**“Ascalon shall see”**
• base fire, or weighed
• Ascalon, which before was base fire and had grown to the measure and weight of sins; and Gaza, which, strong and untameable, promised itself the empire of all; and Accaron, which was barren and without law, will see Emath and the other cities named above struck, and will grieve and be terrified, doing penance, because their hope will be destroyed; and there will be no king in Gaza, that is, Ascalon will have no inhabitants; and the divider will sit, that is, the Lord, who separates the grain from the chaff, in Azotus, where the fire which the Lord casts upon the earth begets those baptized in the Holy Spirit; where also is the cousin and uncle whom the bride desires in the Canticle; where also is the fire of the breast. Whence the Apostle: I gave you milk to drink, not meat. When these things are done, I will destroy the pride of the Philistines. Philistines are “falling by the cup”, who were drunk with the cup of Babylon; but at Christ’s coming, laying aside their pride, they will follow the humble Jesus; from whose mouth blood will be taken away, that is, words of blasphemy, and abominations, that is, the worship of idols and the eating of things offered to idols, from between their teeth; and when these are taken away, the people of the Philistines itself will be left to the Lord, so that, the Jews being rejected, it may itself be a governor in Juda, that is, in the people that confesses; and Accaron, once barren and rooted up, will be as a Jebusite, that is, Jerusalem: the same city is called by three names. And I will encompass, he says, my house, that is, I will fortify the Church, through those who serve me in war in various ministries, and run to and fro at my command; or I will fortify it with the help of angels. And the oppressor shall no more pass through them, that is, he who leads astray outside and drags the conquered into captivity. For now I have seen with my eyes, that is, through the prophets and saints I have seen the calling of the Gentiles and the safety of the Church.
**“and shall fear, and Gaza”** — strong, or empire
**“and shall be very sorrowful: and Accaron”** — barren, or rooted up
**“because her hope is confounded: and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ascalon shall not be inhabited”** — otherwise: And the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ascalon shall not be inhabited
9.6: **“And the divider shall sit in Azotus”** — Azotus: fire begetting, or fire of the uncle, or fire of the breast
9.7: **“And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth: and even he shall be left to our God, and he shall be as a governor in Juda, and Accaron as a Jebusite”** — trodden down
9.9:
**“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem”**
• rejoice, because by my working these evils are to cease in you
• Sion and Jerusalem are the same city, for Sion is the citadel in Jerusalem.
**“Rejoice greatly, O daughter”** — This was fulfilled when they went out to meet Christ with palm branches, crying: “Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest.”
**“BEHOLD THY KING”** — promised by the prophecies of all the prophets
**“will come to thee, the just”** — “The Lord is just, and hath loved justice: his countenance hath beheld righteousness.”
**“and saviour”** — Jesus
**“he is poor”** — though he was rich
**“and riding upon an ass”** — the people of the circumcision, pressed by the yoke of the law
**“and upon a colt the foal of an ass”** — the people of the Gentiles, governed by no law but dashed down the precipices of idolatry, but now, with the Lord seated on it, keeping a straight course
9.10:
**“And I will destroy the chariot out of Ephraim, and the horse out of Jerusalem, and the bow for war shall be broken”**
• that fiery darts may not be shot to strike the hearts of the pleasure-loving
• Ephraim is “fruitfulness”, and signifies the multitude of heretics, of whom it is said: “The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow are in the days of battle.” Of these too it is said: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will call upon the name of the Lord.” But their horse is deceitful; therefore it is scattered from Jerusalem and called to penance by those who say: “Do not become like the horse and the mule.”
• This is not to be watered down by allegory, but to be believed as truly fulfilled, according to that: “Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.”
**“And I will destroy”** — According to the letter God the Father promises that there will be no battles, all being at peace at the birth of Christ.
**“and he shall speak”** — the Son
**“peace”** — “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you.”
**“to the Gentiles, and his power shall be from sea to sea, and from the rivers”** — otherwise: the river
9.11:
**“Thou also”**
• O Christ, the Son
• After the Father has announced to Sion and Jerusalem the coming of Christ, that he would come meek and mighty, he turns to address Christ himself, of whom the prophecy is.
• The Jews say thus: O Christ, whom we await as one to come, who art to reign over all the earth: by the blood of thy testament, namely of the victims which by the precept of the law were commanded to be offered, in which law thou didst testify that good things would be given to thy sons, thou hast sent forth Israel thy people out of the pit of the captivity of the Chaldeans, among whom was no mercy. Therefore, O Israelites, who were prisoners and hoped in the Lord, return to the strongly fortified Jerusalem, for today you have the Lord promising you that for the brief wrong of the captivity you will receive all things double. Because I have bent Juda for me: this they refer to the times of the Machabees, who conquered the Macedonians and, after three years and a half, cleansed the temple defiled by idolatry. I have filled Ephraim as a bow: they think those are signified here who, of the ten tribes called Israel, came over under Ezechias, over whom Josias too is recorded to have reigned.
• At the resurrection of Christ the just, who were held bound in hell for Adam’s sin, rose and appeared to many in Jerusalem. As a sign of this pit, Joseph was sent by his brothers into a pit where there was no water; Daniel by the Chaldeans; Jeremias by the Jews; Banaias too, in a time of snow and cold, went down into a pit to kill lions there.
**“by the blood of thy testament”** — of thy passion, those who were held bound in the prisons of hell, in which there is no refreshing mercy, such as the rich man sought, thou hast freed by thy mercy
**“hast sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit”** — of this world
9.12:
**“Turn ye”** — therefore
**“to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”**
• again the word is directed to those who were prisoners and were to be freed by Christ’s mercy
• you who are now held in a terrible hell, who hope at Christ’s coming for the loosing of sins, return to the strong hold, that is, the dwelling of paradise, that for a brief tribulation you may receive eternal rewards
**“I will render thee double”** — In their own land they shall possess double things. And the Apostle: “The sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us.”
9.13:
**“Because I have bent Juda for me as a bow, I have filled Ephraim”**
• otherwise: because I have bent Juda for me as a bow, I have filled the land of Ephraim
• Because I have bent Juda. When Juda is bent as a bow, and the Gentiles and heretics slain by the sons of Sion, the glory of the Lord appears, and his dart goes forth as lightning. He is here called lightning and splendour and trumpet and clangour, by which ears deaf before are roused to hear; and he will go in the whirlwind of the south: he terrifies and threatens so that he may have mercy upon penance, and afterwards protects those he had terrified before.
**“Because I have bent”** — By Juda the Saviour, who is sent by the Father into the world, who is both the archer and the bow; whence: “Thy arrows are sharp, most mighty.” He is the arrow too; whence: “He hath made me as a chosen arrow: in his quiver he hath hidden me”, that is, the Word in the flesh. With this Ephraim is filled, so that, when he is armed for war, he himself is wounded with the Lord’s arrows along with the Gentiles. Of his tribe Jeroboam first divided the people, who signifies the heretics. And, O Sion, that is, the Church, I will raise up thy sons to keep watch over the Church, through whom the contrary teachings and the assertions of the Gentile philosophers will be destroyed, because the Lord himself is the sword of the mighty, by which wounded enemies become friends.
**“and I will raise up thy sons, O Sion”** — the catholics, who defend the Church
**“above thy sons, O Greece”** — the philosophers, masters of perverse teaching
**“and I will make thee”** — O son
9.14:
**“And the Lord God shall be seen over them, and … shall go forth as lightning”** — burning and shining
**“his dart … and the Lord God will sound the trumpet, and go in the whirlwind of the south”** — not of the north
**“and the Lord God will sound the trumpet”** — These things too the Jews refer to the times of the Machabees, in whose victories over Antiochus the battle and the victory were the Lord’s, whose might appeared like lightning, and who, the enemies being conquered and scattered like a whirlwind, protected the Jews.
9.15:
**“The Lord of hosts will protect them: and they shall devour”**
• the Hebrews: the Greeks
• The sons of Sion, that is, of grace, protected by their God, will devour their enemies, and will subdue them with the stones of the sling: with the threats of Scripture sent out by the whirl of the mouth they make the proud humble. And drinking they shall be inebriated as it were with wine: for love of eternal things they will forget earthly things and themselves. And that drunkenness will please God, like the sacrifice of the altar; and the Lord their God will save them in that day as the flock of his people, because the stones, that is, the saints, though heavy with the burden of the flesh, will be so lightened that they can be set on high in Christ’s building.
**“and they shall devour”** — The sons of Sion being protected, and the Lord terrifying the adversaries, so great will be the ruin of the Greeks that they will be overwhelmed not only by swords but by the throwing of stones, and will become the enemies’ prey.
**“and subdue”** — to servitude
**“with the stones of the sling: and drinking they shall be inebriated as it were with wine”** — the victors will fight like drunken men, with desperation
**“and they shall be filled as bowls”** — they will please the Lord as a libation upon the altar; for libations are poured on the altar from bowls
9.16:
**“And the Lord their God will save them in that day, as the flock of his people”** — he will not fight against the Macedonians as an armed host trained in the art of war, but will come like a flock ready for death, and with the Lord’s help will overcome
**“for holy stones shall be lifted up over his land”** — the saints, hard as stones yet trodden down, will be lifted up from their lowliness to be glorious in his land
9.17:
**“For what is the good thing of him”** — God’s
**“and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?”**
• that is, the law, which feeds the uninstructed and delights them, that by its authority they may worship the one God
• So the Machabees, with God’s help, will cast the Macedonians out of the land of Israel, that the temple may be cleansed and the precepts of the law kept, and the teaching of the Scriptures may again bring forth virgins, that is, a people believing in the one God, which before was defiled by the worship of idols.
**“the corn of the elect”** — The corn is the Saviour, because he is “the bread which came down from heaven” and strengthens the heart of the elect; he is drunk by those who are holy in body and spirit, who, brought into the cellar of wine, follow the Lamb with joy whithersoever he goeth.

10.1:
**“Ask ye of the Lord rain”**
• A great happiness is promised, which is seen to have been fulfilled in the time of the Machabees, when the law of Israel grew greater and the Lord granted all prosperity, the idols being destroyed and their priests proved false. Other Jews say these things are to be fulfilled in the time of their Christ.
• In the last time, when the world is already declining to its end, when the promises of the prophets ought now to be fulfilled, ask of God the Father rain, that is, Christ, by whose teaching hearts are nourished; and the Lord Christ himself, sent by the Father, will make snows to cool, and rain, that is, the abundance of the gospel shower, to water the dryness of the earth; through whom he will give to each of the faithful the grass of good work in the field of the world. And then those who believe in Christ, both of the Gentiles and of the Jews, will understand that they worshipped images in vain and heard the lies of diviners or dreamers in vain, and that therefore they were led by the devil into captivity and afflicted, not having God for their shepherd.
• It can be said that God exhorts those who believe in Christ to ask for rain at the consummation of the world, when the fulness of grace is to be given, because then all images are to be destroyed; which is understood also of the heretics and their teachings, who, though they have the name of Christ, yet have not Christ for shepherd, and so will be afflicted by the devil’s captivity.
**“in the latter season, and the Lord will make snows, and will give them showers of rain”** — so
10.2:
**“For the idols”** — the heretics who give heed
**“a lie, and the dreamers”** — otherwise: dreamers
**“have spoken vanity: they comforted in vain”** — they promised vain things
**“therefore they were led away”** — by the devil into the captivity of Babylon, as the devil’s flock
**“as a flock”** — like sheep they are laid in hell
**“they shall be afflicted, because they have no shepherd”** — who says: “I am the good shepherd.”
10.3:
**“My wrath is kindled against the shepherds”**
• Some Jews say these things are to be fulfilled at the coming of Christ; others say they were fulfilled in the time of the Machabees in this way. Through the fault of the priests that people had been handed over into the hands of persecutors; but afterwards God raised up Judas Machabeus and others, whom he made as the horse of his glory in the battle. Out of Juda himself, that is, of his stock, were leaders in the people, who were the corner, because they held the people together with kingly power; and were the pin, that is, priests fixed in the Lord’s temple; and the bow of battle, because they were the first to leap forward to battle. Out of him shall come forth every exacter together: there will be no rank in the army that is not ordered at his will; and these mighty men will tread down the Macedonians in battle like the mire of the ways; and they will be able to do this because the Lord will be with them.
• Ours refer these things to the times of persecution, because for the vices of the priests the people is often handed over to its adversaries; and yet afterwards God has mercy on the house of Juda, that is, those who confess God with mouth and heart, whom he makes horses to carry God against the enemy in battle, and angels, messengers of the divine will, and a pin, a pillar and a support in the house of God, through whom every rank in the Church too will be ordered; and in martyrdom they tread down the adversaries, saying: “I will not fear what man can do unto me.”
**“upon”** — or: to
**“the buck goats”**
• or: lambs
• who applauded the sins of the shepherds
• wanton and lustful
**“I will visit”** — I will punish
**“for … hath visited”** — afterwards, truly
10.5:
**“And they shall be as mighty men, treading under foot”**
• otherwise: treading
• When God visits the house of Juda, that is, the confessing Church, the pomp of the devil and the pride of this world are drowned in the Red Sea, which are dragged to the precipice by the four disturbances as by four wheels unless they are steered by a good charioteer. Then the Lord strengthens the house of Juda and the house of Joseph, so that those who were divided under the reign of Jeroboam may be joined in one flock under the rule of Christ.
**“And they shall be as mighty men”** — These things too the Jews say were done under the Machabees, or are to be fulfilled under the Christ: when Judas has so trodden down the adversaries, then all the cavalry of Greece will fall, and the house of Juda, that is, of the two tribes, and of Joseph, that is, of the ten, will return from the captivity in which they had been, and will be as before the captivity, because I will hear them when they pray; and Ephraim, who are now held captive, being afterwards released, will come to such gladness that you would think them soaked with wine; and their sons, seeing the triumphs of their fathers, will rejoice in the Lord, through whom they gained the victory.
10.6:
**“And I will strengthen the house of Juda”** — of Christ, who is of Juda
**“and save the house of Joseph”** — of Christ, who satisfied the world’s famine by his presence, as Joseph the famine of Egypt
**“and I will bring them back again”** — from captivity
**“because I will have mercy on them: and they shall be”** — one in faith
**“as they were when I had cast them off”** — all these things can be taken in the persecutions: when all, as it were, despair, God hears his servants
10.7:
**“And they shall be as the valiant men of Ephraim”** — who before were weak and feeble will bear fruit like the strong
**“and their heart shall rejoice as through wine”** — when they have drunk the wine of Sorec
**“and their children”** — their imitators
**“shall see, and shall rejoice, and their heart shall be joyful in the Lord”** — who supplies all good things
10.8:
**“I will whistle for them”**
• like a shepherd
• They will have as the sign of their gathering, whether under the Macedonians or at the consummation of the world, my whistle, by which I will show myself present to gather them.
• Allegorically. To those who were captive in their sins the Lord gives a sign in his clemency, that they may be gathered to him as to their redeemer, saying: “Take up my yoke upon you.” These he multiplies, not with a fleshly but with a spiritual blessing; these are sown among the peoples to whom it is said: “Going therefore, teach ye all nations”; and through these that are sown, peoples set far off by idolatry will remember the Lord, in whose sight “all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore”. And they shall live with their children, and shall return, so that those who were dead in unbelief before may live by faith; these are the children to whom Paul gave milk to drink. And I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt and from among the Assyrians: from the land in which king Pharao ruled, who said: “The rivers are mine, and I made them”; and in which land the king of Assyria ruled, that is, “great understanding”, namely the proud devil, who is also interpreted “accusing” or “convicting”. Such as these are led into the land of Galaad, that is, from fleshly to spiritual things; for Galaad is interpreted “witness of passing over”. And to Libanus, that is, “whitening”, that, led out of the darkness of the world, they may be made white. And then place is not found for them, because they will not be pressed by the narrowness of the earth, but will enjoy the breadth of heaven.
**“and I will gather … together”**
• from captivity
• to the faith
**“them”** — scattered
**“because I have redeemed them”**
• with the blood of the lamb
• with an outstretched arm
**“and I will multiply them as they were multiplied before”** — “So shall thy seed be, as the stars of heaven.”
10.9: **“And I will sow them among peoples”** — So that the scattering among peoples may not seem a dividing, but the work of sowing; and with the harvest of children multiplied they shall live with their children and shall return, not only from Egypt but from among the Assyrians, to Judea and Galaad and Libanus, places which the ten tribes had possessed before; and so great will be the number of those brought back that the land will not hold the multitude.
10.10: **“And I will bring them back out of the land of Egypt, and will gather them from among the Assyrians”** — otherwise: I will gather
10.11:
**“And he shall pass over the strait of the sea, and shall strike the waves in the sea”**
• the threats of the persecutor
• Allegorically. With the Lord going before, we pass over the strait of this world. Into this sea, where the saints are hemmed in, the apostles went down, and the Lord went down first to free us from the bitter waves; and when the strait is trodden, all the depths of the river shall be confounded, so that preaching in the rivers of the world they may pass over on foot; and, the devil humbled, his rule may depart from the saints; and the freed will be strengthened, and will glory in the Lord, saying: “God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.”
**“And he shall pass over the strait of the sea”** — The Hebrews say that the Jews were carried away by the Assyrians and Chaldeans not only to the Persians and Medes but also to the Bosphorus and the northern region, and were brought back or called back from there in part by God’s clemency. Whence he says: He shall pass over the strait of the sea, that is, the narrows of the Propontis, which divides Constantinople from Chalcedon; and the Lord, going before his people, will strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the river shall be confounded, as was done once at the river Jordan or the Red Sea; and so, their enemies humbled, they will glory in the land of Israel in the name of the Lord.
**“And”** — so
**“all the depths of the river shall be confounded, and”** — then
**“the pride of Assyria shall be humbled”** — of the devil
**“and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart”** — and so
10.12:
**“I will strengthen them”** — “The Lord is my strength and my praise.”
**“in the Lord”** — the Son
**“and … in … name”** — the Christian
**“they shall walk … his”**
• with the Lord, like Enoch
• “from virtue to virtue”

11.1:
**“Open … O Libanus”**
• that the Roman army may enter
• Having foretold the captivity of the people of Israel by the Assyrians and Babylonians, he added also the restoration of the temple and the happiness of the people that followed; now he passes to the things that were done by the Romans to the temple and Jerusalem, in vengeance for the blood of Christ. So by Libanus the temple is signified, which was opened that the Roman army might enter. By the names of the trees that follow, the princes and priests of that people are signified.
**“thy gates”** — the temple restored by Zorobabel
**“and let fire devour thy cedars”** — either fire will lay all waste, or the enemy’s onslaught will consume the leaders and priests
11.2:
**“Howl, thou fir tree”** — let the priests and princes mourn, lamenting one another
**“for the cedar is fallen, for the mighty are laid waste”** — what he had set down obscurely he explains more plainly
**“howl, ye oaks of Basan”** — of confusion and shame
**“because the fenced forest is cut down”** — because the temple, which had been built with impregnable strength, was destroyed by the Romans
11.3:
**“The voice of the howling of the shepherds”**
• is heard
• By another metaphor, those he had called mighty he now calls shepherds, that is, princes and teachers, whom he invites to mourning, because their glory is laid waste, that is, the temple, in which they gloried.
**“because their glory is laid waste”** — otherwise: glory
**“the voice of the roaring of the lions”** — those he first called trees, then shepherds, he now calls lions, who weep for the destruction of the temple, in which certain just and mighty men and warriors were nourished like lions
**“the voice of the roaring”** — As he compared the height of the temple, according to the lie of the land of Judea, to the height of Libanus, because in the land of promise there is nothing loftier or more wooded than Libanus, so to the Jordan, which is the greatest river in Judea, beside which lions dwell, he joins the roaring of lions, because of the heat of thirst or the nearness of the desert. Whence it is said: “The lion is come up from Jordan”, that is, Nabuchodonosor, against Jerusalem from his seat, like a lion from his lair. So the voice of lions, that is, of the roaring Romans, is heard against Jerusalem.
**“because the pride of the Jordan is spoiled”** — of the running water
11.4:
**“Thus saith the Lord my God: Feed”**
• O Zacharias
• Whatever teachers, whether in the Old Testament or in the New, act carelessly and scandalize the least, feed the flock of slaughter, and have no pity on them, but sell those entrusted to them, and gain riches from the deaths of others, praising those who make plunder and blessing the wretched and the wicked.
• No wonder if the enemies slew and sold them, when their own shepherds did not spare them, and for their fault the flock was handed over to wolves.
**“Thus saith the Lord”** — Because Libanus is opened and all the pride of the Jordan laid waste, therefore thus saith the Lord my God: Feed the flock of the slaughter, that is, let it be fed and grow meanwhile for now, because afterwards it is to be slain by the enemy like sheep and cattle.
11.5:
**“Which they that”** — the Romans
**“possessed”** — by right of victory
**“slew”** — mercilessly
**“and repented not”** — for such great cruelty
**“and they sold them”** — some they kept, not for clemency but for the price
**“saying: Blessed be the Lord, we are become rich”** — this the Romans said: the Jews offended God by their sins, therefore we have crushed them, and are made rich by their price
11.6:
**“And I will no more spare the inhabitants of the land, saith the Lord”** — because their shepherds did not spare them, therefore I too will not spare the inhabitants of Judea
**“behold I will deliver”**
• After the overthrow of the temple, which happened because they would not repent for forty-two years, they were delivered every one into his neighbour’s hand, because they butchered one another in mutual slaughter.
• When Jerusalem was besieged by the Romans there were such wars and civil discords among the Jews themselves that the people was divided into three parts, as is read in the histories.
**“and they shall destroy the land, and I will not deliver it out of their hand”** — And they shall destroy, that is, the Romans will destroy the whole land and all the cities of the Jews, and I will not deliver them out of the hand of the Romans, but they will be weighed down under them in everlasting captivity. And I will feed the flock of slaughter, so that the Jews may always be fed for death. For the sentence is the Lord’s. O ye poor, that is, the just of Israel who have received the Son of God, hear what is said, and learn the sacraments of the following chapter.
11.7:
**“And I will feed the flock of slaughter for this, O ye poor of the flock. And I took unto me two rods”** — for ruling
**“And I took unto me”**
• Because above he had spoken of the irreparable laying waste of the temple and Jerusalem, and because this could seem to be said only of the Jewish people, which, after slaying the prophets, killed even the Son of God himself, saying, “His blood be upon us and upon our children”, now the creator of all things sets out the mysteries of his world, saying that he had two rods, and with them fed the people bound to him.
• The creator, to show the bearing of a shepherd, took two rods, or staffs. One he called Beauty, that is, the whole human race, which, when the world was restored under Noe, he protected with his blessing before it was soiled with sins. And so the calling of all nations is called beautiful, because nothing is more just than that all should call equally on the father of all, being begotten by him. And the other I called a Cord: when the bounds of the nations were set according to the number of the angels of God, “Jacob was the people of God, and the cord of his inheritance”. And I fed the flock of Israel, and with Israel the whole human race. And I cut off, and so on, three shepherds: Moses and Aaron and Mary; of whom Mary died in the first month, which is called Nisan, in the desert of Sin; and in the same place and the same month, because of the water of contradiction, Moses and Aaron were condemned not to enter the land of promise; so it came about that of the tribe of Juda one was cut off by present death, two by the sentence of future death. And my soul was straitened in their regard, over the three shepherds whom I had set over my flock; for their soul also varied in my regard, because they did not glorify me at the water of contradiction. Or the people fought against me in various ways, wavering this way and that between me and idols. Therefore in indignation I said to Moses: “I will not feed you”; but that which dieth, let it die, and that which is cut off, let it be cut off. Let the bodies of all fall in the wilderness, and, turned to sedition, let them tear one another with mutual bites like beasts, and let none enter the land of promise.
**“one I called Beauty”** — the human race
**“and the other I called a Cord”** — namely the Jews
11.10:
**“And I took my rod”** — When Israel, which is the Lord’s cord, was taken up, the nations of the whole world, separated from the worship of God, worshipped idols.
**“that was called Beauty, and I cut it asunder to make void my covenant, which I had made with all people”** — he explains what he meant by the rod Beauty, namely all the nations, which are cast off by God
11.11:
**“And it was made void in that day”** — when Israel was taken up
**“and so the poor of the flock … understood”** — the people of Israel
**“that keep for me”** — my commandments, for my honour
**“that it is the word of the Lord”** — it is God’s will to cast off the nations that deny him and to take up, in Abraham, Israel that confesses him
11.12:
**“And I said to them: If it be good”** — if it please your free will
**“in your eyes, bring hither my wages”**
• because I have taken you, few as you are, and cast off the nations, keep my commandments
• if you will not pay the wages, nor be counted by my name, refuse openly; do what you will
**“and if not, be quiet. And they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver”** — those who said, “All that God hath commanded we will do”, afterwards gave thirty pieces of silver to Judas the traitor for my blood
**“And they weighed”** — The Jews maliciously interpret the thirty pieces of silver as the thirty commandments of the law which they were bidden to do, and again thirty-six others that were forbidden; and they are told to render the silver of the Lord’s commandments to their God, the potter and maker; and because they would not do it they were cast off.
11.13:
**“And the Lord said to me”** — the Father to the Son, or God to the prophet
**“Cast”** — he does not say “put it down” but “cast it”, that the Lord’s wages may be weighed by the potter’s judgement
**“it to the statuary”** — others: to the smelter
**“a handsome price, that I was prized at by them. And”** — the Lord says through the prophet
**“I took the thirty pieces of silver”** — as I had been commanded
**“and I cast them into the house of the Lord to the statuary”**
• “Casting down the pieces of silver in the temple, he went and hanged himself with an halter.”
• To the statuary, that is, to the caster of statues, whom others call the moulder, that is, the fashioner or potter, where the creator of all may judge of the price, which he calls theirs ironically, as if to say: the people I chose for sons judged me fit to be sold and bought at so cheap a price.
**“Cast it to the statuary”** — Statuarium, or statarius: a weight. Hence statuarius, that is, a weigher.
**“and I cast them into the house of the Lord”** — I had them returned by the traitor to the priests and Pharisees, who bought with it the potter’s field, that is, the field of the creator of all, in which are buried strangers and foreigners to the law, redeemed by the blood of Christ.
11.14:
**“And I cut off my second rod”** — the peculiar people
**“that was called a Cord”** — when the Lord had been crucified, and his price given for a burial ground, God does not put off giving sentence against Jerusalem, which was properly his portion and cord, but now it is cast off
**“that I might break”**
• “For I came not to send peace upon earth, but the sword.”
• As before Israel and Juda were separated from each other, so after Christ the apostles and those who did penance are again called Juda, that is, confessing the Lord. Those who remained in hardness of heart, saying, “We have no king but Caesar”, are called Israel, Ephraim, Joseph. So he divides the believers from the same people; for them he does not make void the testament of God, but stretches out his hand to this day; others he leaves in unbelief.
**“the brotherhood between Juda and Israel”** — the covenant and concord that had been between Juda and Israel
11.15:
**“And the Lord said to me”** — the prophet
**“Take to thee yet the instruments”** — the scrip, the staff, the pipe, the whistle
**“Take to thee yet”** — He who had first taken the rods, which were cast away at various times by their fault, and at last, when the brotherhood was broken, the Gentiles were grafted into the good olive tree, is commanded again to take the instruments of a foolish shepherd, that is, the prophecy of Antichrist.
**“of a foolish shepherd”** — that is, the insignia and bearing of Antichrist, so that you may show what he will be like when he comes, not only by voice but by bearing
11.16:
**“For behold I will raise up a shepherd”** — the good shepherd visits the sick sheep, seeks the scattered, brings back the forsaken, holds up the weary; the bad shepherd on the contrary does everything perversely
**“and he shall eat the flesh of the fat ones”** — Whatever flourished in the fatness of charity and wisdom he will devour, and will loosen and twist the hoofs of the rams and sheep, so that they cannot walk with a straight foot.
11.17:
**“O shepherd, and idol, that forsaketh the flock”**
• the shepherd having been described, the prophetic word turns to him
• This shepherd rises up in Israel because the true shepherd had said: Now I will not feed you. He is called by another name “the abomination of desolation”, who is to sit in the temple of God as though he were God.
• Therefore the sword of the Lord will be upon his arm and his eye will be worn away, so that his strength and all the boasting of his might may be dried up with withering, and the knowledge he promised himself under a false name may be darkened with everlasting darkness.
**“O shepherd, and idol”** — You are so wicked that you are called not a worshipper of idols but an idol, since you wish to be adored by men; you who forsake the flock to be devoured by beasts, which the Lord had guarded all the time.
**“the sword upon his arm and upon his right eye”** — with which he boasted that he saw the sacraments of God more sharply than all the prophets, so much that he called himself the Son of God

12.1:
**“The burden of the word of the Lord upon Israel”** — the following words show with how great a burden God is to press Jerusalem
**“The burden of the word of the Lord”** — From this place to the place where it says, “Awake, O sword”, there is a threefold exposition. Some of the Jews think these things were already partly fulfilled from Zorobabel to Gnaeus Pompeius, who was the first of the Romans to take Judea and the temple, as Josephus says; others that they are to be fulfilled at the end of the world, when Jerusalem will be restored. But Christians say these things are fulfilled daily in the Church until the end of the world. What is to be fitted to what, or to whom, let the prudent reader understand from the variety of what is set in between.
**“Thus saith the Lord, who stretcheth forth the heavens”** — like a skin
**“and layeth the foundations of the earth”** — he made it firm with a deep mass
**“and formeth the spirit”** — that is, the soul
12.2:
**“Behold I will make Jerusalem a lintel of surfeiting to all the people round about: and Juda also shall be in the siege against Jerusalem”**
• taken by the enemy and passing into their company, he will be forced to besiege his own capital, Jerusalem
• Allegorically. The persecutors who fight against the house of God are made drunk with that cup which Jeremias gives all nations to drink, that they may drink and be drunk and fall and vomit and go mad. For in the time of persecution many Christians were compelled to fight against the Church; and they lift the stone indeed and bear it up with their hands, for the anger of God with which he chastises sinners; but he who lifts it will not go unpunished, God’s sword fighting against him.
**“Behold I will make Jerusalem a lintel of surfeiting”** — So that whoever touches its threshold by dwelling there may be made drunk and fall, overcome by surfeit. Or the lintel itself will fall and crush him by whom it is touched.
12.3:
**“And it shall come to pass”** — besides what has been said
**“in that day, that I will make”** — namely this
**“Jerusalem a burdensome stone to all people: all that shall lift it up”** — the stone
**“shall be rent and torn”**
• they will not bear it unpunished
• by the weight of the stone
**“and all the kingdoms of the earth shall be gathered together against her”** — because they will be gathered against Jerusalem
**“a burdensome stone”** — It was the custom in Judea to set in some much-frequented place round stones of very great weight, which young men, to test their different strength, lifted, some to the knees, some to the navel, or even above the neck; and they did not go down to the contest until it was known from the lifting of the weight who should be matched with whom. So the sense is: I will set Jerusalem before the nations like a heavy stone for lifting, and they will lift it and lay it waste according to their different strength. But the heavy stone, while it is being lifted, will leave a rending or a scraping on the bodies of those who lift it.
12.4:
**“In that day, saith the Lord, I will strike every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open my eyes upon the house of Juda, and will strike every horse of the nations with blindness”**
