14.text: The eyes of a wise man are in his head: the fool walketh in darkness: and I learned that they were to die both alike.

15.text: And I said in my heart: If the death of the fool and mine shall be one, what doth it avail me, that I have applied myself more to the study of wisdom? And speaking with my own mind, I perceived that this also was vanity.

16.text: For there shall be no remembrance of the wise no more than of the fool for ever, and the times to come shall cover all things together with oblivion: the learned dieth in like manner as the unlearned.

17.text: And therefore I was weary of my life, when I saw that all things under the sun are evil, and all vanity and vexation of spirit.

18.text: Again I hated all my application wherewith I had earnestly laboured under the sun, being like to have an heir after me,

19.text: Whom I know not whether he will be a wise man or a fool, and he shall have rule over all my labours with which I have laboured and been solicitous: and is there any thing so vain?

20.text: Wherefore I left off and my heart renounced labouring any more under the sun.

21.text: For when a man laboureth in wisdom, and knowledge, and carefulness, he leaveth what he hath gotten to an idle man: so this also is vanity, and a great evil.

22.text: For what profit shall a man have of all his labour, and vexation of spirit, with which he hath been tormented under the sun?

23.text: All his days are full of sorrows and miseries, even in the night he doth not rest in mind: and is not this vanity?

24.text: Is it not better to eat and drink, and to shew his soul good things of his labours? and this is from the hand of God.

25.text: Who shall so feast and abound with delights as I?

26.text: God hath given to a man that is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care, to heap up and to gather together, and to give it to him that hath pleased God: but this also is vanity, and a fruitless solicitude of the mind.

1.text: All things have their season, and in their times all things pass under heaven.

2.text: A time to be born and a time to die. A time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted.

3.text: A time to kill, and a time to heal. A time to destroy, and a time to build.

4.text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh. A time to mourn, and a time to dance.

5.text: A time to scatter stones, and a time to gather. A time to embrace, and a time to be far from embraces.

6.text: A time to get, and a time to lose. A time to keep, and a time to cast away.

7.text: A time to rend, and a time to sew. A time to keep silence, and a time to speak.

8.text: A time of love, and a time of hatred. A time of war, and a time of peace.

9.text: What hath man more of his labour?

10.text: I have seen the trouble, which God hath given the sons of men to be exercised in it.

11.text: He hath made all things good in their time, and hath delivered the world to their consideration, so that man cannot find out the work which God hath made from the beginning to the end.

12.text: And I have known that there was no better thing than to rejoice, and to do well in this life.

13.text: For every man that eateth and drinketh, and seeth good of his labour, this is the gift of God.

14.text: I have learned that all the works which God hath made, continue for ever: we cannot add any thing, nor take away from those things which God hath made that he may be feared.

15.text: That which hath been made, the same continueth: the things that shall be, have already been: and God restoreth that which is past.

16.text: I saw under the sun in the place of judgment wickedness, and in the place of justice iniquity.

17.text: And I said in my heart: God shall judge both the just and the wicked, and then shall be the time of every thing.

18.text: I said in my heart concerning the sons of men, that God would prove them, and shew them to be like beasts.

19.text: Therefore the death of man, and of beasts is one, and the condition of them both is equal: as man dieth, so they also die: all things breathe alike, and man hath nothing more than beast: all things are subject to vanity.

20.text: And all things go to one place: of earth they were made, and into earth they return together.

21.text: Who knoweth if the spirit of the children of Adam ascend upward, and if the spirit of the beasts descend downward?

22.text: And I have found that nothing is better than for a man to rejoice in his work, and that this is his portion. For who shall bring him to know the things that shall be after him?

1.text: I turned myself to other things, and I saw the oppressions that are done under the sun, and the tears of the innocent, and they had no comforter; and they were not able to resist their violence, being destitute of help from any.

2.text: And I praised the dead rather than the living:

3.text: And I judged him happier than them both, that is not yet born, nor hath seen the evils that are done under the sun.

4.text: Again I considered all the labours of men, and I remarked that their industries are exposed to the envy of their neighhour: so in this also there is vanity, and fruitless care.

5.text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh, saying:

6.text: Better is a handful with rest, than both hands full with labour, and vexation of mind.

7.text: Considering I found also another vanity under the sun:

8.text: There is but one, and he hath not a second, no child, no brother, and yet he ceaseth not to labour, neither are his eyes satisfied with riches, neither doth he reflect, saying: For whom do I labour, and defraud my soul of good things? in this also is vanity, and a grievous vexation.

9.text: There is but one, and he hath not a second, no child, no brother, and yet he ceaseth not to labour, neither are his eyes satisfied with riches, neither doth he reflect, saying: For whom do I labour, and defraud my soul of good things? in this also is vanity, and a grievous vexation.

10.text: If one fall he shall be supported by the other: woe to him that is alone, for when he falleth, he hath none to lift him up.

11.text: And if two lie together, they shall warm one another: how shall one alone be warmed?

12.text: And if a man prevail against one, two shall withstand him: a threefold cord is not easily broken.

13.text: Better is a child that is poor and wise, than a king that is old and foolish, who knoweth not to foresee for hereafter.

14.text: Because out of prison and chains sometimes a man cometh forth to a kingdom: and another born king is consumed with poverty.

15.text: I saw all men living, that walk under the sun with the second young man, who shall rise up in his place.

16.text: The number of the people, of all that were before him is infinite: and they that shall come afterwards, shall not rejoice in him: but this also is vanity, and vexation of spirit.

1.text: Keep thy foot, when thou goest into the house of God, and draw nigh to hear. For much better is obedience, than the victims of fools, who know not what evil they do.

2.text: Speak not any thing rashly, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

3.text: Dreams follow many cares: and in many words shall be found folly.

4.text: If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it: for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeaseth him: but whatsoever thou hast vowed, pay it.

5.text: And it is much better not to vow, than after a vow not to perform the things promised.

6.text: Give not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin: and say not before the angel: There is no providence: lest God be angry at thy words, and destroy all the works of thy hands.

7.text: Where there are many dreams, there are many vanities, and words without number: but do thou fear God.

8.text: If thou shalt see the oppressions of the poor, and violent judgments, and justice perverted in the province, wonder not at this matter: for he that is high hath another higher, and there are others still higher than these:

9.text: Moreover there is the king that reigneth over all the land subject to him.

10.text: A covetous man shall not be satisfied with money: and he that loveth riches shall reap no fruit from them: so this also is vanity.

11.text: Where there are great riches, there are also many to eat them. And what doth it profit the owner, but that he seeth the riches with his eyes?

12.text: Sleep is sweet to a labouring man, whether he eat little or much: but the fulness of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

13.text: There is also another grievous evil, which I have seen under the sun: riches kept to the hurt of the owner.

14.text: For they are lost with very great affliction: he hath begotten a son, who shall be in extremity of want.

15.text: As he came forth naked from his mother’s womb, so shall he return, and shall take nothing away with him of his labour.

16.text: A most deplorable evil: as he came, so shall he return. What then doth it profit him that he hath laboured for the wind?

17.text: All the days of his life he eateth in darkness, and in many cares, and in misery, and sorrow.

18.text: This therefore hath seemed good to me, that a man should eat and drink, and enjoy the fruit of his labour, wherewith he hath laboured under the sun, all the days of his life, which God hath given him: and this is his portion.

19.text: And every man to whom God hath given riches, and substance, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to enjoy his portion, and to rejoice of his labour: this is the gift of God.

20.text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life, because God entertaineth his heart with delight,

1.text: There is also another evil, which I have seen under the sun, and that frequent among men:

2.text: A man to whom God hath given riches, and substance, and honour, and his soul wanteth nothing of all that he desireth: yet God doth not give him power to eat thereof, but a stranger shall eat it up. This is vanity and a great misery.

3.text: If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, and attain to a great age, and his soul make no use of the goods of his substance, and he be without burial: of this man I pronounce, that the untimely born is better than he.

4.text: For he came in vain, and goeth to darkness, and his name shall be wholly forgotten.

5.text: He hath not seen the sun, nor known the distance of good and evil:

6.text: Although he lived two thousand years, and hath not enjoyed good things: do not all make haste to one place?

7.text: All the labour of man is for his mouth, but his soul shall not be filled.

8.text: What hath the wise man more than the fool? and what the poor man, but to go thither, where there is life?

9.text: Better it is to see what thou mayst desire, than to desire that which thou canst not know. But this also is vanity, and presumption of spirit.

10.text: He that shall be, his name is already called: and it is known, that he is man, and cannot contend in judgment with him that is stronger than himself.

11.text: There are many words that have much vanity in disputing.

12.text: What needeth a man to seek things that are above him, whereas he knoweth not what is profitable for him in his life, in all the days of his pilgrimage, and the time that passeth like a shadow? Or who can tell him what shall be after him under the sun?

1.text: A good name is better than precious ointments: and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

2.text: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to the house of feasting: for in that we are put in mind of the end of all, and the living thinketh what is to come.

3.text: Anger is better than laughter: because by the sadness of the countenance the mind of the offender is corrected.

4.text: The heart of the wise is where there is mourning, and the heart of fools where there is mirth.

5.text: It is better to be rebuked by a wise man, than to be deceived by the flattery of fools.

6.text: For as the crackling of thorns burning under a pot, so is the laughter of a fool: now this also is vanity.

7.text: Oppression troubleth the wise, and shall destroy the strength of his heart.

8.text: Better is the end of a speech than the beginning. Better is the patient man than the presumptuous.

9.text: Be not quickly angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of a fool.

10.text: Say not: What thinkest thou is the cause that former times were better than they are now? for this manner of question is foolish.

11.text: Wisdom with riches is more profitable, and bringeth more advantage to them that see the sun.

12.text: For as wisdom is a defence, so money is a defence: but learning and wisdom excel in this, that they give life to him that possesseth them.

13.text: Consider the works of God, that no man can correct whom he hath despised.

14.text: In the good day enjoy good things, and beware beforehand of the evil day: for God hath made both the one and the other, that man may not find against him any just complaint.

15.text: These things also I saw in the days of my vanity: A just man perisheth in his justice, and a wicked man liveth a long time in his wickedness.

16.text: Be not over just: and be not more wise than is necessary, lest thou become stupid.

17.text: Be not overmuch wicked: and be not foolish, lest thou die before thy time.

18.text: It is good that thou shouldst hold up the just, yea and from him withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God, neglecteth nothing.

19.text: Wisdom hath strengthened the wise more than ten princes of the city.

20.text: For there is no just man upon earth, that doth good, and sinneth not.

21.text: But do not apply thy heart to all words that are spoken: lest perhaps thou hear thy servant reviling thee.

22.text: For thy conscience knoweth that thou also hast often spoken evil of others.

23.text: I have tried all things in wisdom. I have said: I will be wise: and it departed farther from me,

24.text: Much more than it was: it is a great depth, who shall find it out?

25.text: I have surveyed all things with my mind, to know, and consider, and seek out wisdom and reason: and to know the wickedness of the fool, and the error of the imprudent:

26.text: And I have found a woman more bitter than death, who is the hunter’s snare, and her heart is a net, and her hands are bands. He that pleaseth God shall escape from her: but he that is a sinner, shall be caught by her.

27.text: Lo this have I found, said Ecclesiastes, weighing one thing after another, that I might find out the account,

28.text: Which yet my soul seeketh, and I have not found it. One man among a thousand I have found, a woman among them all I have not found.

29.text: Only this I have found, that God made man right, and he hath entangled himself with an infinity of questions. Who is as the wise man? and who hath known the resolution of the word?

1.text: The wisdom of a man shineth in his countenance, and the most mighty will change his face.

2.text: I observe the mouth of the king, and the commandments of the oath of God.

3.text: Be not hasty to depart from his face, and do not continue in an evil work: for he will do all that pleaseth him:

4.text: And his word is full of power: neither can any man say to him: Why dost thou so?

5.text: He that keepeth the commandments shall find no evil. The heart of a wise man understandeth time and answer.

6.text: There is a time and opportunity for every business, and great affliction for man:

7.text: Because he is ignorant of things past, and things to come he cannot know by any messenger.

8.text: It is not in man’s power to stop the spirit, neither hath he power in the day of death, neither is he suffered to rest when war is at hand, neither shall wickedness save the wicked.

9.text: All these things I have considered, and applied my heart to all the works that are done under the sun. Sometimes one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

10.text: I saw the wicked buried: who also when they were yet living were in the holy place, and were praised in the city as men of just works: but this also is vanity.

11.text: For because sentence is not speedily pronounced against the evil, the children of men commit evils without any fear.

12.text: But though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and by patience be borne withal, I know from thence that it shall be well with them that fear God, who dread his face.

13.text: But let it not be well with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged, but as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord.

14.text: There is also another vanity, which is done upon the earth. There are just men to whom evils happen, as though they had done the works of the wicked: and there are wicked men, who are as secure, as though they had the deeds of the just: but this also I judge most vain.

15.text: Therefore I commended mirth, because there was no good for a man under the sun, but to eat, and drink, and be merry, and that he should take nothing else with him of his labour in the days of his life, which God hath given him under the sun.

16.text: And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to understand the distraction that is upon earth: for there are some that day and night take no sleep with their eyes.

17.text: And I understood that man can find no reason of all those works of God that are done under the sun: and the more he shall labour to seek, so much the less shall he find: yea, though the wise man shall say, that he knoweth it, he shall not be able to find it.

1.text: All these things have I considered in my heart, that I might carefully understand them: there are just men and wise men, and their works are in the hand of God: and yet man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred:

2.text: But all things are kept uncertain for the time to come, because all things equally happen to the just and to the wicked, to the good and to the evil, to the clean and to the unclean, to him that offereth victims, and to him that despiseth sacrifices. As the good is, so also is the sinner: as the perjured, so he also that sweareth truth.

3.text: This is a very great evil among all things that are done under the sun, that the same things happen to all men: whereby also the hearts of the children of men are filled with evil, and with contempt while they live, and afterwards they shall be brought down to hell.

4.text: There is no man that liveth always, or that hopeth for this: a living dog is better than a dead lion.

5.text: For the living know that they shall die, but the dead know nothing more, neither have they a reward any more: for the memory of them is forgotten.

6.text: Their love also, and their hatred, and their envy are all perished, neither have they any part in this world, and in the work that is done under the sun.

7.text: Go then, and eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with gladness: because thy works please God.

8.text: At all times let thy garments be white, and let not oil depart from thy head.

9.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest, all the days of thy unsteady life, which are given to thee under the sun, all the time of thy vanity: for this is thy portion in life, and in thy labour wherewith thou labourest under the sun.

10.text: Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly: for neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell, whither thou art hastening.

11.text: I turned me to another thing, and I saw that under the sun, the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the learned, nor favour to the skillful: but time and chance in all.

12.text: Man knoweth not his own end: but as fishes are taken with the hook, and as birds are caught with the snare, so men are taken in the evil time, when it shall suddenly come upon them.

13.text: This wisdom also I have seen under the sun, and it seemed to me to be very great:

14.text: A little city, and few men in it: there came against it a great king, and invested it, and built bulwarks round about it, and the siege was perfect.

15.text: Now there was found in it a man poor and wise, and he delivered the city by his wisdom, and no man afterward remembered that poor man.

16.text: And I said that wisdom is better than strength: how then is the wisdom of the poor man slighted, and his words not heard?

17.text: The words of the wise are heard in silence, more than the cry of a prince among fools.

18.text: Better is wisdom, than weapons of war: and he that shall offend in one, shall lose many good things.

1.text: Dying flies spoil the sweetness of the ointment. Wisdom and glory is more precious than a small and shortlived folly.

2.text: The heart of a wise man is in his right hand, and the heart of a fool is in his left hand.

3.text: Yea, and the fool when he walketh in the way, whereas he himself is a fool, esteemeth all men fools.

4.text: If the spirit of him that hath power, ascend upon thee, leave not thy place: because care will make the greatest sins to cease.

5.text: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as it were by an error proceeding from the face of the prince:

6.text: A fool set in high dignity, and the rich sitting beneath.

7.text: I have seen servants upon horses: and princes walking on the ground as servants.

8.text: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

9.text: He that removeth stones, shall be hurt by them: and he that cutteth trees, shall be wounded by them.

10.text: If the iron be blunt, and be not as before, but be made blunt, with much labour it shall be sharpened: and after industry shall follow wisdom.

11.text: If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly.

12.text: The words of the mouth of a wise man are grace: but the lips of a fool shall throw him down headlong.

13.text: The beginning of his words is folly, and the end of his talk is a mischievous error.

14.text: A fool multiplieth words. A man cannot tell what hath been before him: and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

15.text: The labour of fools shall afflict them that know not how to go to the city.

16.text: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and when the princes eat in the morning.

17.text: Blessed is the land, whose king is noble, and whose princes eat in due season for refreshment, and not for riotousness.

18.text: By slothfulness a building shall be brought down, and through the weakness of hands, the house shall drop through.

19.text: For laughter they make bread, and wine that the living may feast: and all things obey money.

20.text: Detract not the king, no not in thy thought; and speak not evil of the rich man in thy private chamber: because even the birds of the air will carry thy voice, and he that hath wings will tell what thou hast said.

1.text: Cast thy bread upon the running waters: for after a long time thou shalt find it again.

2.text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight: for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

3.text: If the clouds be full, they will pour out rain upon the earth. If the tree fall to the south, or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be.

4.text: He that observeth the wind, shall not sow: and he that considereth the clouds, shall never reap.

5.text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones are joined together in the womb of her that is with child: so thou knowest not the works of God, who is the maker of all.

6.text: In the morning sow thy seed, and In the evening let not thy hand cease: for thou knowest not which may rather spring up, this or that: and if both together, it shall be the better.

7.text: The light is sweet, and it is delightful for the eyes to see the sun.

8.text: If a man live many years, and have rejoiced in them all, he must remember the darksome time, and the many days: which when they shall come, the things past shall be accused of vanity.

9.text: Rejoice therefore, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart be in that which is good in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thy eyes: and know that for all these God will bring thee into judgment.

10.text: Remove anger from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh. For youth and pleasure are vain.

1.text: Remember thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the time of affliction come, and the years draw nigh of which thou shalt say: They please me not:

2.text: Before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars be darkened, and the clouds return after the rain:

3.text: When the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall stagger, and the grinders shall be idle in a small number, and they that look through the holes shall be darkened:

4.text: And they shall shut the doors in the street, when the grinder’s voice shall be low, and they shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music shall grow deaf.

5.text: And they shall fear high things, and they shall be afraid in the way, the almond tree shall flourish, the locust shall be made fat, and the caper tree shall be destroyed: because man shall go into the house of his eternity, and the mourners shall go round about in the street.

6.text: Before the silver cord be broken, and the golden fillet shrink back, and the pitcher be crushed at the fountain, and the wheel be broken upon the cistern,

7.text: And the dust return into its earth, from whence it was, and the spirit return to God, who gave it.

8.text: Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes, and all things are vanity.

9.text: And whereas Ecclesiastes was very wise, he taught the people, and declared the things that he had done: and seeking out, he set forth many parables.

10.text: He sought profitable words, and wrote words most right, and full of truth.

11.text: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails deeply fastened in, which by the counsel of masters are given from one shepherd.

12.text: More than these, my son, require not. Of making many books there is no end: and much study is an affliction of the flesh.

13.text: Let us all hear together the conclusion of the discourse. Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is all man:

14.text: And all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil.

2.text: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth: for thy breasts are better than wine,

3.text: Smelling sweet of the best ointments. Thy name is as oil poured out: therefore young maidens have loved thee.

4.text: Draw me: we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments. The king hath brought me into his storerooms: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, remembering thy breasts more than wine: the righteous love thee.

5.text: I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Cedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

6.text: Do not consider me that I am brown, because the sun hath altered my colour: the sons of my mother have fought against me, they have made me the keeper in the vineyards: my vineyard I have not kept.

7.text: Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions.

8.text: If thou know not thyself, O fairest among women, go forth, and follow after the steps of the flocks, and feed thy kids beside the tents of the shepherds.

9.text: To my company of horsemen, in Pharao’s chariots, have I likened thee, O my love.

10.text: Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove’s, thy neck as jewels.

11.text: We will make thee chains of gold, inlaid with silver.

12.text: While the king was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.

13.text: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts.

14.text: A cluster of cypress my love is to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi.

15.text: Behold thou art fair, O my love, behold thou art fair, thy eyes are as those of doves.

16.text: Behold thou art fair, my beloved, and comely. Our bed is flourishing.

17.text: The beams of our houses are of cedar, our rafters of cypress trees.

1.text: I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.

2.text: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

3.text: As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow, whom I desired: and his fruit was sweet to my palate.

4.text: He brought me into the cellar of wine, he set in order charity in me.

5.text: Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love.

6.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

7.text: I adjure you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and the harts of the, fields, that you stir not up, nor make the beloved to awake, till she please.

8.text: The voice of my beloved, behold he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills.

9.text: My beloved is like a roe, or a young hart. Behold he standeth behind our wall, looking through the windows, looking through the lattices.

10.text: Behold my beloved speaketh to me: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come.

11.text: For winter is now past, the rain is over and gone.

12.text: The flowers have appeared in our land, the time of pruning is come: the voice of the turtle is heard in our land:

13.text: The fig tree hath put forth her green figs: the vines in flower yield their sweet smell. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come:

14.text: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow places of the wall, shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.

15.text: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vines: for our vineyard hath flourished.

16.text: My beloved to me, and I to him who feedeth among the lilies,

17.text: Till the day break, and the shadows retire. Return: be like, my beloved, to a roe, or to a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

1.text: In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, and found him not.

2.text: I will rise, and will go about the city: in the streets and the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, and I found him not.

3.text: The watchmen who keep the city, found me: Have you seen him, whom my soul loveth?

4.text: When I had a little passed by them, I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him: and I will not let him go, till I bring him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that bore me.

5.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor awake my beloved, till she please.

6.text: Who is she that goeth up by the desert, as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer?

7.text: Behold threescore valiant ones of the most valiant of Israel, surrounded the bed of Solomon?

8.text: All holding swords, and most expert in war: every man’s sword upon his thigh, because of fears in the night.

9.text: King Solomon hath made him a litter of the wood of Libanus:

10.text: The pillars thereof he made of silver, the seat of gold, the going up of purple: the midst he covered with charity for the daughters of Jerusalem.

11.text: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and see king Solomon in the diadem, wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the joy of his heart.

1.text: How beautiful art thou, my love, how beautiful art thou! thy eyes are doves’ eyes, besides what is hid within. Thy hair is as flocks of goats, which Come up from mount Galaad.

2.text: Thy teeth as flocks of sheep, that are shorn which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.

3.text: Thy lips are as a scarlet lace: and thy speech sweet. Thy cheeks are as a piece of a pomegranate, besides that which lieth hid within.

4.text: Thy neck, is as the tower of David, which is built with bulwarks: a thousand bucklers hang upon it, all the armour of valiant men.

5.text: Thy two breasts like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

6.text: Till the day break, and the shadows retire, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

7.text: Thou art all fair, O my love, and there is not a spot in thee.

8.text: Come from Libanus, my spouse, come from Libanus, come: thou shalt be crowned from the top of Amana, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

9.text: Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse, thou hast wounded my heart with one of thy eyes, and with one hair of thy neck.

10.text: How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister, my spouse! thy breasts are more beautiful than wine, and the sweet smell of thy ointments above all aromatical spices.

11.text: Thy lips, my spouse, are as a dropping honeycomb, honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments, as the smell of frankincense.

12.text: My sister, my spouse, is a garden enclosed, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed up.

13.text: Thy plants are a paradise of pomegranates with the fruits of the orchard. Cypress with spikenard.

14.text: Spikenard and saffron, sweet cane and cinnamon, with all the trees of Libanus, myrrh and aloes with all the chief perfumes.

15.text: The fountain of gardens: the well of living waters, which run with a strong stream from Libanus.

16.text: Arise, O north wind, and come, O south wind, blow through my garden, and let the aromatical spices thereof flow.

1.text: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees. I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved.

2.text: I sleep, and my heart watcheth; the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights.

3.text: I have put off my garment, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them?

4.text: My beloved put his hand through the key hole, and my bowels were moved at his touch.

5.text: I arose up to open to my beloved: my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh.

6.text: I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved: but he had turned aside, and was gone. My soul melted when he spoke: I sought him, and found him not: I called, and he did not answer me.

7.text: The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me: and wounded me: the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

8.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love.

9.text: What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women? what manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, that thou hast so adjured us?

10.text: My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands.

11.text: His head is as the finest gold: his locks as branches of palm trees, black as a raven.

12.text: His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams.

13.text: His cheeks are as beds of aromatical spices set by the perfumers. His lips are as lilies dropping choice myrrh.

14.text: His hands are turned and as of gold, full of hyacinths. His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires.

15.text: His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold. His form as of Libanus, excellent as the cedars.

16.text: His throat most sweet, and he is all lovely: such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.

1.text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou most beautiful among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside, and we will seek him with thee?

2.text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the bed of aromatical spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

3.text: I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, who feedeth among the lilies.

4.text: Thou art beautiful, O my love, sweet and comely as Jerusalem: terrible as an army set in array.

5.text: Turn away thy eyes from me, for they have made me flee away. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from Galaad.

6.text: Thy teeth as a flock of sheep, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.

7.text: Thy cheeks are as the bark of a pomegranate, beside what is hidden within thee.

8.text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and young maidens without number.

9.text: One is my dove, my perfect one is but one, she is the only one of her mother, the chosen of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and declared her most blessed: the queens and concubines, and they praised her.

10.text: Who is she that cometh forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, terrible as an army set in array?

11.text: I went down into the garden of nuts, to see the fruits of the valleys, and to look if the vineyard had flourished, and the pomegranates budded.

12.text: I knew not: my soul troubled me for the chariots of Aminadab.

13.text: Return, return, O Sulamitess: return, return that we may behold thee.

1.text: What shalt thou see in the Sulamitess but the companies of camps? How beautiful are thy steps in shoes, O prince’s daughter! The joints of thy thighs are like jewels, that are made by the hand of a skillful workman.

2.text: Thy navel is like a round bowl never wanting cups. Thy belly is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.

3.text: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

4.text: Thy neck as a tower of ivory. Thy eyes like the fishpools in Hesebon, which are in the gate of the daughter of the multitude. Thy nose is as the tower of Libanus, that looketh toward Damascus.

5.text: Thy head is like Carmel: and the hairs of thy head as the purple of the king bound in the channels.

6.text: How beautiful art thou, and how comely, my dearest, in delights!

7.text: Thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

8.text: I said: I will go up into the palm tree, and will take hold of the fruit thereof: and thy breasts shall be as the clusters of the vine: and the odour of thy mouth like apples.

9.text: Thy throat like the best wine, worthy for my beloved to drink, and for his lips and his teeth to ruminate.

10.text: I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me.

11.text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field, let us abide in the villages.

12.text: Let us get up early to the vineyards, let us see if the vineyard flourish, if the flowers be ready to bring forth fruits, if the pomegranates flourish: there will I give thee my breasts.

13.text: The mandrakes give a smell. In our gates are all fruits: the new and the old, my beloved, I have kept for thee.

1.text: Who shall give thee to me for my brother, sucking the breasts of my mother, that I may find thee without, and kiss thee, and now no man may despise me?

2.text: I will take hold of thee, and bring thee Into my mother’s house: there thou shalt teach me, and I will give thee a cup of spiced wine and new wine of my pomegranates.

3.text: His left hand under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

4.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that you stir not up, nor awake my love till she please.

5.text: Who is this that cometh up from the desert, flowing with delights, leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple tree I raised thee up: there thy mother was corrupted, there she was defloured that bore thee.

6.text: Put me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell, the lamps thereof are fire and flames.

7.text: Many waters cannot quench charity, neither can the floods drown it: if a man should give all the substance of his house for love, he shall despise it as nothing.

8.text: Our sister is little, and hath no breasts. What shall we do to our sister in the day when she is to be spoken to?

9.text: If she be a wall: let us build upon it bulwarks of silver: if she be a door, let us join it together with boards of cedar.

10.text: I am a wall: and my breasts are as a tower since I am become in his presence as one finding peace.

11.text: The peaceable had a vineyard, in that which hath people: he let out the same to keepers, every man bringeth for the fruit thereof a thousand pieces of silver.

12.text: My vineyard is before me. A thousand are for thee, the peaceable, and two hundred for them that keep the fruit thereof.

13.text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the friends hearken: make me hear thy voice.

14.text: Flee away, O my beloved, and be like to the roe, and to the young hart upon the mountains of aromatical spices.

1.text: Love justice, you that are the judges of the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart.

2.text: For he is found by them that tempt him not: and he sheweth himself to them that have faith in him.

3.text: For perverse thoughts separate from God: and his power, when it is tried, reproveth the unwise:

4.text: For wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins.

5.text: For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding, and he shall not abide when iniquity cometh in.

6.text: For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not acquit the evil speaker from his lips: for God is witness of his reins, and he is a true searcher of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

7.text: For the spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole world: and that, which containeth all things, hath knowledge of the voice.

8.text: Therefore he that speaketh unjust things cannot be hid, neither shall the chastising judgment pass him by.

9.text: For inquisition shall be made into the thoughts of the ungodly: and the hearing of his words shall come to God, to the chastising of his iniquities.

10.text: For the ear of jealousy heareth all things, and the tumult of murmuring shall not be hid.

11.text: Keep yourselves therefore from murmuring, which profiteth nothing, and refrain your tongue from detraction, for an obscure speech shall not go for nought: and the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul.

12.text: Seek not death in the error of your life, neither procure ye destruction by the works of your hands.

13.text: For God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living.

14.text: For he created all things that they might be: and he made the nations of the earth for health: and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor kingdom of hell upon the earth.

15.text: For justice is perpetual and immortal.

16.text: But the wicked with works and words have called it to them: and esteeming it a friend have fallen away, and have made a covenant with it: because they are worthy to be of the part thereof.

1.text: For they have said, reasoning with themselves, but not right: The time of our life is short and tedious, and in the end of a man there is no remedy, and no man hath been known to have returned from hell:

2.text: For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been: for the breath in our nostrils is smoke: and speech a spark to move our heart,

3.text: Which being put out, our body shall be ashes, and our spirit shall be poured abroad as soft air, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, which is driven away by the beams of the sun, and overpowered with the heat thereof:

4.text: And our name in time shall be forgotten, and no man shall have any remembrance of our works.

5.text: For our time is as the passing of a shadow, and there is no going back of our end: for it is fast sealed, and no man returneth.

6.text: Come therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth.

7.text: Let us fill ourselves with costly wine, and ointments: and let not the flower of the time pass by us.

8.text: Let us crown ourselves with roses, before they be withered: let no meadow escape our riot.

9.text: Let none of us go without his part in luxury: let us everywhere leave tokens of joy: for this is our portion, and this our lot.

10.text: Let us oppress the poor just man, and not spare the widow, nor honour the ancient grey hairs of the aged.

11.text: But let our strength be the law of justice: for that which is feeble, is found to be nothing worth.

12.text: Let us therefore lie in wait for the just, because he is not for our turn, and he is contrary to our doings, and upbraideth us with transgressions of the law, and divulgeth against us the sins of our way of life.

13.text: He boasteth that he hath the knowledge of God, and calleth himself the son of God.

14.text: He is become a censurer of our thoughts.

15.text: He is grievous unto us, even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, and his ways are very different.

16.text: We are esteemed by him as triflers, and he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness, and he preferreth the latter end of the just, and glorieth that he hath God for his father.

17.text: Let us see then if his words be true, and let us prove what shall happen to him, and we shall know what his end shall be.

18.text: For if he be the true son of God, he will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies.

19.text: Let us examine him by outrages and tortures, that we may know his meekness and try his patience.

20.text: Let us condemn him to a most shameful death: for there shall be respect had unto him by his words.

21.text: These things they thought, and were deceived: for their own malice blinded them.

22.text: And they knew not the secrets of God, nor hoped for the wages of justice, nor esteemed the honour of holy souls.

23.text: For God created man incorruptible, and to the image of his own likeness he made him.

24.text: But by the envy of the devil, death came into the world: And they follow him that are of his side.

1.text: But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.

2.text: In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure was taken for misery:

3.text: And their going away from us, for utter destruction: but they are in peace.

4.text: And though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality.

5.text: Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded: because God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself.

6.text: As gold in the furnace he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust he hath received them, and in time there shall be respect had to them.

7.text: The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds.

8.text: They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.

9.text: They that trust in him, shall understand the truth: and they that are faithful in love shall rest in him: for grace and peace is to his elect.

10.text: But the wicked shall be punished according to their own devices: who have neglected the just, and have revolted from the Lord.

11.text: For he that rejecteth wisdom, and discipline, is unhappy: and their hope is vain, and their labours without fruit, and their works unprofitable.

12.text: Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked.

13.text: Their offspring is cursed: for happy is the barren: and the undefiled, that hath not known bed in sin: she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.

14.text: And the eunuch, that hath not wrought iniquity with his hands, nor thought wicked things against God: for the precious gift of faith shall be given to him, and a most acceptable lot in the temple of God.

15.text: For the fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of wisdom never faileth.

16.text: But the children of adulterers shall not come to perfection, and the seed of the unlawful bed shall be rooted out.

17.text: And if they live long, they shall be nothing regarded, and their last old age shall be without honour.

18.text: And if they die quickly, they shall have no hope, nor speech of comfort in the day of trial.

19.text: For dreadful are the ends of a wicked race.

1.text: O how beautiful is the chaste generation with glory: for the memory thereof is immortal: because it is known both with God and with men.

2.text: When it is present, they imitate it: and they desire it when it hath withdrawn itself, and it triumpheth crowned for ever, winning the reward of undefiled conflicts.

3.text: But the multiplied brood of the wicked shall not thrive, and bastard slips shall not take deep root, nor any fast foundation.

4.text: And if they flourish in branches for a time, yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.

5.text: For the branches not being perfect, shall be broken, and their fruits shall be unprofitable, and sour to eat, and fit for nothing.

6.text: For the children that are born of unlawful beds, are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their trial.

7.text: But the just man, if he be prevented with death, shall be in rest.

8.text: For venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs.

9.text: And a spotless life is old age.

10.text: He pleased God and was beloved, and living among sinners he was translated.

11.text: He was taken away lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.

12.text: For the bewitching of vanity obscureth good things, and the wandering of concupiscence overturneth the innocent mind.

13.text: Being made perfect in a short space, he fulfilled a long time:

14.text: For his soul pleased God: therefore he hastened to bring him out of the midst of iniquities: but the people see this, and understand not, nor lay up such things in their hearts:

15.text: That the grace of God, and his mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect to his chosen.

16.text: But the just that is dead, condemneth the wicked that are living, and youth soon ended, the long life of the unjust.

17.text: For they shall see the end of the wise man, and shall not understand what God hath designed for him, and why the Lord hath set him in safety.

18.text: They shall see him, and shall despise him: but the Lord shall laugh them to scorn.

19.text: And they shall fall after this without honour, and be a reproach among the dead for ever: for he shall burst them puffed up and speechless, and shall shake them from the foundations, and they shall be utterly laid waste: they shall be in sorrow, and their memory shall perish.

20.text: They shall come with fear at the thought of their sins, and their iniquities shall stand against them to convict them.

1.text: Then shall the just stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours.

2.text: These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation.

3.text: Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: These are they, whom we had some time in derision, and for a parable of reproach.

4.text: We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour.

5.text: Behold how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints.

6.text: Therefore we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us.

7.text: We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known.

8.text: What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?

9.text: All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on,

10.text: And as a ship that passeth through the waves: whereof when it is gone by, the trace cannot be found, nor the path of its keel in the waters:

11.text: Or as when a bird flieth through the air, of the passage of which no mark can be found, but only the sound of the wings beating the light air, and parting it by the force of her flight; she moved her wings, and hath flown through, and there is no mark found afterwards of her way:

12.text: Or as when an arrow is shot at a mark, the divided air presently cometh together again, so that the passage thereof is not known:

13.text: So we also being born, forthwith ceased to be: and have been able to shew no mark of virtue: but are consumed in our wickedness. Such things as these the sinners said in hell:

14.text: For the hope of the wicked is as dust, which is blown away with the wind, and as a thin froth which is dispersed by the storm: and a smoke that is scattered abroad by the wind: and as the remembrance of a guest of one day that passeth by.

15.text: But the just shall live for evermore: and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them with the most High.

16.text: Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord: for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them.

17.text: And his zeal will take armour, and he will arm the creature for the revenge of his enemies.

18.text: He will put on justice as a breastplate, and will take true judgment instead of a helmet.

19.text: He will take equity for an invincible shield:

20.text: And he will sharpen his severe wrath for a spear, and the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise.

21.text: Then shafts of lightning shall go directly from the clouds, as from a bow well bent, they shall be shot out, and shall fly to the mark.

22.text: And thick hail shall be cast upon them from the stone casting wrath: the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall run together in a terrible manner.

23.text: A mighty wind shall stand up against them, and as a whirlwind shall divide them: and their iniquity shall bring all the earth to a desert, and wickedness shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.

1.text: Wisdom is better than strength, and a wise man is better than a strong man. Hear therefore, ye kings, and understand: learn, ye that are judges of the ends of the earth.

2.text: Give ear, you that rule the people, and that please yourselves in multitudes of nations:

3.text: For power is given you by the Lord, and strength by the most High, who will examine your works, and search out your thoughts:

4.text: Because being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged rightly, nor kept the law of justice, nor walked according to the will of God.

5.text: Horribly and speedily will he appear to you: for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule.

6.text: For to him that is little, mercy is granted: but the mighty shall be mightily tormented.

7.text: For God will not except any man’s person, neither will he stand in awe of any man’s greatness: for he made the little and the great, and he hath equally care of all.

8.text: But a greater punishment is ready for the more mighty.

9.text: To you, therefore, O kings, are these my words, that you may learn wisdom, and not fall from it.

10.text: For they that have kept just things justly, shall be justified: and they that have learned these things, shall find what to answer.

11.text: Covet ye therefore my words, and love them, and you shall have instruction.

12.text: Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away, and is easily seen by them that love her, and is found by them that seek her.

13.text: She preventeth them that covet her, so that she first sheweth herself unto them.

14.text: He that awaketh early to seek her, shall not labour: for he shall find her sitting at his door.

15.text: To think therefore upon her, is perfect understanding: and he that watcheth for her, shall quickly be secure.

16.text: For she goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, and she sheweth herself to them cheerfully in the ways, and meeteth them with all providence.

17.text: For the beginning of her is the most true desire of discipline.

18.text: And the care of discipline is love: and love is the keeping of her laws: and the keeping of her laws is the firm foundation of incorruption:

19.text: And incorruption bringeth near to God.

20.text: Therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to the everlasting kingdom.

21.text: If then your delight be in thrones, and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, love wisdom, that you may reign for ever. Love the light of wisdom, all ye that bear rule over peoples.

22.text: Now what wisdom is, and what was her origin, I will declare: and I will not hide from you the mysteries of God, but will seek her out from the beginning of her birth, and bring the knowledge of her to light, and will not pass over the truth:

23.text: Neither will I go with consuming envy: for such a man shall not be partaker of wisdom.

24.text: Now the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the whole world: and a wise king is the upholding of the people.

25.text: Receive therefore instruction by my words, and it shall be profitable to you.

1.text: I myself also am a mortal man, like all others, and of the race of him, that was first made of the earth, and in the womb of my mother I was fashioned to be flesh.

2.text: In the time of ten months I was compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure of sleep concurring.

3.text: And being born I drew in the common air, and fell upon the earth, that is made alike, and the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do.

4.text: I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and with great cares.

5.text: For none of the kings had any other beginning of birth.

6.text: For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.

7.text: Wherefore I wished, and understanding was given me: and I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came upon me:

8.text: And I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.

9.text: Neither did I compare unto her any precious stone: for all gold in comparison of her, is as a little sand, and silver in respect to her shall be counted as clay.

10.text: I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for her light cannot be put out.

11.text: Now all good things came to me together with her, and innumerable riches through her hands,

12.text: And I rejoiced in all these: for this wisdom went before me, and I knew not that she was the mother of them all.

13.text: Which I have learned without guile, and communicate without envy, and her riches I hide not.

14.text: For she is an infinite treasure to men! which they that use, become the friends of God, being commended for the gift of discipline.

15.text: And God hath given to me to speak as I would, and to conceive thoughts worthy of those things that are given me: because he is the guide of wisdom, and the director of the wise:

16.text: For in his hand are both we, and our words, and all wisdom, and the knowledge and skill of works.

17.text: For he hath given me the true knowledge of the things that are: to know the disposition of the whole world, and the virtues of the elements,

18.text: The beginning, and ending, and midst of the times, the alterations of their courses, and the changes of seasons,

19.text: The revolutions of the year, and the dispositions of the stars,

20.text: The natures of living creatures, and rage of wild beasts, the force of winds, and reasonings of men, the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots,

21.text: And all such things as are hid and not foreseen, I have learned: for wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me.

22.text: For in her is the spirit of understanding: holy, one, manifold, subtile, eloquent, active, undefiled, sure, sweet, loving that which is good, quick, which nothing hindereth, beneficent,

23.text: Gentle, kind, steadfast, assured, secure, having all power, overseeing all things, and containing all spirits, intelligible, pure, subtile.

24.text: For wisdom is more active than all active things: and reacheth everywhere by reason of her purity.

25.text: For she is a vapour of the power of God, and a certain pure emanation of the glory of the almighty God: and therefore no defiled thing cometh into her.

26.text: For she is the brightness of eternal light, and the unspotted mirror of God’s majesty, and the image of his goodness.

27.text: And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself the same, she reneweth all things, and through nations conveyeth herself into holy souls, she maketh the friends of God and prophets.

28.text: For God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom.

29.text: For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of the stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it.

30.text: For after this cometh night, but no evil can overcome wisdom.

1.text: She reacheth therefore from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly.

2.text: Her have I loved, and have sought her out from my youth, and have desired to take her for my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty.

3.text: She glorifieth her nobility by being conversant with God: yea and the Lord of all things hath loved her.

4.text: For it is she that teacheth the knowledge of God, and is the chooser of his works.

5.text: And if riches be desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, which maketh all things?

6.text: And if sense do work: who is a more artful worker than she of those things that are?

7.text: And if a man love justice: her labours have great virtues; for she teacheth temperance, and prudence, and justice, and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in life.

8.text: And if a man desire much knowledge: she knoweth things past, and judgeth of things to come: she knoweth the subtilties of speeches, and the solutions of arguments: she knoweth signs and wonders before they be done, and the events of times and ages.

9.text: I purposed therefore to take her to me to live with me: knowing that she will communicate to me of her good things, and will be a comfort in my cares and grief.

10.text: For her sake I shall have glory among the multitude, and honour with the ancients, though I be young:

11.text: And I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of the mighty, and the faces of princes shall wonder at me.

12.text: They shall wait for me when I hold my peace, and they shall look upon me when I speak, and if I talk much they shall lay their hands on their mouths.

13.text: Moreover by the means of her I shall have immortality: and shall leave behind me an everlasting memory to them that come after me.

14.text: I shall set the people in order: and nations shall be subject to me.

15.text: Terrible kings hearing shall be afraid of me: among the multitude I shall be found good, and valiant in war.

16.text: When I go into my house, I shall repose myself with her: for her conversation hath no bitterness, nor her company any tediousness, but joy and gladness.

17.text: Thinking these things with myself, and pondering them in my heart, that to be allied to wisdom is immortality,

18.text: And that there is great delight in her friendship, and inexhaustible riches in the works of her hands, and in the exercise of conference with her, wisdom, and glory in the communication of her words: I went about seeking, that I might take her to myself.

19.text: And I was a witty child and had received a good soul.

20.text: And whereas I was more good, I came to a body undefiled.

21.text: And as I knew that I could not otherwise be continent, except God gave it, and this also was a point of wisdom, to know whose gift it was: I went to the Lord, and besought him, and said with my whole heart:

1.text: God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who hast made all things with thy word,

2.text: And by thy wisdom hast appointed man, that he should have dominion over the creature that was made by thee,

3.text: That he should order the world according to equity and justice, and execute justice with an upright heart:

4.text: Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne, and cast me not off from among thy children:

5.text: For I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid, a weak man, and of short time, and falling short of the understanding of judgment and laws.

6.text: For if one be perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.

7.text: Thou hast chosen me to be king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters.

8.text: And hast commanded me to build a temple on thy holy mount, and an altar in the city of thy dwelling place, a resemblance of thy holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning:

9.text: And thy wisdom with thee, which knoweth thy works, which then also was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was agreeable to thy eyes, and what was right in thy commandments.

10.text: Send her out of thy holy heaven, and from the throne of thy majesty, that she may be with me, and may labour with me, that I may know what is acceptable with thee:

11.text: For she knoweth and understandeth all things, and shall lead me soberly in my works, and shall preserve me by her power.

12.text: So shall my works be acceptable, and I shall govern thy people justly, and shall be worthy of the throne of my father.

13.text: For who among men is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can think what the will of God is?

14.text: For the thoughts of mortal men are fearful, and our counsels uncertain.

15.text: For the corruptible body is a load upon the soul, and the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things.

16.text: And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth: and with labour do we find the things that are before us. But the things that are in heaven, who shall search out?

17.text: And who shall know thy thought, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above:

18.text: And so the ways of them that are upon earth may be corrected, and men may learn the things that please thee? For by wisdom they were healed, whosoever have pleased thee, O Lord, from the beginning.

1.text: She preserved him, that was first formed by God the father of the world, when he was created alone,

2.text: And she brought him out of his sin, and gave him power to govern all things.

3.text: But when the unjust went away from her in his anger, he perished by the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.

4.text: For whose cause, when water destroyed the earth, wisdom healed it again, directing the course of the just by contemptible wood.

5.text: Moreover when the nations had conspired together to consent to wickedness, she knew the just, and preserved him without blame to God, and kept him strong against the compassion for his son.

6.text: She delivered the just man who fled from the wicked that were perishing, when the fire came down upon Pentapolis:

7.text: Whose land for a testimony of their wickedness is desolate, and smoketh to this day, and the trees bear fruits that ripen not, and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an incredulous soul.

8.text: For regarding not wisdom, they did not only slip in this, that they were ignorant of good things, but they left also unto men a memorial of their folly, so that in the things in which they sinned, they could not so much as lie hid.

9.text: But wisdom hath delivered from sorrow them that attend upon her.

10.text: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother’s wrath, through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

11.text: In the deceit of them that overreached him, she stood by him, and made him honourable.

12.text: She kept him safe from his enemies, and she defended him from seducers, and gave him a strong conflict, that he might overcome, and know that wisdom is mightier than all.

13.text: She forsook not the just when he was sold, but delivered him from sinners: she went down with him into the pit.

14.text: And in bands she left him not, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: and shewed them to be liars that had accused him, and gave him everlasting glory.

15.text: She delivered the just people, and blameless seed from the nations that oppressed them.

16.text: She entered into the soul of the servant of God, and stood against dreadful kings in wonders and signs.

17.text: And she rendered to the just the wages of their labours, and conducted them in a wonderful way: and she was to them for a covert by day, and for the light of stars by night:

18.text: And she brought them through the Red Sea, and carried them over through a great water.

19.text: But their enemies she drowned in the sea, and from the depth of hell she brought them out. Therefore the just took the spoils of the wicked.

20.text: And they sung to thy holy name, O Lord, and they praised with one accord thy victorious hand.

21.text: For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of infants eloquent.

1.text: She prospered their works in the hands of the holy prophet.

2.text: They went through wildernesses that were not inhabited, and in desert places they pitched their tents.

3.text: They stood against their enemies, and revenged themselves of their adversaries.

4.text: They were thirsty, and they called upon thee, and water was given them out of the high rock, and a refreshment of their thirst out of the hard stone.

5.text: For by what things their enemies were punished, when their drink failed them, while the children of Israel abounded therewith and rejoiced: By the same things they in their need were benefited.

6.text: For instead of a fountain of an ever running river, thou gavest human blood to the unjust.

7.text: And whilst they were diminished for a manifest reproof of their murdering the infants, thou gavest to thine abundant water unlooked for:

8.text: shewing by the thirst that was then, how thou didst exalt thine, and didst kill their adversaries.

9.text: For when they were tried, and chastised with mercy, they knew how the wicked were judged with wrath and tormented.

10.text: For thou didst admonish and try them as a father: but the others, as a severe king, thou didst examine and condemn.

11.text: For whether absent or present, they were tormented alike.

12.text: For a double affliction came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past.

13.text: For when they heard that by their punishments the others were benefited, they remembered the Lord, wondering at the end of what was come to pass.

14.text: For whom they scorned before, when he was thrown out at the time of his being wickedly exposed to perish, him they admired in the end, when they saw the event: their thirsting being unlike to that of the just.

15.text: But for the foolish devices of their iniquity, because some being deceived worshipped dumb serpents and worthless beasts, thou didst send upon them a multitude of dumb beasts for vengeance.

16.text: That they might know that by what things a man sinneth, by the same also he is tormented.

17.text: For thy almighty hand, which made the world of matter without form, was not unable to send upon them a multitude of bears, or fierce lions,

18.text: Or unknown beasts of a new kind, full of rage: either breathing out a fiery vapour, or sending forth a stinking smoke, or shooting horrible sparks out of their eyes:

19.text: Whereof not only the hurt might be able to destroy them, but also the very sight might kill them through fear.

20.text: Yea and without these, they might have been slain with one blast, persecuted by their own deeds, and scattered by the breath of thy power: but thou hast ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.

21.text: For great power always belonged to thee alone: and who shall resist the strength of thy arm?

22.text: For the whole world before thee is as the least grain of the balance, and as a drop of the morning dew, that falleth down upon the earth:

23.text: But thou hast mercy upon all, because thou canst do all things, and overlookest the sins of men for the sake of repentance.

24.text: For thou lovest all things that are, and hatest none of the things which thou hast made: for thou didst not appoint, or make any thing hating it.

25.text: And how could any thing endure, if thou wouldst not? or be preserved, if not called by thee.

26.text: But thou sparest all: because they are thine, O Lord, who lovest souls.

1.text: O how good and sweet is thy spirit, O Lord, in all things!

2.text: And therefore thou chastisest them that err, by little and little: and admonishest them, and speakest to them, concerning the things wherein they offend: that leaving their wickedness, they may believe in thee, O Lord.

3.text: For those ancient inhabitants of thy holy land, whom thou didst abhor,

4.text: Because they did works hateful to thee by their sorceries, and wicked sacrifices,

5.text: And those merciless murderers of their own children, and eaters of men’s bowels, and devourers of blood from the midst of thy consecration,

6.text: And those parents sacrificing with their own hands helpless souls, it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our parents,

7.text: That the land which of all is most dear to thee might receive a worthy colony of the children of God.

8.text: Yet even those thou sparedst as men, and didst send wasps, forerunners of thy host, to destroy them by little and little.

9.text: Not that thou wast unable to bring the wicked under the just by war, or by cruel beasts, or with one rough word to destroy them at once:

10.text: But executing thy judgments by degrees thou gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a wicked generation, and their malice natural, and that their thought could never be changed.

11.text: For it was a cursed seed from the beginning: neither didst thou for fear of any one give pardon to their sins.

12.text: For who shall say to thee: What hast thou done? or who shall withstand thy judgment? or who shall come before thee to be a revenger of wicked men? or who shall accuse thee, if the nations perish, which thou hast made?

13.text: For there is no other God but thou, who hast care of all, that thou shouldst shew that thou dost not give judgment unjustly.

14.text: Neither shall king, nor tyrant in thy sight inquire about them whom thou hast destroyed.

15.text: For so much then as thou art just, thou orderest all things justly: thinking it not agreeable to thy power, to condemn him who deserveth not to be punished.

16.text: For thy power is the beginning of justice: and because thou art Lord of all, thou makest thyself gracious to all.

17.text: For thou shewest thy power, when men will not believe thee to be absolute in power, and thou convincest the boldness of them that know thee not.

18.text: But thou being master of power, judgest with tranquillity; and with great favour disposest of us: for thy power is at hand when thou wilt.

19.text: But thou hast taught thy people by such works, that they must be just and humane, and hast made thy children to be of a good hope: because in judging thou givest place for repentance for sins.

20.text: For if thou didst punish the enemies of thy servants, and that deserved to die, with so great deliberation, giving them time and place whereby they might be changed from their wickedness:

21.text: With what circumspection hast thou judged thy own children, to whose parents thou hast sworn and made covenants of good promises?

22.text: Therefore whereas thou chastisest us, thou scourgest our enemies very many ways, to the end that when we judge we may think on thy goodness: and when we are judged, we may hope for thy mercy.

23.text: Wherefore thou hast also greatly tormented them who in their life have lived foolishly and unjustly, by the same things which they worshipped.

24.text: For they went astray for a long time in the ways of error, holding those things for gods which are the most worthless among beasts, living after the manner of children without understanding.

25.text: Therefore thou hast sent a judgment upon them as senseless children to mock them.

26.text: But they that were not amended by mockeries and reprehensions, experienced the worthy judgment of God.

27.text: For seeing with indignation that they suffered by those very things which they took for gods, when they were destroyed by the same, they acknowledged him the true God, whom in time past they denied that they knew: for which cause the end also of their condemnation came upon them.

1.text: But all men are vain, in whom there is not the knowledge of God: and who by these good things that are seen, could not understand him that is, neither by attending to the works have acknowledged who was the workman:

2.text: But have imagined either the fire, or the wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the great water, or the sun and moon, to be the gods that rule the world.

3.text: With whose beauty, if they, being delighted, took them to be gods: let them know how much the Lord of them is more beautiful than they: for the first author of beauty made all those things.

4.text: Or if they admired their power and their effects, let them understand by them, that he that made them, is mightier than they:

5.text: For by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby.

6.text: But yet as to these they are less to be blamed. For they perhaps err, seeking God, and desirous to find him.

7.text: For being conversant among his works, they search: and they are persuaded that the things are good which are seen.

8.text: But then again they are not to be pardoned.

9.text: For if they were able to know so much as to make a judgment of the world: how did they not more easily find out the Lord thereof?

10.text: But unhappy are they, and their hope is among the dead, who have called gods the works of the hands of men, gold and silver, the inventions of art, and the resemblances of beasts, or an unprofitable stone the work of an ancient hand.

11.text: Or if an artist, a carpenter, hath cut down a tree proper for his use in the wood, and skillfully taken off all the bark thereof, and with his art, diligently formeth a vessel profitable for the common uses of life,

12.text: And useth the chips of his work to dress his meat:

13.text: And taking what was left thereof, which is good for nothing, being a crooked piece of wood, and full of knots, carveth it diligently when he hath nothing else to do, and by the skill of his art fashioneth it and maketh it like the image of a man:

14.text: Or the resemblance of some beast, laying it over with vermilion, and painting it red, and covering every spot that is in it:
