10.text: All these things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.

11.text: All things that are of the earth, shall return to the earth again, and all waters shall return to the sea.

12.text: All bribery, and injustice shall blotted out, and fidelity shall stand for ever.

13.text: The riches of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall pass away with a noise like a great thunder in rain.

14.text: While he openeth his hands he shall rejoice: but transgressors shall pine away in the end.

15.text: The offspring of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches, and make a noise as unclean roots upon the top of a rock.

16.text: The weed growing over every water, and at the bank of the river, shall be pulled up before all grass.

17.text: Grace is like a paradise in blessings, and mercy remaineth for ever.

18.text: The life of a labourer that is content with what he hath, shall be sweet, and in it thou shalt find a treasure.

19.text: Children, and the building of a city shall establish a name, but a blameless wife shall be counted above them both.

20.text: Wine and music rejoice the heart, but the love of wisdom is above them both.

21.text: The flute and the psaltery make a sweet melody, but a pleasant tongue is above them both.

22.text: Thy eye desireth favour and beauty, but more than these green sown fields.

23.text: A friend and companion meeting together in season, but above them both is a wife with her husband.

24.text: Brethren are a help in the time of trouble, but mercy shall deliver more than they.

25.text: Gold and silver make the feet stand sure: but wise counsel is above them both.

26.text: Riches and strength lift up the heart: but above these is the fear of the Lord. There is no want in the fear of the Lord, and it needeth not to seek for help.

27.text: The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and they have covered it above all glory.

28.text: My son, in thy lifetime be not indigent: for it is better to die than to want.

29.text: The life of him that looketh toward another man’s table is not to be counted a life: for he feedeth his soul with another man’s meat. But a man, well instructed and taught, will look to himself.

30.text: Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the unwise, but in his belly there shall burn a fire.

1.text: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that hath peace in his possessions! To a man that is at rest, and whose ways are prosperous in all things, and that is yet able to take meat!

2.text: O death, thy sentence is welcome to the man that is in need, and to him whose strength faileth: Who is in a decrepit age, and that is in care about all things, and to the distrustful that loseth patience!

3.text: Fear not the sentence of death. Remember what things have been before thee, and what shall come after thee: this sentence is from the Lord upon all flesh.

4.text: And what shall come upon thee by the good pleasure of the most High? Whether ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.

5.text: For among the dead there is no accusing of life. The children of sinners become children of abominations, and they that converse near the houses of the ungodly.

6.text: The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, and with their posterity shall be a perpetual reproach.

7.text: The children will complain of an ungodly father, because for his sake they are in reproach.

8.text: Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the most high Lord.

9.text: And if you be born, you shall be born in malediction: and if you die, in malediction shall be your portion.

10.text: All things that are of the earth, shall return into the earth: so the ungodly shall from malediction to destruction.

11.text: The mourning of men is about their body, but the name of the ungodly shall be blotted out.

12.text: Take care of a good name: for this shall continue with thee, more than a thousand treasures precious and great.

13.text: A good life hath its number of days: but a good name shall continue for ever.

14.text: My children, keep discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?

15.text: Better is the man that hideth his folly, than the man that hideth his wisdom.

16.text: Wherefore have a shame of these things I am now going to speak of. For it is not good to keep all shamefacedness: and all things do not please all men in opinion.

17.text: Be ashamed of fornication before father and mother: and of a lie before a governor and a man in power:

18.text: Of an offence before a prince, and a judge: of iniquity before a congregation and a people:

19.text: Of injustice before a companion and friend: and in regard to the place where thou dwellest, Of theft, and of the truth of God, and the covenant: of leaning with thy elbow over meat, and of deceit in giving and taking:

20.text: Of silence before them that salute thee: of looking upon a harlot: and of turning away thy face from thy kinsman.

21.text: Turn not away thy face from thy neighbour, and of taking away a portion and not restoring. Gaze not upon another man’s wife, and be not inquisitive after his handmaid, and approach not her bed.

22.text: Be ashamed of upbraiding speeches before friends: and after thou hast given, upbraid not.

23.text: Repeat not the word which thou hast heard, and disclose not the thing that is secret; so shalt thou be truly without confusion, and shall find favour before all men: be not ashamed of any of these things, and accept no person to sin thereby:

1.text: Repeat not the word which thou hast heard, and disclose not the thing that is secret; so shalt thou be truly without confusion, and shall find favour before all men: be not ashamed of any of these things, and accept no person to sin thereby:

2.text: Of the law of the most High, and of his covenant, and of judgment to justify the ungodly:

3.text: Of the affair of companions and travellers, and of the gift of the inheritance of friends:

4.text: Of exactness of balance and weights, of getting much or little:

5.text: Of the corruption of buying, and of merchants, and of much correction of children, and to make the side of a wicked slave to bleed.

6.text: Sure keeping is good over a wicked wife.

7.text: Where there are many hands, shut up, and deliver all things in number, and weight: and put all in writing that thou givest out or receivest in.

8.text: Be not ashamed to inform the unwise and foolish, and the aged, that are judged by young men: and thou shalt be well instructed in all things, and well approved in the sight of all men living.

9.text: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth, and the care for her taketh away his sleep, when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age, and when she is married, lest she should be hateful:

10.text: In her virginity, lest she should be corrupted, and be found with child in her father’s house: and having a husband, lest she should misbehave herself, or at the least become barren.

11.text: Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter: lest at any time she make thee become a laughingstock to thy enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and she make thee ashamed before all the multitude.

12.text: Behold not everybody’s beauty: and tarry not among women.

13.text: For from garments cometh a moth, and from a woman the iniquity of a man.

14.text: For better is the iniquity of a man, than a woman doing a good turn, and a woman bringing shame and reproach.

15.text: I will now remember the works of the Lord, and I will declare the things I have seen. By the words of the Lord are his works.

16.text: The sun giving light hath looked upon all things, and full of the glory of the Lord is his work.

17.text: Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works, which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established for his glory?

18.text: He hath searched out the deep, and the heart of men: and considered their crafty devices.

19.text: For the Lord knoweth all knowledge, and hath beheld the signs of the world, he declareth the things that are past, and the things that are to come, and revealeth the traces of hidden things.

20.text: No thought escapeth him, and no word can hide itself from him.

21.text: He hath beautified the glorious works of his wisdom: and he Is from eternity to eternity, and to him nothing may be added, Nor can he be diminished, and he hath no need of any counsellor.

22.text: O how desirable are all his works, and what we can know is but as a spark!

23.text: All these things live, and remain for ever, and for every use all things obey him.

24.text: All things are double, one against another, and he hath made nothing defective.

25.text: He hath established the good things of every one. And who shall be filled with beholding his glory?

1.text: The firmament on high is his beauty, the beauty of heaven with its glorious shew.

2.text: The sun when he appeareth shewing forth at his rising, an admirable instrument, the work of the most High.

3.text: At noon he burneth the earth, and who can abide his burning heat? As one keeping a furnace in the works of heat:

4.text: The sun three times as much, burneth the mountains, breathing out fiery vapours, and shining with his beams, he blindeth the eyes.

5.text: Great is the Lord that made him, and at his words he hath hastened his course.

6.text: And the moon in all in her season, is for a declaration of times and a sign of the world.

7.text: From the moon is the sign of the festival day, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.

8.text: The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her perfection. Being an instrument of the armies on high, shining gloriously in the Armament of heaven.

9.text: The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven; the Lord enlighteneth the world on high.

10.text: By the words of the holy one they shall stand in judgment, and shall never fail in their watches.

11.text: Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it: it is very beautiful in its brightness.

12.text: It encompasseth the heaven about with the circle of its glory, the hands of the most High have displayed it.

13.text: By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth forth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment.

14.text: Through this are the treasures opened, and the clouds fly out like birds.

15.text: By his greatness he hath fixed the clouds, and the hailstones are broken.

16.text: At his sight shall the mountains be shaken, and at his will the south wind shall blow.

17.text: The noise of his thunder shall strike the earth, so doth the northern storm, and the whirlwind: And as the birds lighting upon the earth, he scattereth snow, and the falling thereof, is as the coming down of locusts.

18.text: The eye admireth at the beauty of the whiteness thereof, and the heart is astonished at the shower thereof.

19.text: He shall pour frost as salt upon the earth: and when it freezeth, it shall become like the tops of thistles.

20.text: The cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into crystal; upon every gathering together of waters it shall rest, and shall clothe the waters as a breastplate.

21.text: And it shall devour the mountains, and burn the wilderness, and consume all that is green as with fire.

22.text: A present remedy of all is the speedy coming of a cloud, and a dew that meeteth it, by the heat that cometh, shall overpower it.

23.text: At his word the wind is still, and with his thought he appeaseth the deep, and the Lord hath planted islands therein.

24.text: Let them that sail on the sea, tell the dangers thereof: and when we hear with our ears, we shall admire.

25.text: There are great and wonderful works: a variety of beasts, and of all living things, and the monstrous creatures of whales.

26.text: Through him is established the end of their journey, and by his word all things are regulated.

27.text: We shall say much, and yet shall want words: but the sum of our words is, He is all.

28.text: What shall we be able to do to glorify him? for the Almighty himself is above all his works.

29.text: The Lord is terrible, and exceeding great, and his power is admirable.

30.text: Glorify the Lord as much as ever you can, for he will yet far exceed, and his magnificence is wonderful. Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can: for he is above all praise. When you exalt him put forth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can never go far enough.

31.text: Who shall see him, and declare him? and who shall magnify him as he is from the beginning?

32.text: There are many things hidden from us that are greater than these: for we have seen but a few of his works.

33.text: But the Lord hath made all things, and to the godly he hath given wisdom.

1.text: Let us now praise men of renown, and our fathers in their generation.

2.text: The Lord hath wrought great glory through his magnificence from the beginning.

3.text: Such as have borne rule in their dominions, men of great power, and endued with their wisdom, shewing forth in the prophets the dignity of prophets,

4.text: And ruling over the present people, and by the strength of wisdom instructing the people in most holy words.

5.text: Such as by their skill sought out musical tunes, and published canticles of the scriptures.

6.text: Rich men in virtue, studying beautifulness: living at peace in their houses.

7.text: All these have gained glory in their generations, and were praised in their days.

8.text: They that were born of them have left a name behind them, that their praises might be related:

9.text: And there are some, of whom there is no memorial: who are perished, as if they had never been: and are become as if they had never been born, and their children with them.

10.text: But these were men of mercy, whose godly deeds have not failed:

11.text: Good things continue with their seed, Their posterity are a holy inheritance, and their seed hath stood in the covenants.

13.text: And their children for their sakes remain for ever: their seed and their glory shall not be forsaken.

14.text: Their bodies are buried in peace, and their name liveth unto generation and generation.

15.text: Let the people shew forth their wisdom, and the church declare their praise.

16.text: Henoch pleased God, and was translated into paradise, that he may give repentance to the nations.

17.text: Noe was found perfect, just, and in the time of wrath he was made a reconciliation. Therefore was there a remnant left to the earth, when the flood came.

18.text: The covenants of the world were made with him, that all flesh should no more be destroyed with the flood.

19.text: Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations, and there was not found the like to him in glory, who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him.

20.text: In his flesh he established the covenant, and in temptation he was found faithful.

21.text: Therefore by an oath he gave him glory in his posterity, that he should increase as the dust of the earth, And that he would exalt his seed as the stars, and they should inherit from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.

22.text: And he did in like manner with Isaac for the sake of Abraham his father.

23.text: The Lord gave him the blessing of all nations, and confirmed his covenant upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessings, and gave him an inheritance, and divided him his portion in twelve tribes.

1.text: And he preserved for him men of mercy, that found grace in the eyes of all flesh. Moses was beloved of God, and men: whose memory is in benediction.

2.text: He made him like the saints in glory, and magnified him in the fear of his enemies, and with his words he made prodigies to cease.

3.text: He glorified him in the sight of kings, and gave him commandments in the sight of his people, and shewed him his glory.

4.text: He sanctified him in his faith, and meekness, and chose him out of all flesh.

5.text: For he heard him, and his voice, and brought him into a cloud. And he gave him commandments before his face, and a law of life and instruction, that he might teach Jacob his covenant, and Israel his judgments.

6.text: He exalted Aaron his brother, and like to himself of the tribe of Levi:

7.text: He made an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him the priesthood of the nation, and made him blessed in glory, And he girded him about with a glorious girdle, and clothed him with a robe of glory, and crowned him with majestic attire.

8.text: He put upon him a garment to the feet, and breeches, and as ephod, and he compassed him with many little bells of gold all round about,

9.text: He put upon him a garment to the feet, and breeches, and as ephod, and he compassed him with many little bells of gold all round about, That as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple, for a memorial to the children of his people.

10.text: He gave him a holy robe of gold, and blue, and purple, a woven work of a wise man, endued with judgment and truth:

11.text: Of twisted scarlet the work of an artist, with precious stones cut and set in gold, and graven by the work of a lapidary for a memorial, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

12.text: And a crown of gold upon his mitre wherein was engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour: a work of power, and delightful to the eyes for its beauty.

13.text: Before him there were none so beautiful, even from the beginning. No stranger was ever clothed with them, but only his children alone, and his grandchildren for ever.

14.text: His sacrifices were consumed with fire every day.

15.text: Moses filled his hands and anointed him with holy oil. This was made to him for an everlasting testament, and to his seed as the days of heaven, to execute the office of the priesthood, and to have praise, and to glorify his people in his name.

16.text: He chose him out of all men living, to offer sacrifice to God, incense, and a good savour, for a memorial to make reconciliation for his people:

17.text: And he gave him power in his commandments, in the covenants of his judgments, that he should teach Jacob his testimonies, and give light to Israel in his law.

18.text: And strangers stood up against him, and through envy the men that were with Dathan and Abiron, compassed him about in the wilderness, and the congregation of Core in their wrath.

19.text: The Lord God saw and it pleased him not, and they were consumed in his wrathful indignation. He wrought wonders upon them, and consumed them with a flame of fire.

20.text: And he added glory to Aaron, and gave him an inheritance, and divided unto him the firstfruits of the increase of the earth.

21.text: He prepared them bread in the first place unto fulness: for the sacrifices also of the Lord they shall eat, which he gave to him, and to his seed.

22.text: But he shall not inherit among the people in the land, and he hath no portion among the people: for he himself is his portion and inheritance.

23.text: Phinees the son of Eleazar is the third in glory, by imitating him in the fear of the Lord: And he stood up in the shameful fall of the people: in the goodness and readiness of his soul he appeased God for Israel.

24.text: Therefore he made to him a covenant of peace, to be the prince of the sanctuary, and of his people, that the dignity of priesthood should be to him and to his seed for ever.

26.text: And a covenant to David the king, the son of Jesse of the tribe of Juda, an inheritance to him and to his seed, that he might give wisdom into our heart to judge his people in justice, that their good things might not be abolished, and he made their glory in their nation everlasting.

1.text: Valiant in war was Jesus the son of Nave, who was successor of Moses among the prophets, who was great according to his name, Very great for the saving the elect of God, to overthrow the enemies that rose up against them, that he might get the inheritance for Israel.

2.text: How great glory did he gain when he lifted up his hands, and stretched out swords against the cities?

3.text: Who before him hath so resisted? for the Lord himself brought the enemies.

4.text: Was not the sun stopped in his anger, and one day made as two?

5.text: He called upon the most high Sovereign when the enemies assaulted him on every side, and the great and holy God heard him by hailstones of exceeding great force.

6.text: He made a violent assault against the nation of his enemies, and in the descent he destroyed the adversaries. That the nations might know his power, that it is not easy to fight against God. And he followed the mighty one:

7.text: And in the days of Moses he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephone, in standing against the enemy, and withholding the people from sins, and appeasing the wicked murmuring.

8.text: And they two being appointed, were delivered out of the danger from among the number of six hundred thousand men on foot, to bring them into their inheritance, into the land that floweth with milk and honey.

9.text: And the Lord gave strength also to Caleb, and his strength continued even to his old age, so that he went up to the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an inheritance:

10.text: That all the children of Israel might see, that it is good to obey the holy God.

11.text: Then all the judges, every one by name, whose heart was not corrupted: who turned not away from the Lord,

12.text: That their memory might be blessed, and their bones spring up out of their place, And their name continue for ever, the glory of the holy men remaining unto their children.

13.text: Samuel the prophet of the Lord, the beloved of the Lord his God, established a new government, and anointed princes over his people.

14.text: By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the God of Jacob beheld, and by his fidelity he was proved a prophet.

15.text: And he was known to be faithful in his words, because he saw the God of light:

16.text: And called upon the name of the Lord Almighty, in fighting against the enemies who beset him on every side, when he offered a lamb without blemish.

17.text: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.

18.text: And he crushed the princes of the Tyrians, and all the lords of the Philistines:

19.text: And before the time of the end of his life in the world, he protested before the Lord, and his anointed: money, or any thing else, even to a shoe, he had not taken of any man, and no man did accuse him.

20.text: And after this he slept, and he made known to the king, and shewed him the end of his life, and he lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy to blot out the wickedness of the nation.

1.text: Then Nathan the prophet arose in the days of David.

2.text: And as the fat taken away from the flesh, so was David chosen from among the children of Israel.

3.text: He played with lions as with lambs: and with bears he did in like manner as with the lambs of the flock, in his youth.

4.text: Did not he kill the giant, and take away reproach from his people? In lifting up his hand, with the stone in the sling he beat down the boasting of Goliath:

5.text: For he called upon the Lord the Almighty, and he gave strength in his right hand, to take away the mighty warrior, and to set up the horn of his nation.

6.text: So in ten thousand did he glorify him, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in offering to him a crown of glory:

7.text: For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and extirpated the Philistines the adversaries unto this day: he broke their horn for ever.

8.text: In all his works he gave thanks to the holy one, and to the most High, with words of glory. With his whole heart he praised the Lord, and loved God that made him: and he gave him power against his enemies:

9.text: And he set singers before the altar, and by their voices he made sweet melody.

10.text: And to the festivals he added beauty, and set in order the solemn times even to the end of his life, that they should praise the holy name of the Lord, and magnify the holiness of God in the morning.

11.text: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: and he gave him a covenant of the kingdom, and a throne of glory in Israel.

12.text: After him arose up a wise son, and for his sake he cast down all the power of the enemies.

13.text: Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God brought all his enemies under him, that he might build a house in his name, and prepare a sanctuary for ever: O how wise wast thou in thy youth!

14.text: Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God brought all his enemies under him, that he might build a house in his name, and prepare a sanctuary for ever: O how wise wast thou in thy youth! And thou wast filled as a river with wisdom, and thy soul covered the earth.

15.text: And thou wast filled as a river with wisdom, and thy soul covered the earth.

16.text: And thou didst multiply riddles in parables: thy name went abroad to the islands far off, and thou wast beloved in thy peace.

17.text: The countries wondered at thee for thy canticles, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations,

18.text: And at the name of the Lord God, whose surname is, God of Israel. Thou didst gather gold as copper, and didst multiply silver as lead,

19.text: And thou didst bow thyself to women: and by thy body thou wast brought under subjection.

20.text: Thou hast stained thy glory, and defiled thy seed so as to bring wrath upon thy children, and to have thy folly kindled,

21.text: That thou shouldst make the kingdom to be divided, and out of Ephraim a rebellious kingdom to rule.

22.text: But God will not leave off his mercy, and he will not destroy, nor abolish his own works, neither will he cut up by the roots the offspring of his elect: and he will not utterly take away the seed of him that loveth the Lord. Wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and to David of the same stock.

23.text: And Solomon had an end with his fathers. And he left behind him of his seed, the folly of the nation, Even Roboam that had little wisdom, who turned away the people through his counsel:

24.text: And Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin, and their sins were multiplied exceedingly. They removed them far away from their land.

25.text: And they sought out all iniquities, till vengeance came upon them, and put an end to all their sins.

1.text: And Elias the prophet stood up, as a fire, and his word burnt like a torch.

2.text: He brought a famine upon them, and they that provoked him in their envy, were reduced to a small number, for they could not endure the commandments of the Lord.

3.text: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and he brought down fire from heaven thrice.

4.text: Thus was Elias magnified in his wondrous works. And who can glory like to thee?

5.text: Who raisedst up a dead man from below, from the lot of death, by the word of the Lord God.

6.text: Who broughtest down kings to destruction, and brokest easily their power in pieces, and the glorious from their bed.

7.text: Who heardest judgment in Sina, and in Horeb the judgments of vengeance.

8.text: Who anointedst kings to penance, and madest prophets successors after thee.

9.text: Who wast taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.

10.text: Who art registered in the judgments of times to appease the wrath of the Lord, to reconcile the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

11.text: Blessed are they that saw thee, and were honoured with thy friendship. For we live only in our life, but after death our name shall not be such.

12.text: Elias was indeed covered with the whirlwind, and his spirit was filled up in Eliseus: in his days he feared not the prince, and no man was more powerful than he.

13.text: No word could overcome him, and after death his body prophesied.

14.text: In his life he did great wonders, and is death he wrought miracles.

15.text: For all this the people repented not, neither did they depart from their sins till they were cast out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth. And there was left but a small people, and a prince in the house of David.

16.text: Some of these did that which pleased God: but others committed many sins.

17.text: Ezechias fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof, and he digged a rock with iron, and made a well for water.

18.text: In his days Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabsaces, and lifted up his hand against them, and he stretched out his hand against Sion, and became proud through his power.

19.text: Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they were in pain as women in travail.

20.text: And they called upon the Lord who is merciful, and spreading their hands, they lifted them up to heaven: and the holy Lord God quickly heard their voice. He was not mindful of their sins, neither did he deliver them up to their enemies, but he purified them by the hand of Isaias, the holy prophet.

21.text: He overthrew the army of the Assyrians, and the angel of the Lord destroyed them.

22.text: For Ezechias did that which pleased God, and walked valiantly in the way of David his father, which Isaias, the great prophet, and faithful in the sight of God, had commanded him.

23.text: In his days the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king’s life.

24.text: With a great spirit he saw the things that are to come to pass at last, and comforted the mourners in Sion.

25.text: He shewed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things before they came.

1.text: The memory of Josias is like the composition of a sweet smell made by the art of a perfumer: His remembrance shall be sweet as honey in every mouth, and as music at a banquet of wine.

2.text: He was directed by God unto the repentance of the nation, and he took away the abominations of wickedness.

3.text: And he directed his heart towards the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened godliness.

4.text: Except David, and Ezechias, and Josias, all committed sin. For the kings of Juda forsook the law of the most High, and despised the fear of God.

5.text: So they gave their kingdom to others, and their glory to a strange nation.

6.text: They burnt the chosen city of holiness, and made the streets thereof desolate according to the prediction of Jeremias.

7.text: For they treated him evil, who was consecrated a prophet from his mother’s womb, to overthrow, and pluck up, and destroy, and to build again, and renew.

8.text: It was Ezechiel that saw the glorious vision, which was shewn him upon the chariot of cherubims.

9.text: For he made mention of the enemies under the figure of rain, and of doing good to them that shewed right ways.

10.text: And may the bones of the twelve prophets spring up out of their place: for they strengthened Jacob, and redeemed themselves by strong faith.

11.text: How shall we magnify Zorobabel? for he was as a signet on the right hand;

12.text: In like manner Jesus the son of Josedec? who in their days built the house, and set up a holy temple to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.

13.text: And let Nehemias be a long time remembered, who raised up for us our walls that were cast down, and set up the gates and the bars, who rebuilt our houses.

14.text: No man was born upon earth like Henoch: for he also was taken up from the earth.

15.text: Nor as Joseph, who was a man born prince of his brethren, the support of his family, the ruler of his brethren, the stay of the people: And his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied.

16.text: Seth and Sem obtained glory among men: and above every soul Adam in the beginning.

1.text: Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life propped up the house, and in his days fortified the temple.

2.text: By him also the height of the temple was founded, the double building and the high walls of the temple.

3.text: In his days the wells of water flowed out, and they were filled as the sea above measure.

4.text: He took care of his nation, and delivered it from destruction.

5.text: He prevailed to enlarge the city, and obtained glory in his conversation with the people: and enlarged the entrance of the house and the court.

6.text: He shone in his days as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full.

7.text: And as the sun when it shineth, so did he shine in the temple of God.

8.text: And as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds, and as the flower of roses in the days of the spring, and as the lilies that are on the brink of the water, and as the sweet smelling frankincense in the time of summer.

9.text: As a bright fire, and frankincense burning in the fire. As a massy vessel of gold, adorned with every precious stone.

10.text: As an olive tree budding forth, and a cypress tree rearing itself on high, when he put on the robe of glory, and was clothed with the perfection of power.

11.text: When he went up to the holy altar, he honoured the vesture of holiness.

12.text: And when he took the portions out of the hands of the priests, he himself stood by the altar. And about him was the ring of his brethren: and as the cedar planted in mount Libanus, And as branches of palm trees, they stood round about him, and all the sons of Aaron in their glory.

13.text: And the oblation of the Lord was in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel: and finishing his service, on the altar, to honour the offering of the most high King,

14.text: And the oblation of the Lord was in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel: and finishing his service, on the altar, to honour the offering of the most high King,

15.text: He stretched forth his hand to make a libation, and offered of the blood of the grape. He poured out at the foot of the altar a divine odour to the most high Prince.

16.text: Then the sons of Aaron shouted, they sounded with beaten trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard for a remembrance before God.

17.text: Then all the people together made haste, and fell down to the earth upon their faces, to adore the Lord their God, and to pray to the Almighty God the most High.

18.text: And the singers lifted up their voices. and in the great house the sound of sweet melody was increased.

19.text: And the people in prayer besought the Lord the most High, until the worship of the Lord was perfected, and they had finished their office.

20.text: Then coming down, he lifted up his hands over all the congregation of the children of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips, and to glory in his name:

21.text: And he repeated his prayer, willing to shew the power of God.

22.text: And now pray ye to the God of all, who hath done great things in all the earth, who hath increased our days from our mother’s womb, and hath done with us according to his mercy.

23.text: May he grant us joyfulness of heart, and that there be peace in our days in Israel for ever:

24.text: That Israel may believe that the mercy of God is with us, to deliver us in his days.

25.text: There are two nations which my soul abhorreth: and the third is no nation, which I hate:

26.text: They that sit on mount Seir, and the Philistines, and the foolish people that dwell in Sichem.

27.text: Jesus the son of Sirach, of Jerusalem, hath written in this book the doctrine of wisdom and instruction, who renewed wisdom from his heart.

28.text: Blessed is he that is conversant in these good things: and he that layeth them up in his heart, shall be wise always.

29.text: For if he do them, he shall be strong to do all things: because the light of God guideth his steps.

1.text: A prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour.

2.text: I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me. And hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou hast been my helper.

3.text: And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about:

4.text: From the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt.

5.text: From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from a slanderous tongue:

6.text: My soul shall praise the Lord even to death. And my life was drawing near to hell beneath.

7.text: They compassed me on every side, and there was no one that would help me. I looked for the succour of men, and there was none.

8.text: I remembered thy mercy, O Lord, and thy works, which are from the beginning of the world. How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations.

9.text: Thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away.

10.text: I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

11.text: I will praise thy name continually, and will praise it with thanksgiving, and my prayer was heard.

12.text: And thou hast saved me from destruction, and hast delivered me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks, and praise thee, and bless the name of the Lord.

13.text: When I was yet young, before I wandered about, I sought for wisdom openly in my prayer.

14.text: I prayed for her before the temple, and unto the very end I will seek after her, and she flourished as a grape soon ripe.

15.text: My heart delighted in her, my foot walked in the right way, from my youth up I sought after her.

16.text: I bowed down my ear a little, and received her.

17.text: I found much wisdom in myself, and I profited much therein. To him that giveth me wisdom, will I give glory.

18.text: For I have determined to follow her: I have had a zeal for good, and shall not be confounded.

19.text: My soul hath wrestled for her, and in doing it I have been confirmed. I stretched forth my hands on high, and I bewailed my ignorance of her.

20.text: I directed my soul to her, and in knowledge I found her. I possessed my heart with her from the beginning: therefore I shall not be forsaken.

21.text: My entrails were troubled in seeking her: therefore shall I possess a good possession.

22.text: The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward: and with it I will praise him.

23.text: Draw near to me, ye unlearned, and gather yourselves together into the house of discipline.

24.text: Why are ye slow? and what do you say of these things? your souls are exceeding thirsty.

25.text: I have opened my mouth, and have spoken: buy her for yourselves without silver,

26.text: And submit your neck to the yoke, and let your soul receive discipline: for she is near at hand to be found.

27.text: Behold with your eyes how I have laboured a little, and have found much rest to myself.

28.text: Receive ye discipline as a great sum of money, and possess abundance of gold by her.

29.text: Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and you shall not be confounded in his praise.

30.text: Work your work before the time, and he will give you your reward in his time.

1.text: Aleph. How doth the city sit solitary that was full of people! how is the mistress of the Gentiles become as a widow: the princes of provinces made tributary!

2.text: Beth. Weeping she hath wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: there is none to comfort her among all them that were dear to her: all her friends have despised her, and are become her enemies.

3.text: Ghimel. Juda hath removed her dwelling place because of her affliction, and the greatness of her bondage: she hath dwelt among the nations, and she hath found no rest: all her persecutors have taken her in the midst of straits.

4.text: Daleth. The ways of Sion mourn, because there are none that come to the solemn feast: all her gates are broken down: her priests sigh: her virgins are in affliction, and she is oppressed with bitterness.

5.text: He. Her adversaries are become her lords, her enemies are enriched: because the Lord hath spoken against her for the multitude of her iniquities: her children are led into captivity: before the face of the oppressor.

6.text: Vau. And from the daughter of Sion all her beauty is departed: her princes are become like rams that find no pastures: and they are gone away without strength before the face of the pursuer.

7.text: Zain. Jerusalem hath remembered the days of her affliction, and prevarication of all her desirable things which she had from the days of old, when her people fell in the enemy’s hand, and there was no helper: the enemies have seen her, and have mocked at her sabbaths.

8.text: Heth. Jerusalem hath grievously sinned, therefore is she become unstable: all that honoured her have despised her, because they have seen her shame: but she sighed and turned backward.

9.text: Teth. Her filthiness is on her feet, and she hath not remembered her end: she is wonderfully cast down, not having a comforter: behold, O Lord, my affliction, because the enemy is lifted up.

10.text: Jod. The enemy hath put out his hand to all her desirable things: for she hath seen the Gentiles enter into her sanctuary, of whom thou gavest commandment that they should not enter into thy church.

11.text: Caph. All her people sigh, they seek bread: they have given all their precious things for food to relieve the soul: see, O Lord, and consider, for I am become vile.

12.text: Lamed. O all ye that pass by the way, attend, and see if there be any sorrow like to my sorrow: for he hath made a vintage of me, as the Lord spoke in the day of his fierce anger.

13.text: Mem. From above he hath sent fire into my bones, and hath chastised me: he hath spread a net for my feet, he hath turned me back: he hath made me desolate, wasted with sorrow all the day long.

14.text: Nun. The yoke of my iniquities hath watched: they are folded together in his hand, and put upon my neck: my strength is weakened: the Lord hath delivered me into a hand out of which I am not able to rise.

15.text: Samech. The Lord hath taken away all my mighty men out of the midst of me: he hath called against me the time, to destroy my chosen men: the Lord hath trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Juda.

16.text: Ain. Therefore do I weep, and my eyes run down with water: because the comforter, the relief of my soul, is far from me: my children are desolate because the enemy hath prevailed.

17.text: Phe. Sion hath spread forth her hands, there is none to comfort her: the Lord hath commanded against Jacob, his enemies are round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among them.

18.text: Sade. The Lord is just, for I have provoked his mouth to wrath: hear, I pray you, all ye people, and see my sorrow: my virgins, and my young men are gone into captivity.

19.text: Coph. I called for my friends, but they deceived me: my priests and my ancients pined away in the city: while they sought their food, to relieve their souls.

20.text: Res. Behold, O Lord, for I am in distress, my bowels are troubled: my heart is turned within me, for I am full of bitterness: abroad the sword destroyeth, and at home there is death alike.

21.text: Sin. They have heard that I sigh, and there is none to comfort me: all my enemies have heard of my evil, they have rejoiced that thou hast done it: thou hast brought a day of consolation, and they shall be like unto me.

22.text: Thau. Let all their evil be present before thee: and make vintage of them, as thou hast made vintage of me for all my iniquities: for my sighs are many, and my heart is sorrowful.

1.text: Aleph. How hath the Lord covered with obscurity the daughter of Sion in his wrath! how hath he cast down from heaven to the earth the glorious one of Israel, and hath not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger!

2.text: Beth. The Lord hath cast down headlong, and hath not spared, all that was beautiful in Jacob: he hath destroyed in his wrath the strong holds of the virgin of Juda, and brought them down to the ground: he hath made the kingdom unclean, and the princes thereof.

3.text: Ghimel. He hath broken in his fierce anger all the horn of Israel: he hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy: and he hath kindled in Jacob as it were a flaming fire devouring round about.

4.text: Daleth. He hath bent his bow as an enemy, he hath fixed his right hand as an adversary: and he hath killed all that was fair to behold in the tabernacle of the daughter of Sion, he hath poured out his indignation like fire.

5.text: He. The Lord is become as an enemy: he hath cast down Israel headlong, he hath overthrown all the walls thereof: he hath destroyed his strong holds, and hath multiplied in the daughter of Juda the afflicted, both men and women.

6.text: Vau. And he hath destroyed his tent as a garden, he hath thrown down his tabernacle: the Lord hath caused feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Sion: and hath delivered up king and priest to reproach, and to the indignation of his wrath.

7.text: Zain. The Lord hath cast off his altar, he hath cursed his sanctuary: he hath delivered the walls of the towers thereof into the hand of the enemy: they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn feast.

8.text: Heth. The Lord hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Sion: he hath stretched out his line, and hath not withdrawn his hand from destroying: and the bulwark hath mourned, and the wall hath been destroyed together.

9.text: Teth. Her gates are sunk into the ground: he hath destroyed, and broken her bars: her king and her princes are among the Gentiles: the law is no more, and her prophets have found no vision from the Lord.

10.text: Jod. The ancients of the daughter of Sion sit upon the ground, they have held their peace: they have sprinkled their heads with dust, they are girded with haircloth, the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

11.text: Caph. My eyes have failed with weeping, my bowels are troubled: my liver is poured out upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my people, when the children, and the sucklings, fainted away in the streets of the city.

12.text: Lamed. They said to their mothers: Where is corn and wine? when they fainted away as the wounded in the streets of the city: when they breathed out their souls in the bosoms of their mothers.

13.text: Mem. To what shall I compare thee? or to what shall I liken thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? to what shall I equal thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Sion? for great as the sea is thy destruction: who shall heal thee?

14.text: Nun. Thy prophets have seen false and foolish things for thee: and they have not laid open thy iniquity, to excite thee to penance: but they have seen for thee false revelations and banishments.

15.text: Samech. All they that passed by the way have clapped their hands at thee: they have hissed, and wagged their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying: Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of all the earth?

16.text: Phe. All thy enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they have hissed, and gnashed with the teeth, and have said: We will swallow her up: lo, this is the day which we looked for: we have found it, we have seen it.

17.text: Ain. The Lord hath done that which he purposed, he hath fulfilled his word, which he commanded in the days of old: he hath destroyed, and hath not spared, and he hath caused the enemy to rejoice over thee, and hath set up the horn of thy adversaries.

18.text: Sade. Their heart cried to the Lord upon the walls of the daughter of Sion: Let tears run down like a torrent day and night: give thyself no rest, and let not the apple of thy eye cease.

19.text: Coph. Arise, give praise in the night, in the beginning of the watches: pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands to him for the life of thy little children, that have fainted for hunger at the top of all the streets.

20.text: Res. Behold, O Lord, and consider whom thou hast thus dealt with: shall women then eat their own fruit, their children of a span long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?

21.text: Sin. The child and the old man lie without on the ground: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword: thou hast slain them in the day of thy wrath: thou hast killed, and shewn them no pity.

22.text: Thau. Thou hast called as to a festival, those that should terrify me round about, and there was none in the day of the wrath of the Lord that escaped and was left: those that I brought up, and nourished, my enemy hath consumed them.

1.text: Aleph. I am the man that see my poverty by the rod of his indignation.

2.text: Aleph. He hath led me, and brought me into darkness, and not into light.

3.text: Aleph. Only against me he hath turned, and turned again his hand all the day.

4.text: Beth. My skin and my flesh he hath made old, he hath broken my bones.

5.text: Beth. He hath built round about me, and he hath compassed me with gall and labour.

6.text: Beth. He hath set me in dark places as those that are dead for ever.

7.text: Ghimel. He hath built against me round about, that I may not get out: he hath made my fetters heavy.

8.text: Ghimel. Yea, and when I cry, and entreat, he hath shut out my prayer.

9.text: Ghimel. He hath shut up my ways with square stones, he hath turned my paths upside down.

10.text: Daleth. He is become to me as a bear lying in wait: as a lion in secret places.

11.text: Daleth. He hath turned aside my paths, and hath broken me in pieces, he hath made me desolate.

12.text: Daleth. He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for his arrows.

13.text: He. He hath shot into my reins the daughters of his quiver.

14.text: He. I am made a derision to all my people, their song all the day long.

15.text: He. He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath inebriated me with wormwood.

16.text: Vau. And he hath broken my teeth one by one, he hath fed me with ashes.

17.text: Vau. And my soul is removed far off from peace, I have forgotten good things.

18.text: Vau. And I said: My end and my hope is perished from the Lord.

19.text: Zain. Remember my poverty, and transgression, the wormwood, and the gall.

20.text: Zain. I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me.

21.text: Zain. These things I shall think over in my heart, therefore will I hope.

22.text: Heth. The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed.

23.text: Heth. They are new every morning, great is thy faithfulness.

24.text: Heth. The Lord is my portion, said my soul: therefore will I wait for him.

25.text: Teth. The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him.

26.text: Teth. It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of God.

27.text: Teth. It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke from his youth.

28.text: Jod. He shall sit solitary, and hold his peace: because he hath taken it up upon himself.

29.text: Jod. He shall put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.

30.text: Jod. He shall give his cheek to him that striketh him, he shall be filled with reproaches.

31.text: Caph. For the Lord will not cast off for ever.

32.text: Caph. For if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies.

33.text: Caph. For he hath not willingly afflicted, nor cast off the children of men.

34.text: Lamed. To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the land,

35.text: Lamed. To turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the most High,

36.text: Lamed. To destroy a man wrongfully in his judgment, the Lord hath not approved.

37.text: Mem. Who is he that hath commanded a thing to be done, when the Lord commandeth it not?

38.text: Mem. Shall not both evil and good proceed out of the mouth of the Highest?

39.text: Mem. Why hath a living man murmured, man suffering for his sins?

40.text: Nun. Let us search our ways, and seek, and return to the Lord.

41.text: Nun. Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens.

42.text: Nun. We have done wickedly, and provoked thee to wrath: therefore thou art inexorable.

43.text: Samech. Thou hast covered in thy wrath, and hast struck us: thou hast killed and hast not spared.

44.text: Samech. Thou hast set a cloud before thee, that our prayer may not pass through.

45.text: Samech. Thou hast made me as an outcast, and refuse in the midst of the people.

46.text: Phe. All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.

47.text: Phe. Prophecy is become to us a fear, and a snare, and destruction.

48.text: Phe. My eye hath run down with streams of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

49.text: Ain. My eye is afflicted, and hath not been quiet, because there was no rest:

50.text: Ain. Till the Lord regarded and looked down from the heavens.

51.text: Ain. My eye hath wasted my soul because of all the daughters of my city.

52.text: Sade. My enemies have chased me and caught me like a bird, without cause.

53.text: Sade. My life is fallen into the pit, and they have laid a stone over me.

54.text: Sade. Waters have flowed over my head: I said: I am cut off.

55.text: Coph. I have called upon thy name, O Lord, from the lowest pit.

56.text: Coph. Thou hast heard my voice: turn not away thy ear from my sighs, and cries.

57.text: Coph. Thou drewest near in the day, when I called upon thee, thou saidst: Fear not.

58.text: Res. Thou hast judged, O Lord, the cause of my soul, thou the Redeemer of my life.

59.text: Res. Thou hast seen, O Lord, their iniquity against me: judge thou my judgment.

60.text: Res. Thou hast seen all their fury, and all their thoughts against me.

61.text: Sin. Thou hast heard their reproach, O Lord, all their imaginations against me.

62.text: Sin. The lips of them that rise up against me: and their devices against me all the day.

63.text: Sin. Behold their sitting down, and their rising up, I am their song.

64.text: Thau. Thou shalt render them a recompense, O Lord, according to the works of their hands.

65.text: Thau. Thou shalt give them a buckler of heart, thy labour.

66.text: Thau. Thou shalt persecute them in anger, and shalt destroy them from under the heavens, O Lord.

1.text: Aleph. How is the gold become dim, the finest colour is changed, the stones of the sanctuary are scattered in the top of every street?

2.text: Beth. The noble sons of Sion, and they that were clothed with the best gold: how are they esteemed as earthen vessels, the work of the potter’s hands?

3.text: Ghimel. Even the sea monsters have drawn out the breast, they have given suck to their young: the daughter of my people is cruel, like the ostrich in the desert.

4.text: Daleth. The tongue of the sucking child hath stuck to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the little ones have asked for bread, and there was none to break it unto them.

5.text: He. They that were fed delicately have died in the streets; they that were brought up in scarlet have embraced the dung.

6.text: Vau. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people is made greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and hands took nothing in her.

7.text: Zain. Her Nazarites were whiter than snow, purer than milk, more ruddy than the old ivory, fairer than the sapphire.

8.text: Heth. Their face is now made blacker than coals, and they are not known in the streets: their skin hath stuck to their bones, it is withered, and is become like wood.

9.text: Teth. It was better with them that were slain by the sword, than with them that died with hunger: for these pined away being consumed for want of the fruits of the earth.

10.text: Jod. The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

11.text: Caph. The Lord hath accomplished his wrath, he hath poured out his fierce anger: and he hath kindled a fire in Sion, and it hath devoured the foundations thereof.

12.text: Lamed. The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed, that the adversary and the enemy should enter in by the gates of Jerusalem.

13.text: Mem. For the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her.

14.text: Nun. They have wandered as blind men in the streets, they were defiled with blood: and when they could not help walking in it, they held up their skirts.

15.text: Samech. Depart you that are defiled, they cried out to them: Depart, get ye hence, touch not: for they quarrelled, and being removed, they said among the Gentiles: He will no more dwell among them.

16.text: Phe. The face of the Lord hath divided them, he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, neither had they pity on the ancient.

17.text: Ain. While we were yet standing, our eyes failed, expecting help for us in vain, when we looked attentively towards a nation that was not able to save.

18.text: Sade. Our steps have slipped in the way of our streets, our end draweth near: our days are fulfilled, for our end is come.

19.text: Coph. Our persecutors were swifter than the eagles of the air: they pursued us upon the mountains, they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.

20.text: Res. The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins: to whom we said: Under thy shadow we shall live among the Gentiles.

21.text: Sin. Rejoice, and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Hus: to thee also shall the cup come, thou shalt be made drunk, and naked.

22.text: Thau. Thy iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Sion, he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he visited thy iniquity, O daughter of Edom, he hath discovered thy sins.

1.text: Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider and behold our reproach.

2.text: Our inheritance is turned to aliens: our houses to strangers.

3.text: We are become orphans without a father: our mothers are as widows.

4.text: We have drunk our water for money: we have bought our wood.

5.text: We were dragged by the necks, we were weary and no rest was given us.

6.text: We have given our hand to Egypt, and to the Assyrians, that we might be satisfied with bread.

7.text: Our fathers have sinned, and are not: and we have borne their iniquities.

8.text: Servants have ruled over us: there was none to redeem us out of their hand.

9.text: We fetched our bread at the peril of our lives, because of the sword in the desert.

10.text: Our skin was burnt as an oven, by reason of the violence of the famine.

11.text: They oppressed the women in Sion, and the virgins in the cities of Juda.

12.text: The princes were hanged up by their hand: they did not respect the persons of the ancient.

13.text: They abused the young men indecently: and the children fell under the wood.

14.text: The ancients have ceased from the gates: the young men from the choir of the singers.

15.text: The joy of our heart is ceased, our dancing is turned into mourning.

16.text: The crown is fallen from our head: woe to us, because we have sinned.

17.text: Therefore is our heart sorrowful, therefore are our eyes become dim,

18.text: For mount Sion, because it is destroyed, foxes have walked upon it.

19.text: But thou, O Lord, shalt remain for ever, thy throne from generation to generation.

20.text: Why wilt thou forget us for ever? why wilt thou forsake us for a long time?

21.text: Convert us, O Lord, to thee, and we shall be converted: renew our days, as from the beginning.

22.text: But thou hast utterly rejected us, thou art exceedingly angry against us.

1.text: The word of the Lord, that came to Osee the son of Beeri, in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias kings of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel.

2.text: The beginning of the Lord’s speaking by Osee: and the Lord said to Osee: Go, take thee a wife of fornications, and have of her children of fornications: for the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord.

3.text: So he went, and took Gomer the daughter of Debelaim: and she conceived and bore him a son.

4.text: And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezrahel: for yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezrahel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.

5.text: And in that day I will break in pieces the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezrahel.

6.text: And she conceived again, and bore a daughter, and he said to him: Call her name, Without mercy: for I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them.

7.text: And I will have mercy on the house of Juda, and I will save them by the Lord their God: and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, nor by horses, nor by horsemen.

8.text: And she weaned her that was called Without mercy. And she conceived, and bore a son.

9.text: And he said: Call his name, Not my people: for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.

10.text: And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, that is without measure, and shall not be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God.

11.text: And the children of Juda, and the children of Israel shall be gathered together: and they shall appoint themselves one head, and shall come up out of the land: for great is the day of Jezrahel.

1.text: Say ye to your brethren: You are my people, and to your sister: Thou hast obtained mercy.

2.text: Judge your mother, judge her: because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts.

3.text: Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born: and I will make her as a wilderness, and will set her as a land that none can pass through, and will kill her with drought.

4.text: And I will not have mercy on her children: for they are the children of fornications.

5.text: For their mother hath committed fornication, she that conceived them is covered with shame: for she said: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, my oil, and my drink.

6.text: Wherefore behold I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths.

7.text: And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, and shall not find, and she shall say: I will go, and return to my first husband, because it was better with me then, than now.

8.text: And she did not know that I gave her corn and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver, and gold, which they have used in the service of Baal.

9.text: Therefore will I return, and take away my corn in its season, and my wine in its season, and I will set at liberty my wool, and my flax, which covered her disgrace.

10.text: And now I will lay open her folly in the eyes of her lovers: and no man shall deliver her out of my hand:

11.text: And I will cause all her mirth to cease, her solemnities, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her festival times.

12.text: And I will destroy her vines, and her fig trees, of which she said: These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me: and I will make her as a forest, and the beasts of the field shall devour her.

13.text: And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim, to whom she burnt incense, and decked herself out with her earrings, and with her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, saith the Lord.

14.text: Therefore, behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart.

15.text: And I will give her vinedressers out of the same place, and the valley of Achor for an opening of hope: and she shall sing there according to the days of her youth, and according to the days of her coming up out of the land of Egypt.

16.text: And it shall be in that day, saith the Lord, That she shall call me: My husband, and she shall call me no more Baali.

17.text: And I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and she shall no more remember their name.

18.text: And in that day I will make a covenant with them, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air, and with the creeping things of the earth: and I will destroy the bow, and the sword, and war out of the land: and I will make them sleep secure.

19.text: And I will espouse thee to me for ever: and I will espouse thee to me in justice, and judgment, and in mercy, and in commiserations.

20.text: And I will espouse thee to me in faith: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.

21.text: And it shall come to pass in that day: I will hear, saith the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.

22.text: And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil, and these shall hear Jezrahel.

23.text: And I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercy on her that was without mercy. And I will say to that which was not my people: Thou art my people: and they shall say: Thou art my God.

1.text: And the Lord said to me: Go yet again, and love a woman beloved of her friend, and an adulteress: as the Lord loveth the children of Israel, and they look to strange gods, and love the husks of the grapes.

2.text: And I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for a core of barley, and for half a core of barley.

3.text: And I said to her: Thou shalt wait for me many days: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be no man’s, and I also will wait for thee.

4.text: For the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim.

5.text: And after this the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the Lord their God, and David their king: and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness in the last days.

1.text: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel, for the Lord shall enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the land: for there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land.

2.text: Cursing, and lying, and killing, and theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood hath touched blood.

3.text: Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth in it shall languish with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air: yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be gathered together.

4.text: But yet let not any man judge: and let not a man be rebuked: for thy people are as they that contradict the priest.

5.text: And thou shalt fall today, and the prophet also shall fall with thee: in the night I have made thy mother to be silent.

6.text: My people have been silent, because they had no knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me: and thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I also will forget thy children.

7.text: According to the multitude of them so have they sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame.

8.text: They shall eat the sins of my people, and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity.

9.text: And there shall be like people like priest: and I will visit their ways upon them, and I will repay them their devices.

10.text: And they shall eat and shall not be filled: they have committed fornication, and have not ceased: because they have forsaken the Lord in not observing his law.

11.text: Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness take away the understanding.

12.text: My people have consulted their stocks, and their staff hath declared unto them: for the spirit of fornication hath deceived them, and they have committed fornication against their God.

13.text: They offered sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burnt incense upon the hills: under the oak, and the poplar, and the turpentine tree, because the shadow thereof was good: therefore shall your daughters commit fornication, and your spouses shall be adulteresses.

14.text: I will not visit upon your daughters when they shall commit fornication, and upon your spouses when they shall commit adultery: because themselves conversed with harlots, and offered sacrifice with the effeminate, and the people that doth not understand shall be beaten.

15.text: If thou play the harlot, O Israel, at least let not Juda offend: and go ye not into Galgal, and come not up into Bethaven, and do not swear: The Lord liveth.

16.text: For Israel hath gone astray like a wanton heifer: now will the Lord feed them, as a lamb in a spacious place.

17.text: Ephraim is a partaker with idols, let him alone.

18.text: Their banquet is separated, they have gone astray by fornication: they that should have protected them have loved to bring shame upon them.

19.text: The wind hath bound them up in its wings, and they shall be confounded because of their sacrifices.

1.text: Hear ye this, O priests, and hearken, O ye house of Israel, and give ear, O house of the king: for there is a judgment against you, because you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over, and a net spread upon Thabor.

2.text: And you have turned aside victims into the depth: and I am, the teacher of them all.

3.text: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now Ephraim hath committed fornication, Israel is defiled.

4.text: They will not set their thoughts to return to their God: for the spirit of fornication is in the midst of them, and they have not known the Lord.

5.text: And the pride of Israel shall answer in his face: and Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity, Juda also shall fall with them.

6.text: With their flocks, and with their herds, they shall go to seek the Lord, and shall not find him: he is withdrawn from them.

7.text: They have transgressed against the Lord, for they have begotten children that are strangers: now shall a month devour them with their portions.

8.text: Blow ye the cornet in Gabaa, the trumpet in Rama: howl ye in Bethaven, behind thy back, O Benjamin.

9.text: Ephraim shall be in desolation in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel I have shewn that which shall surely be.

10.text: The princes of Juda are become as they that take up the bound: I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.

11.text: Ephraim is under oppression, and broken in judgment: because he began to go after filthiness.

12.text: And I will be like a moth to Ephraim: and like rottenness to the house of Juda.

13.text: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Juda his band: and Ephraim went to the Assyrian, and sent to the avenging king: and he shall not be able to heal you, neither shall he be able to take off the band from you.

14.text: For I will be like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion’s whelp to the house of Juda: I, I will catch, and go: I will take away, and there is none that can rescue.

15.text: I will go and return to my place: until you are consumed, and seek my face.

1.text: In their affliction they will rise early to me: Come, and let us return to the Lord: For he hath taken us, and he will heal us: he will strike, and he will cure us.

2.text: He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on, that we may know the Lord. His going forth is prepared as the morning light, and he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth.

3.text: He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on, that we may know the Lord. His going forth is prepared as the morning light, and he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth.

4.text: What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim? what shall I do to thee, O Juda? your mercy is as a morning cloud, and as the dew that goeth away in the morning.

5.text: For this reason have I hewed them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments shall go forth as the light.

6.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts.

7.text: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant, there have they dealt treacherously against me.

8.text: Galaad is a city of workers of idols, supplanted with blood.

9.text: And like the jaws of highway robbers, they conspire with the priests who murder in the way those that pass out of Sichem: for they have wrought wickedness.

10.text: I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel: the fornications of Ephraim there: Israel is defiled.

11.text: And thou also, O Juda, set thee a harvest, when I shall bring back the captivity of my people.

1.text: When I would have healed Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria, for they have committed falsehood, and the thief is come in to steal, the robber is without.

2.text: And lest they may say in their hearts, that I remember all their wickedness: their own devices now have beset them about, they have been done before my face.

3.text: They have made the king glad with their wickedness: and the princes with their lies.

4.text: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker: the city rested a little from the mingling of the leaven, till the whole was leavened.

5.text: The day of our king, the princes began to be mad with wine: he stretched out his hand with scorners.

6.text: Because they have applied their heart like an oven, when he laid snares for them: he slept all the night baking them, in the morning he himself was heated as a flaming fire.

7.text: They were all heated like an oven, and have devoured their judges: all their kings have fallen: there is none amongst them that calleth unto me.

8.text: Ephraim himself is mixed among the nations: Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes, that is not turned.

9.text: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knew it not: yea, grey hairs also are spread about upon him, and he is ignorant of it.

10.text: And the pride of Israel shall be humbled before his face: and they have not returned to the Lord their God, nor have they sought him in all these.

11.text: And Ephraim is become as a dove that is decoyed, not having a heart: they called upon Egypt, they went to the Assyrians.

12.text: And when they shall go, I will spread my net upon them: I will bring them down as the fowl of the air, I will strike them as their congregation hath heard.

13.text: Woe to them, for they have departed from me: they shall be wasted because they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me.

14.text: And they have not cried to me with their heart, but they howled in their beds: they have thought upon wheat and wine, they are departed from me.

15.text: And I have chastised them, and strengthened their arms: and they have imagined evil against me.

16.text: They returned, that they might be without yoke: they became like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword, for the rage of their tongue. This is their derision in the land of Egypt.

1.text: Let there be a trumpet in thy throat like an eagle upon the house of the Lord: because they have transgressed my covenant, and have violated my law.

2.text: They shall call upon me: O my God, we, Israel, know thee.

3.text: Israel hath cast off the thing that is good, the enemy shall pursue him.

4.text: They have reigned, but not by me: they have been princes, and I knew not: of their silver, and their gold they have made idols to themselves, that they might perish.

5.text: Thy calf, O Samaria, is cast off, my wrath is kindled against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed?

6.text: For itself also is the invention of Israel: a workman made it, and it is no god: for the calf of Samaria shall be turned to spiders’ webs.

7.text: For they shall sow wind, and reap a whirlwind, there is no standing stalk in it, the bud shall yield no meal; and if it should yield, strangers shall eat it.

8.text: Israel is swallowed up: now is he become among the nations like an unclean vessel.

9.text: For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath given gifts to his lovers.

10.text: But even though they shall have hired the nations, now will I gather them together: and they shall rest a while from the burden of the king, and the princes.

11.text: Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin: altars are become to him unto sin.

12.text: I shall write to him my manifold laws, which have been accounted as foreign.

13.text: They shall offer victims, they shall sacrifice flesh, and shall eat it, and the Lord will not receive them: now will he remember their iniquity, and will visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt.

14.text: And Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and hath built temples: and Juda hath built many fenced cities: and I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the houses thereof.

1.text: Rejoice not, O Israel: rejoice not as the nations do: for thou hast committed fornication against thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor.

2.text: The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the wine shall deceive them.

3.text: They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land: Ephraim is returned to Egypt, and hath eaten unclean things among the Assyrians.

4.text: They shall not offer wine to the Lord, neither shall they please him: their sacrifices shall be like the bread of mourners: all that shall eat it shall be defiled: for their bread is life for their soul, it shall not enter into the house of the Lord.

5.text: What will you do in the solemn day, in the day of the feast of the Lord?

6.text: For behold they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them together, Memphis shall bury them: nettles shall inherit their beloved silver, the bur shall be in their tabernacles.

7.text: The days of visitation are come, the days of repaying are come: know ye, O Israel, that the prophet was foolish, the spiritual man was mad, for the multitude of thy iniquity, and the multitude of thy madness.

8.text: The watchman of Ephraim was with my God: the prophet is become a snare of ruin upon all his ways, madness is in the house of his God.

9.text: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa: he will remember their iniquity, and will visit their sin.

10.text: I found Israel like grapes in the desert, I saw their fathers like the firstfruits of the fig tree in the top thereof: but they went in to Beelphegor, and alienated themselves to that confusion, and became abominable, as those things were, which they loved.

11.text: As for Ephraim, their glory hath flown away like a bird from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.
